sec01-card-f09.front: What credential is legally required before operating a motor vehicle on Kansas public roads?
sec01-card-f09.expected_back: Driving a motor vehicle on Kansas public roads requires a driver license.

sec01-card-f10.front: Within how many days of moving into Kansas must a new resident obtain a Kansas driver license?
sec01-card-f10.expected_back: A new Kansas resident must obtain a Kansas driver license within ninety days of moving into the state.

sec01-card-f11.front: Which three personal details must every Kansas license applicant prove with documentation?
sec01-card-f11.expected_back: An applicant must provide proof of name, age and address.

sec01-card-f12.front: Whose approval is required when a Kansas license applicant is younger than eighteen?
sec01-card-f12.expected_back: Applicants below eighteen need parental or guardian consent.

sec01-card-f13.front: What must Kansas applicants do with any driver licenses or identification cards they previously held?
sec01-card-f13.expected_back: Applicants must surrender driver licenses or identification cards they previously held.

sec01-card-f14.front: How do suspended, revoked, denied, or cancelled driving privileges affect Kansas licensing eligibility?
sec01-card-f14.expected_back: An applicant with suspended, revoked, denied or cancelled driving privileges is disqualified under the handbook's eligibility list.

sec01-card-f15.front: What immigration or residency standing in the United States is required for Kansas licensing?
sec01-card-f15.expected_back: Kansas licensing requires lawful presence in the United States.

sec01-card-f16.front: What health requirement must Kansas applicants satisfy for the specific license type they request?
sec01-card-f16.expected_back: Applicants must meet the medical conditions for their requested license type.

sec01-card-f17.front: How do unpaid fines for moving traffic violations affect meeting Kansas licensing requirements?
sec01-card-f17.expected_back: Unpaid moving-violation fines prevent meeting the listed licensing requirements.

sec01-card-f18.front: Does the Kansas passenger-car handbook replace the separate commercial-vehicle manual for commercial licensing?
sec01-card-f18.expected_back: The passenger-car handbook does not replace the separate commercial-vehicle manual for commercial licensing.

sec01-card-f19.front: What must a Kansas motorcycle license applicant study alongside the standard driver handbook?
sec01-card-f19.expected_back: Motorcycle licensing requires study of the separate motorcycle manual in addition to this handbook.

sec01-card-f62.front: How does a court finding of mental incompetence affect the handbook's Kansas licensing eligibility list?
sec01-card-f62.expected_back: The handbook includes a court finding of mental incompetence among the conditions that prevent meeting its licensing eligibility list.

sec01-card-r68.front: A Kansas Class C license covers vehicles whose gross vehicle weight rating stays below what pound threshold?
sec01-card-r68.expected_back: A Class C license permits a vehicle whose gross vehicle weight rating is below twenty-six thousand one pounds.

sec01-card-f03.front: Are internet driver-education completion certificates accepted for Kansas driver licensing?
sec01-card-f03.expected_back: An internet driver-education completion certificate is not accepted for Kansas licensing.

sec01-card-f04.front: What accreditation and agency approval must a Kansas school-district driver-education program hold?
sec01-card-f04.expected_back: Kansas-approved school-district driver education must come from an accredited district with Department of Education approval.

sec01-card-f05.front: How many classroom hours does an approved private driver-education program in Kansas provide?
sec01-card-f05.expected_back: An approved private driver-education program provides eight classroom hours.

sec01-card-f06.front: How many hours of behind-the-wheel instruction are included in an approved Kansas private driver-education program?
sec01-card-f06.expected_back: An approved private driver-education program includes six hours of behind-the-wheel instruction.

sec01-card-f61.front: When must a Kansas applicant younger than eighteen complete approved driver education?
sec01-card-f61.memory_hook: Complete driver ed when path requires
sec01-card-f61.expected_back: An applicant below eighteen must complete approved driver education when that requirement applies to the applicant's Kansas licensing path.

sec01-card-f01.front: What is the minimum age to apply for a Kansas non-commercial Class C instructional permit?
sec01-card-f01.expected_back: A Kansas non-commercial Class C instructional permit requires the applicant to be at least fourteen.

sec01-card-f40.front: What parental document does an instructional-permit applicant younger than sixteen need?
sec01-card-f40.memory_hook: Under sixteen needs written parent application
sec01-card-f40.expected_back: An instructional-permit applicant younger than sixteen needs a parent's or guardian's written application.

sec01-card-f41.front: Where and when does a parent or guardian sign the Kansas instructional-permit affidavit?
sec01-card-f41.expected_back: A parent or guardian signs the instructional-permit affidavit at the licensing office when applying.

sec01-card-f42.front: Which exams or driver-education form qualify you for a Kansas Class C instructional permit?
sec01-card-f42.memory_hook: Pass vision and written or DE-ninety-nine
sec01-card-f42.expected_back: For a Class C instructional permit, pass the vision and written exams or bring the DE99 form authorizing the permit from the approved driver-education course you are attending.

sec01-card-f43.front: How long is a Kansas Class C instructional permit valid before expiring, and how can it be renewed?
sec01-card-f43.memory_hook: One year valid, retest to renew
sec01-card-f43.expected_back: A Class C instructional permit expires after one year and may be renewed with testing.

sec01-card-f44.front: Who must sit in the front seat whenever a Kansas instructional-permit holder drives?
sec01-card-f44.expected_back: An instructional-permit holder may drive only with a licensed adult seated in front.

sec01-card-f45.front: At least how old must the licensed adult supervising a Kansas instructional-permit driver be?
sec01-card-f45.expected_back: The adult supervising an instructional-permit driver must be at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f46.front: How much driving experience must the adult supervising an instructional-permit holder have?
sec01-card-f46.expected_back: The adult supervising an instructional-permit driver needs at least one year of driving experience.

sec01-card-f47.front: Who is allowed to sit in the front seat beside a Kansas instructional-permit driver?
sec01-card-f47.memory_hook: Only your supervisor sits up front
sec01-card-f47.expected_back: The supervising adult is the only person permitted in the front seat beside an instructional-permit driver.

sec01-card-f48.front: For what two reasons may a Kansas instructional-permit driver use a wireless device while driving?
sec01-card-f48.memory_hook: Report crime or get emergency help
sec01-card-f48.expected_back: An instructional-permit driver may use a wireless device only for reporting illegal activity or obtaining emergency assistance.

sec01-card-f20.front: What age range qualifies an applicant to seek a Kansas farm permit?
sec01-card-f20.expected_back: A farm-permit applicant must be at least fourteen and younger than seventeen.

sec01-card-f21.front: What living or work tie to a farm must a Kansas farm-permit applicant have?
sec01-card-f21.memory_hook: Live there or earn farm pay
sec01-card-f21.expected_back: A farm-permit applicant must live on a farm or have paid employment on one.

sec01-card-f22.front: At least how many agricultural acres define a farm under the Kansas farm-permit rule?
sec01-card-f22.expected_back: For the farm-permit rule, a farm has at least twenty acres devoted to agricultural use.

sec01-card-f23.front: What must a farm employer sign when an applicant qualifies through paid farm employment?
sec01-card-f23.expected_back: A farm employer must sign an affidavit confirming the applicant's farm employment.

sec01-card-f24.front: Whose signatures are required on the affidavit in the Kansas farm-permit application process?
sec01-card-f24.memory_hook: Parent or guardian plus employer sign
sec01-card-f24.expected_back: The farm-permit process requires an affidavit signed by a parent or guardian and the employer.

sec01-card-f25.front: What exams or completion slip must a Kansas farm-permit applicant pass or present?
sec01-card-f25.expected_back: A farm-permit applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the DE-ninety-nine driver-education completion slip.

sec01-card-f26.front: For what work purposes may a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old Kansas farm-permit holder drive?
sec01-card-f26.expected_back: A farm-permit driver aged fourteen or fifteen may drive for farm work, employment or other farm-related work.

sec01-card-f27.front: How may a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old Kansas farm-permit holder drive to school, and what is excluded?
sec01-card-f27.expected_back: A farm-permit driver aged fourteen or fifteen may use the most direct home-school route to attend school, excluding school activities.

sec01-card-f28.front: Which minor passengers are barred from riding with a fourteen- or fifteen-year-old farm-permit driver?
sec01-card-f28.expected_back: Farm-permit drivers aged fourteen or fifteen may not carry minor passengers who are not siblings.

sec01-card-f29.front: When may a Kansas farm-permit holder legally use a wireless device behind the wheel?
sec01-card-f29.expected_back: A farm-permit driver may use a wireless device only to report unlawful activity or request emergency help.

sec01-card-f30.front: How many practice hours must a parent or guardian confirm by affidavit for lesser farm-permit restrictions at sixteen or seventeen?
sec01-card-f30.expected_back: Before receiving the lesser farm-permit restrictions for ages sixteen and seventeen, an applicant needs a parental or guardian affidavit confirming at least fifty practice hours.

sec01-card-f31.front: At least how many nighttime hours must be included in the farm-permit practice affidavit for lesser restrictions?
sec01-card-f31.memory_hook: Include at least ten night hours
sec01-card-f31.expected_back: The farm-permit practice affidavit for lesser restrictions must include at least ten nighttime hours.

sec01-card-f32.front: Between what daily hours may a Kansas farm-permit holder under lesser restrictions generally drive?
sec01-card-f32.memory_hook: Five in morning to nine night
sec01-card-f32.expected_back: Farm-permit holders under the lesser restrictions may drive between five a.m. and nine p.m.

sec01-card-f33.front: What school-related travel is permitted for a Kansas driver under lesser-restricted farm-permit rules?
sec01-card-f33.expected_back: A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.

sec01-card-f34.front: What faith-based travel is allowed for a lesser-restricted Kansas farm-permit driver?
sec01-card-f34.expected_back: A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may travel to or from an activity held by a religious organization.

sec01-card-f35.front: What job and agricultural trips remain authorized under lesser-restricted Kansas farm-permit rules?
sec01-card-f35.expected_back: Lesser-restricted farm-permit driving is permitted for work, employment and farm-related duties.

sec01-card-f36.front: Who can sit in the front passenger seat to allow a lesser-restricted farm-permit holder to drive anytime?
sec01-card-f36.expected_back: A lesser-restricted farm-permit driver may drive while a licensed adult occupies the front passenger seat.

sec01-card-f37.front: How many minor passengers outside the immediate family may ride with a lesser-restricted farm-permit driver?
sec01-card-f37.expected_back: The lesser-restricted farm-permit path allows only one minor passenger from outside the driver's immediate family.

sec01-card-f38.front: How long must a Kansas farm-permit applicant younger than seventeen hold a state learner permit before license issuance?
sec01-card-f38.expected_back: A farm-permit applicant below seventeen must have held a state learner permit for at least one year before license issuance.

sec01-card-f39.front: At age sixteen, holding a lesser-restricted license or farm permit for how long removes the listed age restrictions?
sec01-card-f39.memory_hook: Six months at sixteen clears limits
sec01-card-f39.expected_back: At age sixteen, holding a lesser-restricted license or farm permit for six months removes the listed age restrictions.

sec01-card-f59.front: At least how old must the accompanying adult be during age-sixteen practice for a less-restricted farm permit?
sec01-card-f59.expected_back: For less-restricted farm-permit practice at age sixteen, the accompanying adult must be at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f49.front: What is the minimum age to apply for a Kansas restricted driver license?
sec01-card-f49.expected_back: A restricted-license applicant must be at least fifteen.

sec01-card-f50.front: How long must a restricted-license applicant hold a state learner permit, and what permit time is excluded?
sec01-card-f50.memory_hook: One year permit, exclude course slip
sec01-card-f50.expected_back: A restricted-license applicant must have held a state learner permit for at least one year, excluding time on a driver-education permit slip.

sec01-card-f51.front: How many supervised practice hours does a fifteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license applicant need?
sec01-card-f51.expected_back: A restricted-license applicant aged fifteen needs twenty-five supervised practice hours.

sec01-card-f52.front: How does the approved driver-education requirement differ between fifteen-year-old and sixteen-year-old restricted-license applicants?
sec01-card-f52.expected_back: Restricted-license applicants aged fifteen must complete approved driver education, while applicants aged sixteen do not have that requirement.

sec01-card-f53.front: How many supervised practice hours must a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license applicant complete?
sec01-card-f53.expected_back: Restricted-license applicants aged sixteen need fifty supervised practice hours.

sec01-card-f54.front: Out of the supervised practice required for sixteen-year-old restricted-license applicants, how many hours must be at night?
sec01-card-f54.expected_back: Of the practice required for restricted-license applicants aged sixteen, ten hours must be at night.

sec01-card-f55.front: How do a restricted-license applicant's parent or guardian verify completed supervised practice?
sec01-card-f55.expected_back: A parent or guardian must attest by affidavit to the restricted-license applicant's supervised practice.

sec01-card-f56.front: What additional practice affidavit must a fifteen-year-old restricted driver with twenty-five hours submit before moving to age-sixteen restrictions?
sec01-card-f56.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged fifteen with only twenty-five supervised hours must submit another affidavit for twenty-five additional hours, including ten at night, before moving to the restrictions for ages sixteen and seventeen.

sec01-card-f57.front: How old must the accompanying adult be during supervised Class C practice for a fifteen-year-old restricted applicant?
sec01-card-f57.expected_back: For the restricted Class C practice requirement at age fifteen, the accompanying adult must be at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f58.front: How old must the accompanying adult be for the less-restricted Class C practice requirement at age sixteen?
sec01-card-f58.expected_back: For the less-restricted Class C practice requirement at age sixteen, the accompanying adult must be at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f60.front: Which exams or completion document qualify a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license applicant?
sec01-card-f60.expected_back: A restricted-license applicant aged sixteen must pass the vision, written and driving exams or present the DE-ninety-nine driver-education completion slip.

sec01-card-r01.front: What work-related driving is allowed for a fifteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license holder?
sec01-card-r01.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged fifteen may travel for a job, employment or farm work.

sec01-card-r02.front: When and how may a fifteen-year-old restricted-license driver commute to school, and what stays off-limits?
sec01-card-r02.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged fifteen may take the direct home-school route on school days for attendance, excluding school activities.

sec01-card-r03.front: How may a fifteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license holder travel for religious events?
sec01-card-r03.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged fifteen may travel directly to or from an activity held by a religious organization.

sec01-card-r04.front: When may a fifteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license holder drive outside solo trip categories?
sec01-card-r04.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged fifteen may drive when a licensed adult sits in front.

sec01-card-r05.front: Which minor passengers may a fifteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license driver never carry?
sec01-card-r05.expected_back: Restricted-license drivers aged fifteen may not carry minors who are not siblings.

sec01-card-r06.front: Under what two exceptions may a Kansas restricted-license holder use a wireless device while driving?
sec01-card-r06.expected_back: A restricted-license driver may use a wireless device only for reporting unlawful activity or summoning emergency help.

sec01-card-r07.front: During what daily hours may a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license driver drive for general purposes?
sec01-card-r07.memory_hook: Five in morning to nine night
sec01-card-r07.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may drive between five a.m. and nine p.m.

sec01-card-r08.front: What school-related destinations are open to a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license driver?
sec01-card-r08.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may travel to or from school and authorized school activities.

sec01-card-r09.front: How may a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license holder travel for a religious organization's activity?
sec01-card-r09.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may travel directly to or from a religious organization's activity.

sec01-card-r10.front: What employment and agricultural trips are permitted for a sixteen-year-old restricted-license driver?
sec01-card-r10.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may drive for work, employment or farm duties.

sec01-card-r11.front: Who can accompany a sixteen-year-old restricted-license holder in front to allow driving outside solo limits?
sec01-card-r11.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may drive while accompanied by a licensed adult in front.

sec01-card-r12.front: How many non-sibling minor passengers may ride with a sixteen-year-old Kansas restricted-license driver?
sec01-card-r12.expected_back: A restricted-license driver aged sixteen may carry only one minor passenger who is not a sibling.

sec01-card-r13.front: When is a sixteen-year-old Kansas driver released from all age-related driving restrictions in the handbook?
sec01-card-r13.memory_hook: Age sixteen plus six months held
sec01-card-r13.expected_back: After reaching age sixteen and holding a restricted license for six months, the driver is released from all age-related driving restrictions described in the handbook.

sec01-card-f07.front: What does the department recommend doing before visiting a Kansas driver-licensing office?
sec01-card-f07.expected_back: The department recommends arranging an appointment before visiting a licensing office.

sec01-card-f08.front: How can eligible Kansas applicants avoid taking the non-commercial knowledge exam at the licensing office?
sec01-card-f08.expected_back: Eligible Kansas applicants may complete the non-commercial knowledge exam online and bring the passing result to avoid the office knowledge exam.

sec01-card-r17.front: Instead of station vision screening, what eye-exam document may a Kansas license applicant present?
sec01-card-r17.expected_back: A license applicant may take station vision screening or present the Driver Licensing eye-examination form completed within the previous ninety days by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.

sec01-card-r18.front: What minimum visual acuity is required to pass Kansas station vision screening?
sec01-card-r18.expected_back: Station vision screening requires at least twenty over forty vision in one eye.

sec01-card-r19.front: What happens when a Kansas driver needs corrective lenses to pass the vision standard?
sec01-card-r19.expected_back: Drivers who need corrective lenses to meet the vision standard receive a restriction requiring those lenses whenever driving.

sec01-card-r20.front: Who must complete the licensing eye form when an applicant fails Kansas station vision screening?
sec01-card-r20.expected_back: An applicant who fails vision screening must have the licensing eye form completed by a licensed ophthalmologist or optometrist.

sec01-card-r21.front: Within how many days of the eye exam must the completed form return so staff can decide next steps?
sec01-card-r21.expected_back: Returning the eye form within ninety days of examination lets licensing staff decide whether to issue a license or require further testing.

sec01-card-r22.front: What two core subject areas does the Kansas written knowledge exam test?
sec01-card-r22.expected_back: The Kansas knowledge exam covers traffic law and sign recognition by shape, color or symbol.

sec01-card-r23.front: Where does the Kansas driving exam take place, and what does it evaluate?
sec01-card-r23.expected_back: The driving exam uses a designated traffic route to demonstrate basic vehicle-operation skills.

sec01-card-r24.front: How does Kansas graduated driver licensing build skill for beginner drivers?
sec01-card-r24.expected_back: Graduated licensing introduces beginner drivers to more complex situations in stages after initial lower-risk experience.

sec01-card-r25.front: How soon may you retest after a first, second, or third written or driving exam failure, and what is required?
sec01-card-r25.expected_back: After the first, second or third failure of the written or driving exam, next-working-day retesting is available after payment of the re-exam fee.

sec01-card-r26.front: What re-examination fee does the Kansas handbook list?
sec01-card-r26.expected_back: The handbook lists a re-examination fee of one dollar and fifty cents.

sec01-card-r27.front: How many opportunities do Kansas applicants receive to pass the written knowledge exam?
sec01-card-r27.expected_back: Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the written exam.

sec01-card-r28.front: How many opportunities do Kansas applicants receive to pass the behind-the-wheel driving exam?
sec01-card-r28.expected_back: Applicants receive four opportunities to pass the driving exam.

sec01-card-r29.front: How long must an applicant hold off before retesting after failing either Kansas exam a fourth time?
sec01-card-r29.expected_back: A fourth failure of either exam requires waiting at least six months from the latest failure before retesting.

sec01-card-r30.front: What two broad requirements must be satisfied before an applicant actually receives a Kansas driver license?
sec01-card-r30.expected_back: An applicant receives a license only after passing the required exams and meeting the other licensing conditions.

sec01-card-r31.front: Which exam must be passed again when renewing an expired Kansas instructional permit?
sec01-card-r31.expected_back: Renewing an instructional permit requires passing the written exam again.

sec01-card-f02.front: What minimum age does Kansas list for an unrestricted non-commercial Class C driver license?
sec01-card-f02.expected_back: Kansas lists seventeen as the minimum age for an unrestricted non-commercial Class C license.

sec01-card-r14.front: What practice affidavit is required from applicants younger than eighteen applying for an unrestricted Kansas license?
sec01-card-r14.expected_back: Applicants younger than eighteen seeking an unrestricted license need a parent or guardian affidavit confirming at least fifty practice hours.

sec01-card-r15.front: At least how many nighttime hours must appear on the unrestricted-license practice affidavit for applicants below eighteen?
sec01-card-r15.expected_back: The unrestricted-license practice affidavit for applicants below eighteen must include at least ten nighttime hours.

sec01-card-r16.front: What exams or driver-education slip must an unrestricted Kansas license applicant pass or present?
sec01-card-r16.expected_back: An unrestricted-license applicant must pass vision, written and driving exams or present the gold DE-ninety-nine driver-education completion slip.

sec01-card-r32.front: When does a temporary resident's Kansas license, permit, or identification card expire?
sec01-card-r32.expected_back: A temporary resident's license, permit or identification card expires when lawful-presence authorization expires.

sec01-card-r33.front: How far ahead of license expiration does the Division send a renewal notice?
sec01-card-r33.expected_back: The Division sends a license-expiration or renewal notice at least thirty days before expiration.

sec01-card-r34.front: Which contact addresses does the Division use to deliver Kansas license renewal notices?
sec01-card-r34.expected_back: Renewal notices use the mailing address on record or the email address selected for electronic notices.

sec01-card-r35.front: How recent must an ophthalmologist or optometrist eye exam be to replace station vision screening at renewal?
sec01-card-r35.expected_back: For renewal, a licensed ophthalmologist's or optometrist's eye examination may replace station screening if completed no more than ninety days before the renewal application.

sec01-card-r36.front: When may a Kansas licensing examiner require a renewal applicant to take a written or driving test?
sec01-card-r36.expected_back: A licensing examiner may require a renewal applicant to take a written or driving test when ordinary vehicle control is in doubt.

sec01-card-r37.front: What additional expired-license penalty amount does the Kansas handbook list?
sec01-card-r37.expected_back: The handbook lists an additional expired-license penalty of one dollar.

sec01-card-r38.front: What testing is required if a Kansas driver license stays expired for more than one year?
sec01-card-r38.expected_back: A license expired for more than one year requires vision, written and driving testing.

sec01-card-r39.front: Must most Kansas drivers renew in their home county, or may they use any state driver-license office?
sec01-card-r39.expected_back: A Kansas license may generally be renewed at any state driver-license office regardless of the holder's Kansas residence.

sec01-card-r40.front: Where must registered offenders go to renew a Kansas driver license?
sec01-card-r40.expected_back: Registered offenders must use a full-service station for renewal.

sec01-card-r41.front: When may a separate-card concealed-carry holder renew at any Kansas driver-license station?
sec01-card-r41.memory_hook: When name, address, number stay unchanged
sec01-card-r41.expected_back: A separate-card concealed-carry license holder may renew at any station if no name, address or license-number changes are needed.

sec01-card-r66.front: What can happen based on medical details reported on a renewal eye-examination form?
sec01-card-r66.expected_back: Information on a renewal eye-examination form may lead to additional testing.

sec01-card-r69.front: On what recurring personal date does a standard Kansas driver license expire?
sec01-card-r69.expected_back: The handbook says a driver's license expires on the holder's birthday.

sec01-card-r42.front: How many moving-violation convictions within twelve months can suspend a Kansas driver license?
sec01-card-r42.expected_back: Three moving-violation convictions within twelve months can cause a license suspension.

sec01-card-r43.front: How long is your Kansas license suspended for a first refusal to take a required chemical test?
sec01-card-r43.expected_back: For a first chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a one-year suspension.

sec01-card-r44.front: What license penalty applies for failing to appear on a required traffic court date in Kansas?
sec01-card-r44.expected_back: Failure to appear for a required court date carries an indefinite suspension under the handbook.

sec01-card-r45.front: What suspension penalty results from failing to maintain continuous vehicle liability insurance in Kansas?
sec01-card-r45.expected_back: Failure to keep continuous vehicle liability insurance carries an indefinite suspension.

sec01-card-r46.front: What alcohol-test level or driving condition can suspend a Kansas license?
sec01-card-r46.memory_hook: Impaired driving or point zero eight
sec01-card-r46.expected_back: Impaired driving or an alcohol-test result of point zero eight or higher can cause suspension.

sec01-card-r47.front: How can transporting an open alcoholic-beverage container in a vehicle affect your Kansas license?
sec01-card-r47.expected_back: Transporting an open alcoholic-beverage container can cause suspension.

sec01-card-r48.front: What licensing action can follow failing to report a traffic crash when required?
sec01-card-r48.expected_back: Failure to report a traffic crash can cause suspension.

sec01-card-r49.front: What happens to driving privileges after a Kansas vehicular-homicide conviction?
sec01-card-r49.expected_back: A vehicular-homicide conviction can result in revoked driving privileges.

sec01-card-r50.front: What license action follows a conviction for leaving an injury or fatal crash without stopping and helping?
sec01-card-r50.expected_back: A conviction for leaving a crash involving injury or death without stopping and helping can cause revocation.

sec01-card-r51.front: Can a Kansas reckless-driving conviction lead to license revocation?
sec01-card-r51.expected_back: A reckless-driving conviction can cause revocation.

sec01-card-r52.front: What happens to driving privileges after a conviction for any felony committed using a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-r52.expected_back: A conviction for a felony committed using a motor vehicle can result in license revocation.

sec01-card-r53.front: What license penalty can follow a conviction for trying to evade a police officer?
sec01-card-r53.expected_back: A conviction for trying to evade a police officer can cause revocation.

sec01-card-r54.front: What licensing consequence can follow an aggravated-vehicular-homicide conviction in Kansas?
sec01-card-r54.expected_back: An aggravated-vehicular-homicide conviction can result in license revocation.

sec01-card-r55.front: What licensing consequence can follow a Kansas vehicular-battery conviction?
sec01-card-r55.expected_back: A vehicular-battery conviction can result in license revocation.

sec01-card-r62.front: How long does the Kansas handbook suspend a license for a second chemical-test refusal?
sec01-card-r62.expected_back: For a second chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a two-year suspension.

sec01-card-r63.front: How long does the Kansas handbook suspend a license for a third chemical-test refusal?
sec01-card-r63.expected_back: For a third chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a three-year suspension.

sec01-card-r64.front: How long does the Kansas handbook suspend a license for a fourth chemical-test refusal?
sec01-card-r64.expected_back: For a fourth chemical-test refusal, the handbook requires a ten-year suspension.

sec01-card-r65.front: What happens if you fail to respond to a traffic citation issued in Kansas or another state?
sec01-card-r65.expected_back: Failure to respond to a traffic citation from Kansas or another state can cause license suspension.

sec01-card-r57.front: From what age may an out-of-state student classified as nonresident for tuition drive in Kansas on a valid home license?
sec01-card-r57.expected_back: A student who lives outside Kansas and is classified as nonresident for tuition purposes may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age sixteen.

sec01-card-r58.front: From what age may active-duty military members and qualifying spouses or children drive in Kansas on a valid license?
sec01-card-r58.expected_back: Active-duty military members and qualifying spouses and children may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age sixteen.

sec01-card-r59.front: When may a nonresident employee aged sixteen or older drive in Kansas on a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-r59.expected_back: An employee aged sixteen or older of a company licensed to do business in Kansas may use a valid license while temporarily employed in Kansas to receive or provide job instruction.

sec01-card-r60.front: Under what conditions may foreign tourists, teachers, and business visitors drive in Kansas on a valid license?
sec01-card-r60.memory_hook: Up to one year, age sixteen
sec01-card-r60.expected_back: Foreign tourists, teachers and business visitors staying up to one year may use a valid license from age sixteen with valid immigration documents.

sec01-card-r61.front: From what age may a nonresident visitor holding a valid out-of-state license drive in Kansas?
sec01-card-r61.expected_back: A nonresident visitor with a valid state license may drive in Kansas from age sixteen.

sec01-card-r67.front: From what age may foreign military personnel serving temporarily with the Armed Forces and their families drive on a valid license in Kansas?
sec01-card-r67.expected_back: Foreign military personnel temporarily serving with the Armed Forces, and their spouses or children, may drive on a valid license in Kansas from age sixteen.

sec02-card-f23.front: What must you verify before slowing down, turning, or changing lanes in Kansas?
sec02-card-f23.expected_back: Before slowing, turning or changing lanes, check that the movement can be made safely.

sec02-card-f24.front: Which three groups of road users are your signals meant to alert before an intended movement?
sec02-card-f24.expected_back: Use a signal to tell drivers, cyclists and pedestrians your intended movement.

sec02-card-f25.front: At least how many feet before a movement or turn must you activate your required signal in Kansas?
sec02-card-f25.expected_back: Give the required signal at least one hundred feet before the movement or turn.

sec02-card-f26.front: How long should you keep a turn signal operating as you approach a turn?
sec02-card-f26.expected_back: Keep a turn signal operating until you are ready to turn.

sec02-card-f27.front: When a vehicle is legally required to have electric turn signals, how must turns be indicated?
sec02-card-f27.expected_back: A vehicle required to have electric turn signals must use them to indicate a turn.

sec02-card-r11.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt at a stop sign that has a marked stop line?
sec02-card-r11.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop at the marked stop line when one is present.

sec02-card-r12.front: Where must you stop at a stop sign with no painted stop line, both with and without a crosswalk?
sec02-card-r12.expected_back: At a stop sign with no stop line, stop before the near-side crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop nearest the intersecting roadway.

sec02-card-r13.front: What is required when exiting an alley, private driveway, or building in a residential or business area?
sec02-card-r13.expected_back: Stop when leaving an alley, private drive or building in a residential or business area.

sec02-card-r14.front: What must you do when a school crossing guard holds the stop flag in the stop position?
sec02-card-r14.expected_back: Stop when a school crossing guard holds the official flag in the stop position.

sec02-card-r15.front: What action is required when a railroad-crossing flagger or control device directs traffic to halt?
sec02-card-r15.expected_back: Stop when directed by a railroad-crossing flagger or control device.

sec02-card-r16.front: What must a driver do when a construction flagger directs traffic to stop?
sec02-card-r16.expected_back: Stop when a construction flagger directs you to do so.

sec02-card-r17.front: What is your legal duty whenever a police officer directs your vehicle to stop?
sec02-card-r17.expected_back: Stop whenever a police officer directs you to stop.

sec02-card-r19.front: What stop requirement applies at an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic light?
sec02-card-r19.expected_back: A flashing red traffic light requires a complete stop.

sec02-card-f01.front: What general driving speed does Kansas law require at all times?
sec02-card-f01.expected_back: Kansas requires a driving speed that is reasonable for the conditions present.

sec02-card-f02.front: Which four factors does the Kansas handbook tell you to weigh when choosing your speed?
sec02-card-f02.expected_back: Choose speed after considering road conditions, weather, the vehicle and your physical condition.

sec02-card-f03.front: Do Kansas normal-condition maximum speed limits excuse you from slowing down for special hazards?
sec02-card-f03.expected_back: The listed normal-condition maximums do not remove the need to reduce speed for special hazards.

sec02-card-f04.front: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit in a Kansas urban district?
sec02-card-f04.expected_back: Unless a different limit is posted, an urban district has a maximum speed of thirty miles per hour.

sec02-card-f05.front: Outside towns, what is the default maximum speed on a separated multilane highway designated by the Secretary of Transportation?
sec02-card-f05.expected_back: Outside towns, the maximum is seventy-five miles per hour on a separated multilane highway designated and posted by the Secretary of Transportation, unless a different limit is posted.

sec02-card-f06.front: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed outside towns on a Kansas state or federal highway?
sec02-card-f06.expected_back: Outside towns, a state or federal highway has a maximum speed of sixty-five miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

sec02-card-f07.front: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed outside towns on a Kansas county or township road?
sec02-card-f07.expected_back: Outside towns, a county or township road has a maximum speed of fifty-five miles per hour unless a different limit is posted.

sec02-card-f08.front: What maximum speed applies in a properly marked Kansas school zone unless posted otherwise?
sec02-card-f08.expected_back: A properly marked school zone has a twenty-mile-per-hour maximum unless posted otherwise.

sec02-card-f09.front: What is the default maximum speed in a properly marked Kansas business district unless posted otherwise?
sec02-card-f09.expected_back: A properly marked business district has a twenty-mile-per-hour maximum unless posted otherwise.

sec02-card-f10.front: What speed limit does a Kansas school bus follow, and who can set a stricter rule?
sec02-card-f10.expected_back: A school bus follows the posted speed limit unless school-district policy determines otherwise.

sec02-card-f11.front: When is driving slower than a posted minimum speed limit unlawful in Kansas?
sec02-card-f11.expected_back: Driving below a posted minimum is unlawful under normal road, weather and traffic conditions.

sec02-card-f12.front: Can driving unnecessarily slowly be unlawful in Kansas even where no minimum speed sign is posted?
sec02-card-f12.expected_back: Unnecessarily slow driving that blocks normal traffic is unlawful even without a posted minimum.

sec02-card-f13.front: When does driving slower than normal or minimum speeds remain legal in Kansas?
sec02-card-f13.expected_back: A slower speed remains permissible when safe operation under the basic speed rule requires it.

sec02-card-f14.front: What restraint rule does Kansas enforce for passenger-vehicle occupants?
sec02-card-f14.expected_back: Kansas requires passenger-vehicle occupants to use safety restraints.

sec02-card-f15.front: May a Kansas officer pull over a vehicle solely for spotting an unbelted adult in a front seat?
sec02-card-f15.expected_back: An officer may stop a vehicle solely for seeing an unbelted adult in a front seat.

sec02-card-f16.front: In which seating positions can an unrestrained child give a Kansas officer sole cause to stop a vehicle?
sec02-card-f16.expected_back: An officer may stop a vehicle solely for seeing an unrestrained child in any seating position.

sec02-card-f17.front: Who bears legal responsibility for ensuring every child in a passenger car uses an appropriate restraint?
sec02-card-f17.expected_back: The passenger-car driver must ensure that every child in the car is properly protected by an appropriate restraint.

sec02-card-f18.front: How many passengers define a passenger car under the Kansas child and occupant restraint rule?
sec02-card-f18.expected_back: The cited restraint rule defines a passenger car as a vehicle built for fewer than ten passengers.

sec02-card-f19.front: What restraint is mandatory in Kansas for children younger than age four?
sec02-card-f19.expected_back: Children younger than four must ride in a federally approved child safety seat.

sec02-card-f20.front: From what age does the Kansas handbook state that children require a seat belt?
sec02-card-f20.expected_back: The handbook requires a seat belt for children aged eight or older.

sec02-card-f21.front: Which seating position does the Kansas handbook identify as the safest spot for a child safety seat?
sec02-card-f21.expected_back: The handbook identifies the center position in the rear seat as the safest safety-seat location.

sec02-card-f22.front: What guide must you follow when installing and strapping a child safety seat?
sec02-card-f22.expected_back: Install and use a child safety seat according to its manufacturer's instructions.

sec02-card-f28.front: Which lane should you enter early before turning right from a divided four-lane highway?
sec02-card-f28.expected_back: Before turning right from a divided four-lane highway, move into the right lane early.

sec02-card-f29.front: Into which cross-street lane should you steer when turning right from a four-lane divided highway?
sec02-card-f29.expected_back: When turning right from a four-lane divided highway, make a tight turn into the cross street's right lane.

sec02-card-f30.front: From which lane do you begin a left turn on a multilane road?
sec02-card-f30.expected_back: For a left turn on a multilane road, begin in the inside lane near the center line or divider.

sec02-card-f31.front: Where on the cross street should your vehicle enter when completing a left turn from a multilane road?
sec02-card-f31.expected_back: When turning left from a multilane road, enter just right of the cross street's center line without swinging wide.

sec02-card-f32.front: What roadway controls can authorize turning from more than one lane at an intersection?
sec02-card-f32.expected_back: Signs or pavement arrows may authorize turns from multiple lanes.

sec02-card-f33.front: At which two terrain features does Kansas forbid making a U-turn?
sec02-card-f33.expected_back: Do not make a U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop.

sec02-card-f34.front: From at least how many feet away must other drivers be able to see your vehicle to make a legal U-turn?
sec02-card-f34.expected_back: A U-turn is prohibited where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from at least five hundred feet away.

sec02-card-f35.front: Even with clear sightlines, what local rules and controls govern whether a U-turn is legal?
sec02-card-f35.expected_back: Follow local ordinances and regulatory signs controlling U-turns.

sec02-card-r34.front: To whom must a driver turning left at an intersection yield?
sec02-card-r34.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic.

sec02-card-r35.front: Who has priority when a left-turning vehicle and an opposing straight-moving vehicle enter an intersection together?
sec02-card-r35.expected_back: When a left-turning vehicle and a straight-moving vehicle enter together, the straight-moving vehicle has priority.

sec02-card-f36.front: What two conditions are required to pass on the left along a two-lane, two-way Kansas road?
sec02-card-f36.expected_back: On a two-way road with two lanes, a left-side pass requires a safe gap and compliance with the speed limit.

sec02-card-f37.front: What must you check ahead and behind before pulling out to pass another vehicle?
sec02-card-f37.expected_back: Before passing, check ahead for room and behind for another driver beginning to pass.

sec02-card-f38.front: Which turn signal must you activate before moving out to pass on the left?
sec02-card-f38.expected_back: Use the left-turn signal before beginning a pass on the left.

sec02-card-f39.front: What signal is required after overtaking a vehicle before moving back into your normal lane?
sec02-card-f39.expected_back: After passing, signal right before returning to your normal lane.

sec02-card-f40.front: What visual cue in your inside rearview mirror tells you it is safe to return right after passing?
sec02-card-f40.expected_back: Return right after a pass only when the entire front of the passed vehicle appears in your inside mirror.

sec02-card-f41.front: How must you drive when another vehicle is passing you?
sec02-card-f41.expected_back: When another vehicle passes you, stay in your lane without accelerating.

sec02-card-f47.front: What is the rule where a roadside sign prohibits passing?
sec02-card-f47.expected_back: Do not pass where a sign forbids it.

sec02-card-f50.front: Where is the pennant-shaped warning sign placed, and what zone does it mark?
sec02-card-f50.expected_back: The pennant-shaped warning sign marks the start of a no-passing area from the left roadside.

sec02-card-f51.front: What passing rule do double solid yellow center lines set for traffic in both directions?
sec02-card-f51.expected_back: Double solid yellow center lines prohibit traffic from either direction from crossing them.

sec02-card-f52.front: Before an oncoming vehicle closes within how many feet must you finish passing and return to your lane?
sec02-card-f52.expected_back: Finish a pass and return to your lane before an oncoming vehicle is within two hundred feet.

sec02-card-f53.front: Which warning message is the only pennant-shaped warning sign in the Kansas handbook?
sec02-card-f53.expected_back: The handbook identifies the no-passing warning sign as the only pennant-shaped warning sign.

sec02-card-r01.front: On a one-way street, how many same-direction lanes are required before passing on the right is permitted?
sec02-card-r01.expected_back: Passing on the right is permitted on a one-way road marked with at least two lanes traveling in the same direction.

sec02-card-r02.front: When, if ever, may you drive onto the road shoulder to pass another vehicle?
sec02-card-r02.expected_back: Do not use the shoulder to pass except for an emergency or instructions from traffic authorities.

sec02-card-r03.front: What checks and signal are required before executing a legal pass on the right?
sec02-card-r03.expected_back: Check ahead and behind and signal before passing on the right.

sec02-card-r04.front: Which three conditions determine a reasonable following distance in Kansas?
sec02-card-r04.memory_hook: Match gap to weather, road, traffic
sec02-card-r04.expected_back: Following distance must be reasonable for weather, roadway and traffic conditions.

sec02-card-r05.front: How much space must you keep behind the vehicle ahead in case it stops abruptly?
sec02-card-r05.expected_back: Leave enough following space to stop or turn if the vehicle ahead stops abruptly.

sec02-card-r06.front: What minimum following time interval does the Kansas handbook use under ideal driving conditions?
sec02-card-r06.expected_back: The handbook uses a two-second following interval for ideal conditions.

sec02-card-r07.front: What following time interval does the Kansas handbook specify when conditions turn adverse?
sec02-card-r07.expected_back: The handbook uses a four-second following interval when conditions are adverse.

sec02-card-r08.front: How should you adjust your following gap behind vehicles likely to stop often or turn abruptly?
sec02-card-r08.expected_back: Increase the following gap behind vehicles likely to stop frequently or turn abruptly.

sec02-card-r09.front: How should poor weather change your normal following gap?
sec02-card-r09.expected_back: Poor weather calls for an even greater following gap.

sec02-card-r10.front: Besides cutting braking room, what does following too closely do to your forward visibility?
sec02-card-r10.expected_back: Following too closely limits the view of traffic and road conditions ahead.

sec02-card-r18.front: How must you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red lights or a siren?
sec02-card-r18.expected_back: For an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing red lights or a siren, pull right and stop clear of intersections.

sec02-card-r20.front: For which three types of buses stopped to load or unload children must traffic in both directions stop on undivided roads?
sec02-card-r20.expected_back: Unless on the opposing roadway of a divided highway, a driver meeting or overtaking a school, church or day-care bus stopped to load or unload children must stop.

sec02-card-r21.front: After stopping for a bus loading or unloading children, what two cues must happen before you move again?
sec02-card-r21.expected_back: After stopping for a school, church or day-care bus loading or unloading children, remain stopped until its stop signal retracts and red lights turn off.

sec02-card-r22.front: When does oncoming traffic NOT have to stop for a school bus loading or unloading children?
sec02-card-r22.expected_back: Traffic on the opposing roadway of a divided highway need not stop for a school bus loading or unloading children.

sec02-card-r27.front: Which visual or audible warnings give an emergency vehicle legal right-of-way priority in Kansas?
sec02-card-r27.expected_back: An emergency vehicle using a forward red light or a siren or bell has priority.

sec02-card-r28.front: How long must you stay stopped at the right edge for a responding emergency vehicle?
sec02-card-r28.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle using a forward red light, siren or bell, pull right and remain stopped until it has passed.

sec02-card-r29.front: What rule applies to following behind an emergency vehicle responding with active warning signals?
sec02-card-r29.expected_back: Do not follow an emergency vehicle responding with warning signals.

sec02-card-r30.front: On a road with at least two lanes each way, what must you do when approaching a stopped emergency vehicle flashing lights?
sec02-card-r30.expected_back: When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights from behind on a road with at least two lanes in each direction, cautiously move out of its adjacent lane if a lane change is possible.

sec02-card-r31.front: What must you do past a stopped flashing emergency vehicle on a four-lane road if traffic makes changing lanes impossible?
sec02-card-r31.expected_back: If a lane change is impossible when approaching from behind a stopped emergency vehicle using flashing warning lights on a road with at least two lanes each way, slow down and proceed cautiously.

sec02-card-r32.front: Who has priority when construction workers and work vehicles are actively operating on the roadway?
sec02-card-r32.expected_back: Yield to construction workers and vehicles actively working on the road.

sec02-card-r33.front: Which lane choice should you make when passing a construction vehicle actively working on the roadway?
sec02-card-r33.expected_back: Move to a lane away from a construction vehicle working on the roadway.

sec02-card-r23.front: Who must yield when another vehicle has already entered the intersection from a cross road?
sec02-card-r23.expected_back: Yield to a vehicle that has already entered the intersection from another road.

sec02-card-r24.front: When two vehicles from different roads reach an intersection at about the same time, who yields to whom?
sec02-card-r24.expected_back: When vehicles enter an intersection from different roadways at about the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec02-card-r25.front: To whom must you yield at an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or signals?
sec02-card-r25.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right.

sec02-card-r26.front: After stopping at a stop-controlled entrance to a through road, when may you enter?
sec02-card-r26.expected_back: At a stop-controlled entrance to a through road, stop and enter only without interfering with traffic.

sec02-card-r36.front: Who yields when a vehicle enters a public roadway from a private driveway or side road?
sec02-card-r36.expected_back: A vehicle entering from a private drive or side road yields to traffic on the public roadway.

sec02-card-r37.front: What two-step sequence applies before crossing a sidewalk from an alley, driveway, or building in a business or residential district?
sec02-card-r37.expected_back: Before crossing the sidewalk from an alley, driveway or building in a business or residential district, stop and then yield.

sec02-card-r38.front: When does a yield sign require a full stop?
sec02-card-r38.expected_back: At a yield sign, stop only when needed to avoid interfering with priority traffic or pedestrians.

sec02-card-r39.front: What exit condition is required before entering an intersection, crosswalk, or railroad crossing?
sec02-card-r39.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection, crosswalk or railroad crossing without space beyond it for your vehicle.

sec02-card-r40.front: Does a green traffic signal allow you to enter an intersection if traffic blocks room on the far side?
sec02-card-r40.expected_back: A green signal does not permit entering an intersection that lacks room beyond it.

sec02-card-r41.front: Is parking inside an intersection permitted in Kansas?
sec02-card-r41.expected_back: Parking inside an intersection is prohibited.

sec02-card-r42.front: What is the Kansas parking rule for intersection crosswalks?
sec02-card-r42.expected_back: Parking in an intersection crosswalk is prohibited.

sec02-card-r43.front: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Kansas?
sec02-card-r43.expected_back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant.

sec02-card-r44.front: What is the maximum distance your parked wheels may sit away from the curb in Kansas?
sec02-card-r44.expected_back: Do not park with the vehicle more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec02-card-r45.front: What is the Kansas rule on parking in front of a driveway?
sec02-card-r45.expected_back: Parking in front of a driveway is prohibited.

sec02-card-r46.front: May you park on a highway bridge or elevated roadway structure in Kansas?
sec02-card-r46.expected_back: Parking on a highway bridge or elevated structure is prohibited.

sec02-card-r47.front: What is the Kansas rule regarding parking inside a highway tunnel?
sec02-card-r47.expected_back: Parking inside a tunnel is prohibited.

sec02-card-r48.front: What must you do wherever regulatory signs prohibit parking?
sec02-card-r48.expected_back: Do not park where official signs prohibit parking.

sec02-card-r49.front: Is parking alongside another car already parked at the curb allowed in Kansas?
sec02-card-r49.expected_back: Double parking along the curb or roadside is prohibited.

sec02-card-r50.front: When is parking prohibited along a narrow Kansas road?
sec02-card-r50.expected_back: Do not park on a narrow road where the vehicle would obstruct ordinary traffic.

sec02-card-r51.front: May you park a vehicle on a sidewalk in Kansas?
sec02-card-r51.expected_back: Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited.

sec02-card-r52.front: Within how many feet approaching a roadside signal, stop sign, or flashing beacon is parking banned?
sec02-card-r52.expected_back: Do not park within the thirty-foot approach to a roadside signal, stop sign or flashing beacon.

sec02-card-r53.front: May you park in the space between a pedestrian safety zone and the adjacent curb?
sec02-card-r53.expected_back: Do not park between a safety zone and the nearby curb.

sec02-card-r54.front: Within how many feet of the curb points opposite the ends of a safety zone is parking prohibited?
sec02-card-r54.expected_back: Do not park within thirty feet of the curb points opposite the ends of a safety zone.

sec02-card-r55.front: At least how many feet from the nearest railroad-crossing rail must parked vehicles stay?
sec02-card-r55.expected_back: Keep parked vehicles at least fifty feet from the nearest railroad-crossing rail.

sec02-card-r56.front: Within how many feet of a fire-station driveway entrance on the same side is parking prohibited?
sec02-card-r56.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a fire-station driveway entrance.

sec02-card-r57.front: Within how many feet on the opposite street side of a fire-station entrance is parking prohibited?
sec02-card-r57.expected_back: On the opposite side of a fire-station entrance, the handbook prohibits parking within seventy-five feet.

sec02-card-r58.front: When is parking beside or opposite street excavations, roadwork, or obstructions illegal?
sec02-card-r58.expected_back: Do not park beside or opposite roadwork or another obstruction when doing so would block traffic.

sec02-card-r59.front: How does the Kansas handbook classify designated disability-parking spaces?
sec02-card-r59.expected_back: The handbook lists designated disability-parking spaces among restricted parking locations.

sec02-card-r60.front: Which three actions involving written electronic communication does Kansas prohibit while driving?
sec02-card-r60.expected_back: Kansas prohibits composing, sending or reading written electronic communication while driving.

sec02-card-r61.front: Which two everyday message types does the Kansas handbook explicitly include under written electronic communication?
sec02-card-r61.expected_back: The written-communication restriction includes text messages and email.

sec02-card-r62.front: Which two digital functions does the Kansas handbook exclude from its written-communication prohibition?
sec02-card-r62.expected_back: The handbook excludes GPS use and weather reports from its written-communication prohibition.

sec02-card-r63.front: Are talking or dialing on a cell phone specifically banned by Kansas's general adult electronic-communication rule?
sec02-card-r63.expected_back: Talking or dialing on a cell phone is not specifically prohibited by the general rule described in this section.

sec02-card-r64.front: Is a distracting in-car activity safe just because Kansas law does not specifically prohibit it?
sec02-card-r64.expected_back: A distracting activity remains dangerous even when it is not specifically prohibited.

sec02-card-r65.front: What is your best immediate physical response when an aggressive driver closes in?
sec02-card-r65.expected_back: Move out of an aggressive driver's way.

sec02-card-r66.front: Why must you never speed up or defend your lane spot against an aggressive driver?
sec02-card-r66.expected_back: Do not provoke an aggressive driver by accelerating or defending your place in traffic.

sec02-card-r67.front: Why does the Kansas handbook advise avoiding eye contact with an angry or aggressive driver?
sec02-card-r67.expected_back: Avoid eye contact that could further anger an aggressive driver.

sec02-card-r68.front: How should you respond if another driver shouts insults or makes hostile hand gestures?
sec02-card-r68.expected_back: Ignore hostile gestures or insults without responding in kind.

sec03-card-f01.front: Which five personal qualities does the Kansas handbook say safe driving depends on?
sec03-card-f01.expected_back: Safe driving depends on clear sight, alertness, freedom from alcohol or drug impairment, health and emotional readiness.

sec03-card-f02.front: How does poor vision undermine your safety behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f02.expected_back: Poor vision makes it harder to detect road conditions and respond to danger promptly.

sec03-card-f03.front: What sensory check does Kansas require every applicant to pass before issuing a driver license?
sec03-card-f03.expected_back: Kansas requires a successful vision test before issuing a driver license.

sec03-card-f04.front: What is the Kansas vision standard for licensing, and may corrective lenses be used to meet it?
sec03-card-f04.expected_back: The vision standard is at least twenty over forty in one eye, using corrective lenses if needed.

sec03-card-f05.front: What must a driver do when their Kansas license carries a corrective-lens restriction?
sec03-card-f05.expected_back: A corrective-lens license restriction requires the driver to wear glasses or contacts while driving.

sec03-card-f06.front: Why does the Kansas handbook recommend scheduling regular eye examinations?
sec03-card-f06.expected_back: Get regular eye examinations because deteriorating vision may otherwise go unnoticed.

sec03-card-f07.front: Does a corrective-lens restriction apply when running a quick drive close to home?
sec03-card-f07.memory_hook: Short local drives still require lenses
sec03-card-f07.expected_back: A corrective-lens requirement applies even to a short local drive.

sec03-card-f08.front: Why should drivers with a corrective-lens requirement keep a spare pair inside the vehicle?
sec03-card-f08.expected_back: Keep spare corrective lenses in the vehicle in case the usual pair is damaged or lost.

sec03-card-f09.front: Why does the Kansas handbook warn against wearing tinted lenses when driving at night?
sec03-card-f09.expected_back: Avoid tinted lenses at night because they reduce the light available for seeing.

sec03-card-f10.front: Which three traffic sounds can alert a driver to approaching danger before it appears in view?
sec03-card-f10.expected_back: Horns, sirens and skidding-tire sounds can warn a driver about danger.

sec03-card-f11.front: What two changes can a sudden shift in tire noise warn you about?
sec03-card-f11.expected_back: A change in tire noise may signal a changed road surface or tire condition.

sec03-card-f12.front: What can listening to engine sounds reveal while you drive?
sec03-card-f12.expected_back: Engine sounds can provide clues about how the engine is operating.

sec03-card-f13.front: How can hearing loss develop over time without a driver realizing it?
sec03-card-f13.expected_back: Hearing loss can develop gradually without being noticed.

sec03-card-f14.front: How does the Kansas handbook define fatigue, and what common factors trigger it?
sec03-card-f14.expected_back: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness caused by factors such as strain, repetition, illness or insufficient sleep.

sec03-card-f15.front: Which two fundamental driving faculties does fatigue directly weaken?

sec03-card-f16.front: Which two roadway estimates can fatigue distort while you are moving?
sec03-card-f16.expected_back: Fatigue can distort judgments about speed and distance.

sec03-card-f17.front: How does fatigue change a driver's decision speed and emotional temper?
sec03-card-f17.expected_back: A fatigued driver may take longer to decide and become irritated more easily.

sec03-card-f18.front: What ultimate danger makes fatigued driving raise crash risk so sharply?
sec03-card-f18.expected_back: Fatigue increases crash risk and may lead to falling asleep while driving.

sec03-card-f19.front: How many hours of sleep do most adults need to stay properly alert during the day?
sec03-card-f19.expected_back: Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep to stay properly alert during the day.

sec03-card-f20.front: How often should you plan rest breaks by distance or time on a long drive?
sec03-card-f20.expected_back: On a long trip, plan a rest break about every one hundred miles or every two hours.

sec03-card-f21.front: Which two fatigue-fighting benefits can a travel companion provide on a long trip?
sec03-card-f21.expected_back: A travel companion can provide conversation and share driving duties.

sec03-card-f22.front: Which two categories of substances should you avoid before starting a trip to prevent drowsiness?
sec03-card-f22.expected_back: Before a trip, avoid alcohol and medicines that cause sedation.

sec03-card-f23.front: How should you check whether a medicine could cause sedating effects before driving?
sec03-card-f23.expected_back: Check medicine labels or ask a doctor about sedating effects before driving.

sec03-card-f24.front: What does needing loud radio volume or an open window to stay awake tell you?
sec03-card-f24.expected_back: Needing loud radio sound or an open window to remain awake is a fatigue warning.

sec03-card-f25.front: What warning condition is active whenever you struggle to keep your eyes open?
sec03-card-f25.expected_back: Trouble keeping the eyes open is a fatigue warning.

sec03-card-f26.front: What driver condition is signaled by drifting out of your travel lane?
sec03-card-f26.expected_back: Drifting out of the lane is a fatigue warning.

sec03-card-f27.front: What should you do when fatigued, and where should you go instead of pressing on?
sec03-card-f27.expected_back: When fatigued, stop driving and use an exit, rest area or overnight sleeping place.

sec03-card-f28.front: How long of a nap in a safe parking place does the Kansas handbook recommend when sleepy?
sec03-card-f28.expected_back: The handbook recommends a fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap in a safe parking place when sleepy.

sec03-card-f29.front: How much caffeine does the Kansas handbook say can temporarily improve alertness?
sec03-card-f29.expected_back: The handbook says caffeine comparable to two cups of coffee can temporarily improve alertness.

sec03-card-f30.front: Why must drivers never rely on caffeine alone to prevent fatigue?
sec03-card-f30.expected_back: Caffeine wears off and must not be relied on to prevent fatigue.

sec03-card-f31.front: How does the Kansas handbook suggest pairing caffeine and a brief nap?
sec03-card-f31.expected_back: The handbook suggests having caffeine, followed by a brief nap, to gain benefits from both.

sec03-card-f32.front: Between which late-night hours does the Kansas handbook advise avoiding driving?
sec03-card-f32.expected_back: Try to avoid late-night driving between midnight and six a.m.

sec03-card-f33.front: What does the Kansas handbook identify as the best prevention for driver fatigue?
sec03-card-f33.expected_back: Sleep is the best prevention for fatigue.

sec03-card-f34.front: How does the Kansas handbook define a driving distraction?
sec03-card-f34.expected_back: A distraction is anything that draws attention away from operating the vehicle.

sec03-card-f35.front: Can a mental distraction endanger you even while your eyes stay pointed at the road?
sec03-card-f35.expected_back: A mental distraction can be dangerous even while the driver's eyes face the road.

sec03-card-f36.front: Which common electronic devices inside a car can pull attention away from driving?
sec03-card-f36.expected_back: Using a phone, navigation system or other electronic device can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f37.front: How can adjusting audio or climate controls while moving affect your driving?
sec03-card-f37.expected_back: Changing audio or climate settings while moving can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f38.front: Which personal habits like eating or grooming does the handbook warn can divert driving attention?
sec03-card-f38.expected_back: Grooming, eating, drinking or smoking can divert driving attention.

sec03-card-f39.front: How can cabin conversations, children, or unrestrained pets affect driver focus?
sec03-card-f39.expected_back: Conversations and attending to children or pets can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f40.front: What risk comes from reading maps or printed material behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f40.expected_back: Reading maps or other material can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f41.front: Why is reaching down for a dropped object while moving a classic crash trigger?
sec03-card-f41.expected_back: Reaching for a dropped object can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f42.front: How does staring at a roadside crash or police traffic stop endanger your own lane?
sec03-card-f42.expected_back: Watching a roadside crash or traffic stop can divert attention from driving.

sec03-card-f43.front: How does the handbook classify bright sunlight or a dramatic sunset along your drive?
sec03-card-f43.expected_back: Sunlight or a sunset can become an outside distraction.

sec03-card-f44.front: What roadway activity and obstacles can pull a driver's attention away from steering?
sec03-card-f44.expected_back: People or objects in the roadway, as well as road construction, can divert attention from driving.

sec03-card-f45.front: How can reading billboards or roadside advertisements affect vehicle control?
sec03-card-f45.expected_back: Reading billboards or roadside advertisements can distract a driver.

sec03-card-f58.front: What caution does the Kansas handbook give about high doses of caffeine when fighting fatigue?
sec03-card-f58.expected_back: The handbook advises avoiding excessive caffeine when responding to fatigue.

sec03-card-f46.front: What should you do first if you need to use a cell phone during a trip?
sec03-card-f46.expected_back: Park safely before using a cell phone.

sec03-card-f47.front: Which kinds of conversations should you avoid while behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f47.expected_back: Avoid arguments and stressful conversations that compete with attention to the road.

sec03-card-f48.front: How should you handle meals on a trip instead of eating behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f48.expected_back: Allow time to stop for food instead of eating while driving.

sec03-card-f49.front: How should you prepare children before pulling out on a drive?
sec03-card-f49.expected_back: Secure children properly and give them suitable activities before traveling.

sec03-card-f50.front: How should pets ride inside a vehicle, and when must you secure them?
sec03-card-f50.expected_back: Secure pets in a carrier or portable kennel before moving the vehicle.

sec03-card-f51.front: At what three safe moments or ways should vehicle controls be adjusted?
sec03-card-f51.expected_back: Set vehicle controls before departure, at normal stops or with a passenger's help.

sec03-card-f52.front: Where should you keep your attention instead of looking at distant roadside distractions?
sec03-card-f52.expected_back: Keep attention on the immediate travel path rather than distant distractions.

sec03-card-f53.front: When should you plan your route and study maps for an unfamiliar drive?
sec03-card-f53.expected_back: Plan the route and review maps before driving.

sec03-card-f54.front: What must you do first if you need to check a map midway through a trip?
sec03-card-f54.expected_back: If a map must be checked during a trip, first park in a safe place.

sec03-card-f55.front: What rule applies to talking with friends riding in another vehicle alongside yours?
sec03-card-f55.expected_back: Do not converse with friends in another vehicle while driving.

sec03-card-f56.front: What does the Kansas handbook say about wearing music headphones while driving?
sec03-card-f56.expected_back: Do not wear music headphones while driving.

sec03-card-f57.front: Who remains legally responsible if an in-car or roadside distraction contributes to a crash?
sec03-card-f57.expected_back: The driver remains responsible for safe vehicle operation when a distraction contributes to a crash.

sec03-card-r01.front: How does the Kansas handbook define aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r01.expected_back: Aggressive driving involves an intentional driving action or moving traffic violation that endangers people or property.

sec03-card-r02.front: Which three everyday speed and spacing violations does the handbook link to aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r02.expected_back: Speeding, tailgating and unsafe lane changes are examples associated with aggressive driving.

sec03-card-r03.front: How do blowing past traffic controls or signaling improperly relate to aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r03.expected_back: Ignoring traffic controls or signaling improperly can be part of aggressive driving.

sec03-card-r04.front: Which threatening or pursuit behaviors does the handbook list alongside aggressive driving examples?
sec03-card-r04.expected_back: Threatening another driver with a weapon, making hostile gestures or chasing a vehicle to cause harm are examples associated with aggressive driving.

sec03-card-r05.front: What mental posture helps a driver avoid slipping into aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r05.expected_back: To avoid aggressive driving, relax and concentrate on the driving task.

sec03-card-r06.front: How do obeying posted speed limits and planning enough travel time reduce aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r06.expected_back: Use the posted speed limit and plan a realistic travel time to reduce aggressive driving.

sec03-card-r07.front: What social attitude toward other road users helps prevent aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r07.expected_back: Courteous and forgiving behavior helps prevent aggressive driving.

sec03-card-r08.front: What two actions should you take when facing serious aggressive driving behavior?
sec03-card-r08.expected_back: Leave the area if possible and report serious aggressive behavior.

sec03-card-r09.front: How do even small amounts of alcohol or impairing drugs affect collision risk?
sec03-card-r09.expected_back: Alcohol or other impairing drugs increase collision risk even in small amounts.

sec03-card-r10.front: Which three actions involving alcoholic beverages are illegal for people younger than twenty-one?
sec03-card-r10.memory_hook: No buying, holding, drinking under twenty-one
sec03-card-r10.expected_back: People younger than twenty-one may not purchase, possess or drink alcoholic beverages.

sec03-card-r11.front: Which three core driving abilities do alcohol and impairing drugs reduce?
sec03-card-r11.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs reduce perception, emergency response and vehicle-control ability.

sec03-card-r13.front: Which brain functions are disrupted early by alcohol and impairing drugs?
sec03-card-r13.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs interfere with the brain functions used for judgment.

sec03-card-r14.front: Which three vision problems can alcohol and certain drugs trigger behind the wheel?
sec03-card-r14.expected_back: Alcohol and some drugs can blur sight, delay focusing or cause double vision.

sec03-card-r15.front: What three traffic measurements become harder to judge under alcohol or drug impairment?
sec03-card-r15.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs reduce the ability to judge distance, speed and other vehicles' motion.

sec03-card-r16.front: What three lane-departure behaviors appear as driver impairment increases?
sec03-card-r16.expected_back: Increasing impairment can lead to lane wandering, crossing the center line or leaving the road.

sec03-card-r17.front: At how low a blood alcohol concentration does the Kansas handbook state vision is already affected?
sec03-card-r17.memory_hook: Vision drops at point zero two
sec03-card-r17.expected_back: The handbook states that vision is affected at a BAC of point zero two.

sec03-card-r18.front: How can alcohol and impairing drugs affect how you read traffic signs and signals?
sec03-card-r18.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs can reduce the ability to tell road-sign and signal colors apart.

sec03-card-r19.front: What do alcohol and impairing drugs do to mental information processing and driving responses?
sec03-card-r19.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs slow information processing and responses to driving tasks.

sec03-card-r20.front: Besides slowing reactions, what do alcohol and impairing drugs do to wakefulness and situational awareness?
sec03-card-r20.expected_back: Alcohol and impairing drugs can cause drowsiness and reduce awareness of surroundings.

sec03-card-r21.front: What responsibility do you have toward a friend or relative who has been drinking?
sec03-card-r21.expected_back: Do not let a friend or relative drive after drinking.

sec03-card-r22.front: What direct step with car keys does the handbook suggest when a friend or relative has been drinking?
sec03-card-r22.expected_back: For a friend or relative who has been drinking, the handbook suggests taking away their keys.

sec03-card-r23.front: Who should you line up to drive a friend or relative who has consumed alcohol?
sec03-card-r23.expected_back: Arrange a driver who has not been drinking for a friend or relative who has consumed alcohol.

sec03-card-r24.front: What paid transport option does the handbook list instead of letting a drinking friend drive?
sec03-card-r24.expected_back: Calling a taxi is an alternative to letting a friend or relative drive after drinking.

sec03-card-r25.front: What hosting alternative keeps a friend or relative off the road after drinking?
sec03-card-r25.expected_back: Having a friend or relative stay overnight is an alternative to letting them drive after drinking.

sec03-card-r26.front: Does drinking hot coffee clear alcohol or other drugs out of your bloodstream?
sec03-card-r26.expected_back: Coffee does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation.

sec03-card-r27.front: Does breathing fresh air remove alcohol or drugs from your circulation?
sec03-card-r27.expected_back: Fresh air does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation.

sec03-card-r28.front: Does taking a cold shower eliminate alcohol or impairing drugs from circulation?
sec03-card-r28.expected_back: A cold shower does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation.

sec03-card-r29.front: Once alcohol or drugs are in circulation, does eating food remove them?
sec03-card-r29.expected_back: Eating does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation.

sec03-card-r30.front: What is the only medically proven way to clear alcohol or drug combinations from circulation?
sec03-card-r30.expected_back: The handbook identifies passage of time as the only medically proven way to remove alcohol or drug combinations from circulation.

sec03-card-r31.front: How many alcoholic drinks does it take before driving ability can begin to drop?
sec03-card-r31.expected_back: Even a first alcoholic drink can impair the ability to drive.

sec03-card-r32.front: What is the safest rule in the Kansas handbook regarding alcohol, impairing drugs, and driving?
sec03-card-r32.expected_back: The safest advice in the handbook is to avoid driving after consuming alcohol or impairing drugs.

sec03-card-r33.front: What blood alcohol concentration violates the standard Kansas alcohol-driving law?
sec03-card-r33.expected_back: A BAC of point zero eight or greater violates the alcohol-driving law described in the handbook.

sec03-card-r34.front: What suspension length and legal consequences does the handbook note for a BAC of point zero eight or higher?
