sec03-card-f45.teaching_text: Roadside ads are designed to grab your eyes at the exact moment highway traffic compresses.

sec03-card-f58.question_text: What caution does the Kansas handbook give about high doses of caffeine when fighting fatigue?
sec03-card-f58.teaching_text: Overloading energy drinks or coffee causes jittery hands, racing pulse, and a steeper crash later.

sec03-card-f46.question_text: What should you do first if you need to use a cell phone during a trip?
sec03-card-f46.teaching_text: Pulling into a legal parking space removes all crash risk before dialing or checking messages.

sec03-card-f47.question_text: Which kinds of conversations should you avoid while behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f47.teaching_text: Heated cabin arguments hijack your working memory and trigger abrupt, aggressive steering and pedal inputs.

sec03-card-f48.question_text: How should you handle meals on a trip instead of eating behind the wheel?
sec03-card-f48.teaching_text: Stopping ten minutes to eat keeps both hands dry and committed to steering.

sec03-card-f49.question_text: How should you prepare children before pulling out on a drive?
sec03-card-f49.teaching_text: Settling harnesses and handing over quiet toys before shifting into drive prevents mid-highway turnarounds.

sec03-card-f50.question_text: How should pets ride inside a vehicle, and when must you secure them?
sec03-card-f50.teaching_text: An uncrated dog can leap onto your lap or wedge under the brake pedal mid-stop.

sec03-card-f51.question_text: At what three safe moments or ways should vehicle controls be adjusted?
sec03-card-f51.teaching_text: Letting your front passenger tune vents or waiting for a stop keeps your eyes locked up front.

sec03-card-f52.question_text: Where should you keep your attention instead of looking at distant roadside distractions?
sec03-card-f52.teaching_text: Your immediate lane corridor holds the brake lights, debris, and merges that demand instant reaction.

sec03-card-f53.question_text: When should you plan your route and study maps for an unfamiliar drive?
sec03-card-f53.teaching_text: Knowing exit numbers upfront prevents last-second three-lane dives across highway gore zones.

sec03-card-f54.question_text: What must you do first if you need to check a map midway through a trip?
sec03-card-f54.teaching_text: Pulling into a lot takes seconds, whereas reading directions in motion risks drifting into oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-f55.question_text: What rule applies to talking with friends riding in another vehicle alongside yours?
sec03-card-f55.teaching_text: Pacing another car window-to-window blocks passing lanes and pulls both drivers' eyes sideways.

sec03-card-f56.question_text: What does the Kansas handbook say about wearing music headphones while driving?
sec03-card-f56.teaching_text: Earbuds and over-ear headphones seal out sirens, train horns, and screeching brakes around you.

sec03-card-f57.question_text: Who remains legally responsible if an in-car or roadside distraction contributes to a crash?
sec03-card-f57.teaching_text: Blaming a ringing phone, crying toddler, or billboard never excuses a driver from safe control.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: How does the Kansas handbook define aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Notice the word intentional—deliberate traffic violations that put lives or vehicles at risk cross into aggression.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: Which three everyday speed and spacing violations does the handbook link to aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Stacking excessive speed with bumper-riding and abrupt weaving multiplies multi-car highway pileups.

sec03-card-r03.question_text: How do blowing past traffic controls or signaling improperly relate to aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: Running red lights or cutting across lanes unannounced robs nearby drivers of predictable right-of-way.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: Which threatening or pursuit behaviors does the handbook list alongside aggressive driving examples?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Brandishing weapons, flashing hostile gestures, or chasing a car turns traffic conflict into violent crime.

sec03-card-r05.question_text: What mental posture helps a driver avoid slipping into aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Letting your shoulders drop and locking onto smooth driving keeps minor delays from sparking anger.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: How do obeying posted speed limits and planning enough travel time reduce aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: Running late fuels tailgating and risky passes, whereas leaving with spare minutes erases clock pressure.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: What social attitude toward other road users helps prevent aggressive driving?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: Assuming another driver made an honest mistake instead of taking offense defuses tension immediately.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: What two actions should you take when facing serious aggressive driving behavior?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Exiting safely and calling authorities puts trained officers—not your bumper—between a violent driver and traffic.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: How do even small amounts of alcohol or impairing drugs affect collision risk?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Collision odds climb with the very first dose long before a driver feels noticeably drunk.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: Which three actions involving alcoholic beverages are illegal for people younger than twenty-one?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: Merely holding an unopened beer under twenty-one violates possession law even without taking a sip.
sec03-card-r10.must_match_memory_hook: No buying, holding, drinking under twenty-one

visual_sync.text_span: No buying, holding, drinking under twenty-one

sec03-card-r11.question_text: Which three core driving abilities do alcohol and impairing drugs reduce?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: You spot trouble late, react sluggishly, and steer clumsily all at once when impaired.

sec03-card-r13.question_text: Which brain functions are disrupted early by alcohol and impairing drugs?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Because self-assessment breaks first, impaired drivers feel confident right when their skills have collapsed.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: Which three vision problems can alcohol and certain drugs trigger behind the wheel?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: Sluggish eye muscles struggle to shift between your speedometer and dark highway lanes.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: What three traffic measurements become harder to judge under alcohol or drug impairment?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: Pulling left across oncoming headlights turns deadly when your brain misreads closing speed and gap distance.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: What three lane-departure behaviors appear as driver impairment increases?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: Weaving inside lanes, drifting over yellow center stripes, and running off shoulders are classic DUI arrest cues.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: At how low a blood alcohol concentration does the Kansas handbook state vision is already affected?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: At just one-fourth of the adult per-se limit, tracking moving objects already starts degrading.
sec03-card-r17.must_match_memory_hook: Vision drops at point zero two

visual_sync.text_span: Vision drops at point zero two

sec03-card-r18.question_text: How can alcohol and impairing drugs affect how you read traffic signs and signals?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Weakened color contrast makes red, amber, and warning hues harder to distinguish at night.

sec03-card-r19.question_text: What do alcohol and impairing drugs do to mental information processing and driving responses?
sec03-card-r19.teaching_text: When multiple hazards unfold together, an impaired brain cannot sort steering and braking fast enough.

sec03-card-r20.question_text: Besides slowing reactions, what do alcohol and impairing drugs do to wakefulness and situational awareness?
sec03-card-r20.teaching_text: Sedating effects narrow awareness down to a tunnel while pulling drivers toward sleep.

sec03-card-r21.question_text: What responsibility do you have toward a friend or relative who has been drinking?
sec03-card-r21.teaching_text: Stepping in awkwardly for thirty seconds beats living with a preventable impaired crash.

sec03-card-r22.question_text: What direct step with car keys does the handbook suggest when a friend or relative has been drinking?
sec03-card-r22.teaching_text: Removing the keys stops an impaired impulse decision to sneak out to the parking lot.

sec03-card-r23.question_text: Who should you line up to drive a friend or relative who has consumed alcohol?
sec03-card-r23.teaching_text: Pick someone who has had zero alcohol—not merely the person in the group who drank least.

sec03-card-r24.question_text: What paid transport option does the handbook list instead of letting a drinking friend drive?
sec03-card-r24.teaching_text: Any cab fare costs pennies next to court fines, interlocks, or an injury crash.

sec03-card-r25.question_text: What hosting alternative keeps a friend or relative off the road after drinking?
sec03-card-r25.teaching_text: Offering a guest room or couch lets time clear alcohol before morning keys come back out.

sec03-card-r26.question_text: Does drinking hot coffee clear alcohol or other drugs out of your bloodstream?
sec03-card-r26.teaching_text: Coffee only creates a wide-awake impaired driver whose BAC and reaction deficits stay unchanged.

sec03-card-r27.question_text: Does breathing fresh air remove alcohol or drugs from your circulation?
sec03-card-r27.teaching_text: Stepping outside into brisk air feels refreshing for a minute while your liver metabolizes zero faster.

sec03-card-r28.question_text: Does taking a cold shower eliminate alcohol or impairing drugs from circulation?
sec03-card-r28.teaching_text: Cold water shocks your skin awake without lowering blood alcohol concentration a single point.

sec03-card-r29.question_text: Once alcohol or drugs are in circulation, does eating food remove them?
sec03-card-r29.teaching_text: Once alcohol enters your bloodstream, late-night food cannot sponge it back out of circulation.

sec03-card-r30.question_text: What is the only medically proven way to clear alcohol or drug combinations from circulation?
sec03-card-r30.teaching_text: Every exam distractor—coffee, showers, food, fresh air—loses to the passage of time.

sec03-card-r31.question_text: How many alcoholic drinks does it take before driving ability can begin to drop?
sec03-card-r31.teaching_text: Subtle judgment and eye-tracking losses begin on the very first drink, well below legal arrest limits.

sec03-card-r32.question_text: What is the safest rule in the Kansas handbook regarding alcohol, impairing drugs, and driving?
sec03-card-r32.teaching_text: Separating drinking or impairing medications completely from driving eliminates guesswork about BAC numbers.

sec03-card-r33.question_text: What blood alcohol concentration violates the standard Kansas alcohol-driving law?
sec03-card-r33.teaching_text: Hitting point zero eight or higher is an automatic violation regardless of how steady someone claims to feel.

sec03-card-r34.question_text: What suspension length and legal consequences does the handbook note for a BAC of point zero eight or higher?
sec03-card-r34.teaching_text: Administrative license suspension and criminal prosecution run on parallel tracks after a failed alcohol test.

sec03-card-r35.question_text: At what blood alcohol percentage can Kansas drivers younger than twenty-one be arrested for impairment?
sec03-card-r35.teaching_text: Even trace alcohol from a single drink or mouthwash spike can hit point zero two percent.

sec03-card-r36.question_text: How does blood alcohol concentration express the amount of alcohol in a person's body?
sec03-card-r36.teaching_text: BAC tracks concentration inside your bloodstream, rising faster in lighter bodies or rapid drinking.

sec03-card-r37.question_text: Can you still be convicted of impaired driving in Kansas with a BAC below point zero eight?
sec03-card-r37.teaching_text: Point zero eight is never a free pass—weaving or failing roadside checks convicts you at lower numbers.
sec03-card-r37.must_match_memory_hook: Below point zero eight still convicts

visual_sync.text_span: Below point zero eight still convicts

sec03-card-r75.question_text: How widespread are zero-tolerance or similar underage alcohol-driving laws across the United States?
sec03-card-r75.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never relaxes strict under-twenty-one alcohol enforcement anywhere in America.

sec03-card-r76.question_text: Which two personal resources does judgment draw upon when you face a brand-new traffic problem?
sec03-card-r76.teaching_text: Studying rules builds the knowledge half while supervised practice builds the experience half.

sec03-card-r77.question_text: What does being sober strictly mean in the Kansas handbook?
sec03-card-r77.teaching_text: Feeling fine does not equal sobriety if alcohol or impairing substances remain in your bloodstream.

sec03-card-r38.question_text: Which three bodily samples do alcohol-concentration tests typically analyze?
sec03-card-r38.teaching_text: Officers choose approved breath, blood, or urine testing methods to measure exact alcohol concentration.

sec03-card-r39.question_text: What testing agreement do you make under Kansas implied-consent law simply by obtaining a driver license?
sec03-card-r39.teaching_text: Accepting a Kansas license carries pre-agreed consent to lawful officer alcohol testing whenever impairment is suspected.

sec03-card-r40.question_text: How long can you lose your license for refusing a lawfully requested police alcohol test?
sec03-card-r40.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside triggers a one-year suspension under implied consent.
sec03-card-r40.must_match_memory_hook: Refusing police tests costs one year

visual_sync.text_span: Refusing police tests costs one year

sec03-card-r41.question_text: What fine range plus extra fees does the handbook describe for a first alcohol-driving conviction?
sec03-card-r41.teaching_text: Court costs stack right on top of the seven-hundred-fifty to one-thousand-dollar base fine.

sec03-card-r42.question_text: What jail time or community-service hours can accompany a first Kansas alcohol-driving conviction?
sec03-card-r42.teaching_text: Even a very first offense exposes you to two full days behind bars or one hundred community-service hours.

sec03-card-r43.question_text: What happens to your driving privileges upon a first alcohol-driving conviction in Kansas?
sec03-card-r43.teaching_text: Beyond fines and jail, your first alcohol-driving conviction triggers mandatory license suspension.

sec03-card-r44.question_text: What vehicle device does the handbook require driving with after a first alcohol-driving conviction?
sec03-card-r44.teaching_text: Kansas does not save breath-lock devices for repeat offenders—interlock applies right after a first conviction.

sec03-card-r45.question_text: How do penalties change for second and subsequent alcohol-driving convictions?
sec03-card-r45.teaching_text: Fines, custody, suspension lengths, and interlock periods escalate sharply on every repeat offense.

sec03-card-r46.question_text: How severely can prescription and over-the-counter medicines impair driving compared with alcohol?
sec03-card-r46.teaching_text: A doctor's prescription or drugstore receipt never shields you from impairment crashes or DUI charges.

sec03-card-r47.question_text: Which four common household medicine types can trigger drowsiness behind the wheel?
sec03-card-r47.teaching_text: Antihistamines and decongestants often hit peak drowsiness thirty minutes into your morning commute.

sec03-card-r48.question_text: Which four driving hazards can stimulant and diet pills cause?
sec03-card-r48.teaching_text: Pills taken to stay awake backfire with shaky focus, dizziness, and vision glitches.

sec03-card-r49.question_text: What should you read before taking any nonprescription drug product?
sec03-card-r49.teaching_text: Checking the box after swallowing is too late once you already need to drive.

sec03-card-r50.question_text: Whom should you ask when you are unsure how a medication affects safe driving?
sec03-card-r50.teaching_text: Pharmacists and doctors spot sedating interactions between prescriptions that single package labels miss.

sec03-card-r51.question_text: Which four driving faculties can prescription medications impair?
sec03-card-r51.teaching_text: Strong prescriptions dull the exact same mental and visual systems needed to avoid sudden hazards.

sec03-card-r52.question_text: Which four prescription drug categories does the handbook list as affecting safe driving?
sec03-card-r52.teaching_text: Next-morning hangover grogginess from sleep aids impairs morning commutes just like painkillers.

sec03-card-r53.question_text: When should you read prescription bottle and package warnings about medication effects?
sec03-card-r53.teaching_text: Amber pharmacy stickers warn against operating machinery before the dose enters your system.

sec03-card-r54.question_text: Which four core driving skills can illegal drugs impair?
sec03-card-r54.teaching_text: Illicit substances carry unpredictable potency that wrecks reaction timing, eyesight, and risk judgment.

sec03-card-r55.question_text: Which two driving problems does the handbook report more often among marijuana users than other drivers?
sec03-card-r55.teaching_text: Slowed tracking increases lane errors while oncoming headlights blind glare recovery longer at night.

sec03-card-r56.question_text: What fine range plus court costs applies to a first drug-impaired-driving conviction in the handbook?
sec03-card-r56.teaching_text: Kansas punishes first-time drug-impaired driving with the exact same dollar fine bracket as alcohol DUI.

sec03-card-r57.question_text: What minimum jail hours or community-service hours are listed for a first drug-impaired-driving conviction?
sec03-card-r57.teaching_text: First-time drug-impaired convictions mirror Kansas alcohol DUI custody minimums hour for hour in court.

sec03-card-r58.question_text: What happens to your driver license after a first drug-impaired-driving conviction?
sec03-card-r58.teaching_text: Driving impaired by drugs suspends your license on offense one just like failing a breath test.

sec03-card-r59.question_text: How do penalties shift for repeat drug-impaired-driving convictions?
sec03-card-r59.teaching_text: Every repeat drug-impaired conviction steps up fines, custody time, and license suspension penalties sharply.

sec03-card-r60.question_text: What rule does the handbook set on combining alcohol with other drugs?
sec03-card-r60.teaching_text: Even one drink alongside allergy pills or prescriptions triggers unpredictable chemical synergy.

sec03-card-r61.question_text: What two severe outcomes can happen when someone mixes alcohol and drugs?
sec03-card-r61.teaching_text: Combined substances multiply rather than add up, threatening both lethal crashes and medical overdose.

sec03-card-r62.question_text: Does years of driving experience make alcohol-impaired or drug-impaired driving safe?
sec03-card-r62.teaching_text: Seasoned habits cannot override slowed optic nerves and chemically delayed brake reactions.

sec03-card-r63.question_text: How can everyday ailments like a cold, cough, stiff neck, or sore leg affect driving?
sec03-card-r63.teaching_text: A stiff neck skips blind-spot shoulder checks while a sore right leg hesitates slamming the brake.

sec03-card-r64.question_text: What should you do when illness leaves you feeling unwell before a drive?
sec03-card-r64.teaching_text: Handing keys to a healthy driver avoids both feverish distraction and drowsy symptom medicines.

sec03-card-r78.question_text: Under Kansas implied consent, what must a driver suspected of impairment do when an officer lawfully requests a BAC test?
sec03-card-r78.teaching_text: Refusing a lawful police testing request triggers automatic implied-consent license suspension even before court.

sec03-card-r79.question_text: Which three actions involving illegal drugs does the Kansas handbook prohibit?
sec03-card-r79.teaching_text: Purchasing, possessing, and consuming illegal substances are unlawful before you ever touch a car door.

sec03-card-r80.question_text: How do traffic-violation arrest rates among marijuana users compare with other drivers in the handbook?
sec03-card-r80.teaching_text: Higher driving mistake rates translate directly into more traffic stops and violation arrests.

sec03-card-r81.question_text: Beyond fines, jail or service, and suspension, what else can a first drug-impaired-driving conviction bring?
sec03-card-r81.teaching_text: Possession charges, probation terms, and treatment orders frequently stack onto the base DUI sentence.

sec03-card-r65.question_text: Whom should you consult if a medical or health condition might prevent safe driving?
sec03-card-r65.teaching_text: Physicians evaluate seizure, heart, or mobility risks before a medical episode strikes in live traffic.

sec03-card-r66.question_text: Which three mental processes can strong emotions disrupt while you drive?
sec03-card-r66.teaching_text: Emotional overload crowds out hazard scanning just like texting or cognitive distraction.

sec03-card-r67.question_text: Which five strong emotional states does the handbook warn can prevent safe driving?
sec03-card-r67.teaching_text: Notice positive excitement sits right beside anger and sorrow—thrill-fueled distraction causes crashes too.

sec03-card-r68.question_text: What should you do before driving if you feel angry or intensely excited?
sec03-card-r68.teaching_text: Waiting parked until your pulse settles keeps raw adrenaline off the steering wheel and gas pedal.

sec03-card-r69.question_text: Which two simple activities can help an angry or excited person settle down before driving?
sec03-card-r69.teaching_text: Burning off adrenaline on foot or resting resets emotional control before turning the key.

sec03-card-r70.question_text: Where must you deliberately keep your focus if you have to drive while worried or upset?
sec03-card-r70.teaching_text: Replaying an upsetting problem in your head leaves intersections and brake lights unscanned.

sec03-card-r71.question_text: When can listening to the radio help a worried or upset driver?
sec03-card-r71.teaching_text: Steady background music can quiet racing thoughts only so long as tuning never steals attention.

sec03-card-r72.question_text: What two trip-planning habits should an impatient driver practice?
sec03-card-r72.teaching_text: Building extra cushion minutes removes the urge to tailgate slow traffic or beat yellow lights.

sec03-card-r73.question_text: Which two traffic behaviors must you avoid when feeling impatient?
sec03-card-r73.teaching_text: Weaving between cars saves almost zero arrival time while spiking sideswipe and rear-end odds.

sec03-card-r74.question_text: What safe travel option exists when strong emotions interfere with safe driving?
sec03-card-r74.teaching_text: Riding passenger when overwhelmed protects everyone just like handing off keys when sick.

sec03-card-r82.question_text: What effect can strong emotions have on a driver's willingness to take chances?
sec03-card-r82.teaching_text: Anger and excitement shrink perceived danger, tempting tight passes and excessive speed.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: When should you adjust your driver's seat and mirrors?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Reaching down for seat levers or twisting mirrors after shifting into gear pulls your eyes off traffic immediately.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: What sightline and control reach must your driving seat position give you?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Sitting where you can see over the dash and press pedals fully prevents hesitant braking in sudden emergencies.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: What safety cushion must you keep in mind when choosing how close to sit to the wheel?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Airbags punch outward at explosive speed, so crowding the steering hub turns a protective cushion into an impact hazard.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: How should your seat distance let your right foot move between the brake and gas pedals?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Anchoring your heel on the floorboard lets you swing crisply from gas to brake without lifting and missing a pedal.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: Besides sliding the seat, what steering hardware adjustment can help dial in your driving position?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Tilting or telescoping the column lets shorter and taller drivers keep safe chest clearance without sacrificing pedal reach.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: How high should the top rim of your steering wheel sit relative to your shoulders and chin?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Keeping the upper rim below your chin preserves a clean windshield sightline and aims the airbag below your face.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: How many inches of space does the seat-adjustment guide call for between your body and the lower steering wheel?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Ten inches of breathing room gives your arms freedom to turn rapidly while letting the front airbag inflate cleanly.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: What steering problem tells you that you have slid the driver's seat too far forward?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Sitting jammed against the wheel cramps your elbows against your ribs when you need fast evasive steering.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: Why must you avoid reclining the seatback too far backward while driving?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Leaning way back locks your elbows straight on the wheel and shifts your eyes out of your mirror angles.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: What two accessories can help a shorter driver see clearly over the steering wheel without sitting too close?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Raising your seating height or extending the pedals keeps you ten inches off the airbag while seeing the road.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: What specific neck injury do head restraints help prevent, and in what kind of collision?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: When another car hits your rear bumper, your torso shoots forward first and a well-set restraint catches your head.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: How does the Kansas handbook define whiplash after a collision?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Sudden crash acceleration whips soft neck tissues beyond normal motion limits, causing painful ligament and muscle strain.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: Where should the head restraint sit behind your head, and what is its lowest safe height?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Leaving a headrest dropped down behind your neck acts like a pivot point instead of catching the back of your skull.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: What should your center inside rearview mirror frame when properly aimed?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Centering the full rear glass lets quick eye glances spot fast-closing traffic without tilting your head sideways.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: How should you set an inside rearview mirror that has a day-and-night anti-glare setting?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Flipping to night mode cuts blinding high-beam glare after dark, while switching back restores full brightness at sunrise.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: What two posture steps come first before setting your outside mirrors the traditional way?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Aiming mirrors while slouched or before sliding your seat throws every reflection angle off once you sit normally.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: What part of your own vehicle appears in the traditional left-side mirror setup?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Showing a sliver of your left rear fender anchors where adjacent lane traffic sits relative to your bumper.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: What visual reference on your car appears in a traditionally adjusted right-side mirror?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Framing your right body edge helps judge curb distance and right-lane merges without filling the glass with door paint.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: On trucks, vans, and SUVs, which two tasks make traditional side-mirror settings especially useful?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: Seeing your own rear corners alongside a trailer or tight loading bay prevents scraping walls and jackknifing.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: Why shouldn't you rely solely on passenger-car side mirrors to reverse your car?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Outside mirrors leave a huge blind zone directly behind your rear bumper where children, carts, or posts hide.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: How do you position your head while aiming side mirrors under the enhanced mirror method?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: Leaning toward the window for the left mirror and toward center for the right pushes mirror coverage outward into blind zones.

sec04-card-f22.question_text: When sitting normally with enhanced side-mirror settings, do you see the sides of your own car?
sec04-card-f22.teaching_text: Removing redundant door paint from your normal glance shifts that mirror width outward into neighboring travel lanes.

sec04-card-f23.question_text: How many extra degrees of side viewing angle does enhanced mirror adjustment add on each side?
sec04-card-f23.teaching_text: Picking up twelve to sixteen degrees per side shrinks blind-spot pockets where passing cars usually vanish.

sec04-card-f24.question_text: Does enhanced mirror adjustment fit every vehicle on the road, or can traditional settings still be right?
sec04-card-f24.teaching_text: Blocked rear windows, cargo vans, or towing rigs often need traditional edge views instead of wide-outward car angles.

sec04-card-f25.question_text: When must you click your safety belt shut?
sec04-card-f25.teaching_text: Trying to thread a belt one-handed while rolling out of a driveway splits steering control right where pedestrians walk.

sec04-card-f26.question_text: What passenger safety check should a driver finish before pulling away?
sec04-card-f26.teaching_text: An unbuckled rider becomes a heavy human projectile inside the cabin during a rollover or side collision.

sec04-card-f27.question_text: What should you do with the vehicle's door locks before driving off?
sec04-card-f27.teaching_text: Locked doors are less likely to pop open during crash impacts and keep unwanted intruders out at red lights.

sec04-card-f28.question_text: Which door feature should you engage whenever young children ride in the back?
sec04-card-f28.teaching_text: Curious toddlers pull shiny interior handles at highway speed unless the rear child-safety latch disables inside opening.

sec04-card-f29.question_text: How do safety belts change your odds if a crash happens?
sec04-card-f29.teaching_text: Belts stretch slightly to absorb violent deceleration energy instead of letting your skull or chest absorb it.

sec04-card-f30.question_text: How can a modern safety belt let you lean for controls normally yet still hold you in a crash?
sec04-card-f30.teaching_text: Inertia reels pay out webbing during gentle reaches and clamp solid the instant sudden braking or impact hits.

sec04-card-f31.question_text: Which two deadly crash movements does wearing a safety belt help stop?
sec04-card-f31.teaching_text: Being thrown through glass or slammed into pillars accounts for a huge share of fatal crash trauma.

sec04-card-f32.question_text: How does wearing a safety belt help you control the car during a swerve or glancing hit?
sec04-card-f32.teaching_text: You cannot steer or brake out of a skid if the first jolt slides you across the center console.

sec04-card-f33.question_text: What does Kansas law say about operating a vehicle without wearing a safety belt?
sec04-card-f33.teaching_text: Kansas treats driver belt use as a mandatory legal duty rather than a personal comfort choice.

sec04-card-f34.question_text: Does Kansas law allow a front-seat passenger to ride unbuckled?
sec04-card-f34.teaching_text: Front passengers face the windshield and dashboard directly, so state law requires their belt fastened too.

sec04-card-f35.question_text: Should you still buckle up on quick neighborhood errands and low-speed streets?
sec04-card-f35.teaching_text: Many serious crashes happen close to home at everyday city speeds where unbuckled heads still slam windshields.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: Where across your upper body should the shoulder belt lie, and how snug should it be?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Routing webbing squarely over strong ribcage and collarbone bones keeps slack from letting your torso lunge forward.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: Is it safe to tuck a shoulder belt underneath your arm if it rubs your neck?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Webbing tucked under your armpit crushes fragile ribs and internal organs during crash deceleration.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: May you slip the shoulder strap behind your back while leaving the lap belt clicked?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Putting the upper strap behind you removes upper-body restraint completely, letting your head whip straight into the steering wheel.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: What kind of bodily harm can improper shoulder-belt routing cause in a collision?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Belts only protect when resting on sturdy skeletal points rather than pressing directly into soft tissue.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: After clicking the buckle, where and how should you position the lap belt?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Strong pelvic bones can handle crash loads safely, whereas a high belt across your stomach injures abdominal organs.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: In an older vehicle with an automatic motorized shoulder strap, what must you still buckle manually?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Drivers often forget the manual lap buckle when the upper track slides into place automatically.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: What happens in a crash if you use an automatic shoulder strap without buckling the separate lap belt?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Without a lap belt anchoring your hips, crash forces submarine your body downward under the diagonal strap.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: How should your back and feet be positioned while riding in a moving vehicle?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: Sitting square against the seatback with feet on the floor keeps belts aligned on your hips and chest.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: How does slouching low or propping feet up on the dashboard affect crash protection?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: A deploying passenger airbag folds raised legs violently backward into your face while slouching lets hips submarine.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: Do airbags replace the need to wear your safety belt?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Airbags are engineered assuming a belt holds you back first; hitting an inflating bag unbuckled can be fatal.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: Under which age does the Kansas handbook state children must ride restrained in the rear seat while moving?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Watch the exact age wording because this restraint-law rule specifies below fourteen while airbag guidance highlights twelve and younger.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: Why are airbags officially called supplemental restraints?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Supplemental means added help on top of belts, never standalone crash protection.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: Which parts of your body do airbags specifically help keep from slamming into the cabin interior?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Even when belted, heavy crash forces whip your head and chest forward toward the wheel or dash.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: How does an inflated airbag physics-wise lower the severity of frontal crash injuries?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Catching your upper body across a wide fabric pillow lowers peak pressure compared with hitting narrow rim plastic.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: Why won't an airbag protect you during a second impact in a multi-car pileup?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Vents empty the cushion in fractions of a second after the first hit, leaving only your belt for secondary bounces.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: What two jobs does your safety belt handle that make airbags effective across a whole crash sequence?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Your belt keeps your chest back until the bag finishes inflating and keeps holding you through spinouts or rollovers.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: Which collision angles are front dashboard and steering-wheel airbags built to fire in?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Sensors look for sudden nose-on deceleration where occupants pitch straight toward the steering wheel and windshield.

sec04-card-r18.question_text: Which three crash types are front airbags NOT designed to deploy during?
sec04-card-r18.teaching_text: Because front bags stay tucked away in T-bones, rear-enders, and rollovers, your seat belt remains essential every second.

sec04-card-r19.question_text: Why can touching an airbag while it is still inflating hurt an occupant?
sec04-card-r19.teaching_text: To beat your body forward in milliseconds, the bag bursts out fast enough to injure anyone leaning into its path.

sec04-card-r20.question_text: When a properly seated rider experiences airbag deployment, what minor injuries are most common?
sec04-card-r20.teaching_text: Trading small fabric friction scrapes on your forearms for surviving a high-speed head-on crash is an easy bargain.

sec04-card-r21.question_text: How bad can injuries get if someone sits right up against a deploying airbag?
sec04-card-r21.teaching_text: Taking the full opening force against your head, neck, or sternum inside the first inches can cause fatal trauma.

sec04-card-r22.question_text: At least how many inches should separate the center of your chest from the center of the steering wheel?
sec04-card-r22.teaching_text: Ten inches gives the steering-hub cushion room to open fully into a soft pillow before your torso arrives.

sec04-card-r23.question_text: Where should you look for airbag seat-adjustment rules tailored to your specific vehicle?
sec04-card-r23.teaching_text: Sensor layouts, side curtains, and minimum seating clearances vary across makes and model years.

sec04-card-r24.question_text: Where should the steering-wheel airbag point on your body, and what three adjustments help achieve that?
sec04-card-r24.teaching_text: Raising the seat, adding a firm cushion, or tilting the wheel down aims inflation at sturdy chest bone instead of your chin.

sec04-card-r25.question_text: Where on the steering wheel should your hands stay so a firing airbag will not fling them into your face?
sec04-card-r25.teaching_text: Resting a hand or forearm across the center horn pad turns your own arm into a high-speed club if the bag fires.

sec04-card-r26.question_text: Which cabin seat does the handbook warn against putting a child in, especially when an airbag is present?
sec04-card-r26.teaching_text: Passenger dashboard bags are sized and powered for adult frames, putting smaller riders at severe risk up front.

sec04-card-r27.question_text: Children of what age group should sit in the back seat specifically to prevent airbag injuries?
sec04-card-r27.teaching_text: Memorize twelve and younger for airbag safety questions alongside under fourteen for Kansas's rear-restraint rule.

sec04-card-r28.question_text: What does turning a vehicle's front-passenger airbag switch to the off position do?
sec04-card-r28.teaching_text: Pickup trucks and two-seaters include cutoff switches for rare situations when a small rider has no back seat.

sec04-card-r29.question_text: In a pickup or coupe with no rear seat or a tiny rear seat, how should you use the airbag switch for a child twelve or younger?
sec04-card-r29.teaching_text: Shutting off the right-front airbag removes deployment trauma when lack of a usable back row forces front-seat child travel.

sec04-card-r30.question_text: How do you find out exactly which airbags and cutoff features your car carries?
sec04-card-r30.teaching_text: Modern cars hide knee, curtain, seat-bolster, and smart-weight airbags whose rules appear only in the vehicle manual.

sec04-card-r31.question_text: What happens to a child safety seat's crash protection if it is installed loosely or buckled wrong?
sec04-card-r31.teaching_text: Even a top-rated safety seat cannot protect a child if loose anchors or twisted harness straps let it launch.

sec04-card-r32.question_text: What rear-seat restraint check does the handbook repeat for children aged twelve or younger?
sec04-card-r32.teaching_text: Double-checking buckles and boosters in the back row takes five seconds and prevents quiet mid-drive unbuckling.

sec04-card-r33.question_text: Where must you NEVER place a rear-facing infant child seat?
sec04-card-r33.teaching_text: A rear-facing shell sits inches from the dashboard, so an inflating airbag strikes the back of the baby's head with lethal force.

sec04-card-r34.question_text: Which two instruction books should you combine whenever installing and using a child restraint?
sec04-card-r34.teaching_text: Your car manual shows anchor locations and tether hooks while the seat booklet sets height, weight, and strap slots.

sec04-card-r35.question_text: What airbag control comes standard on most vehicles built with no rear seat or only a tiny rear seat?
sec04-card-r35.teaching_text: Manufacturers build manual or key-operated passenger switches into two-seat pickups and sports cars lacking full rear seats.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: Where should you look to confirm the exact engine-starting steps for your specific vehicle?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Push-button hybrids, diesels, and keyed ignitions each use distinct startup sequences detailed in the owner's manual.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: What brake should already be engaged before you start the engine?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Keeping the parking brake set ensures the car stays anchored even on sloped driveways during startup.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: Where should your right foot rest before starting an automatic-transmission car?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Modern automatics require brake pressure to crank and holding the pedal prevents any sudden lurch.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: Which gear-selector position should you verify before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Starting only in park locks the transmission output shaft so the car cannot creep unexpectedly.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: What must your left foot do before cranking a manual-transmission vehicle?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Flooring the clutch disconnects the engine from the gearbox so starter torque never jerks the car forward.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: Which gearshift position should you set before starting a manual-transmission vehicle?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Starting in neutral backs up your foot on the clutch so an accidental slip will not lunge into a wall.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: On a keyed ignition, which position do you turn the key to first before checking dash lights and gauges?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Stopping briefly at the on detent powers up fuel pumps and illuminates warning bulbs so you spot faults early.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: What should you scan on the dashboard before twisting a keyed ignition from on to start?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Confirming oil, battery, brake, and fuel readings work before cranking catches dead warning bulbs and low fuel.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: Which exterior lights does the Kansas startup routine instruct you to turn on right after starting?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Daytime low beams make your approaching car stand out against shaded streets and prairie horizons.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: What quick security step follows turning on low beams in the handbook's startup sequence?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Securing cabin latches before rolling keeps doors shut in side impacts and protects occupants at intersections.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: In an automatic car, what two brake steps come right before shifting the selector into drive?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Holding the foot brake stops lurching into drive while releasing the parking brake prevents dragging rear shoes.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: How do you shift a running manual-transmission car from neutral to get ready to pull forward?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: First gear delivers the leverage needed to get a stationary car rolling smoothly without lugging the engine.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: In a manual car ready to depart, what pedal must you hold down before releasing the parking brake?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: With the clutch floored the car freewheels freely, so your right foot must hold the service brake on slopes.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: What forward check must you make right before rolling away from a curb or parking spot?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Pedestrians, pets, or another car pulling out ahead can step into your lane while you were shifting gears.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: Besides looking ahead, which two traffic zones must you check before pulling away?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Combining mirror checks with a shoulder glance catches cyclists and fast-closing cars in your blind spot.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: What communication step and safety rule apply whenever pulling out into traffic from a stop?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Blinking before your wheels move warns approaching drivers early, though you still wait for a clean gap.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: How hard should you press the gas pedal when pulling away from a stop?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Progressive throttle keeps tires hooked up smoothly and gives you instant margin if someone brakes ahead.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: How should you bring the clutch pedal up when pulling away in a manual-transmission car?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Easing smoothly through the friction bite point transfers engine torque cleanly without bucking or stalling.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: What sudden vehicle motion can happen if you pop the clutch pedal up abruptly?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: A sudden forward lunge in a tight parking row or crosswalk can bump the car or pedestrian ahead.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: Besides jerking forward, what engine problem can abrupt clutch release cause?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Killing the engine mid-intersection leaves you stranded across cross-traffic while following cars close in.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: Which part of your foot presses the accelerator, and where should your heel stay?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Pivoting off an anchored heel lets your ankle meter tiny throttle changes instead of stomping with your whole leg.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: What tire problem does stomping the gas too hard cause, especially on slick pavement?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Overpowering wet or icy pavement breaks tire grip immediately so wheels churn in place instead of pulling cleanly.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: What happens to vehicle stability once hard acceleration sets the drive wheels spinning?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: A spinning tire loses sideways grip too, letting road crown or curves swing your car sideways.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: How should you build speed when rain, snow, sand, or loose gravel cuts tire grip?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Feathering the gas gently keeps torque below the slip threshold on wet paint, slush, or rural gravel.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: What chain reaction follows applying too much engine power when traction is poor?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Once drive wheels break loose at speed, fishtailing or plowing wide into another lane happens in a heartbeat.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: What is your immediate foot correction if your drive wheels start spinning?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Backing off the throttle lets tire tread slow back down to road speed and bite the pavement again.

sec05-card-f27.question_text: What visual check should you make whenever slowing to stop an automatic-transmission vehicle?
sec05-card-f27.teaching_text: Knowing how close the driver behind you is lets you brake earlier and smoother to prevent a rear-end hit.

sec05-card-f28.question_text: Before steering over to stop along a curb, what look and communication steps are required?
sec05-card-f28.teaching_text: Cyclists and Curb-side delivery scooters often ride inside your right blind spot right beside the gutter.

sec05-card-f29.question_text: Where do you bring your front bumper to a halt at a stop sign or red traffic signal?
sec05-card-f29.teaching_text: Stopping short of painted stop bars and crosswalks keeps pedestrian paths open and clears turning truck trailers.

sec05-card-f30.question_text: How do you begin slowing the vehicle smoothly at the start of a normal stop?
sec05-card-f30.teaching_text: Letting off the accelerator early bleeds speed gently before your foot ever squeezes the brake pedal.

sec05-card-f31.question_text: How should you press the brake pedal to bring the car to a smooth, controlled stop?
sec05-card-f31.teaching_text: Progressive squeezing instead of late stabbing keeps tires from skidding and stops passengers from pitching forward.

sec05-card-f32.question_text: In a manual-transmission vehicle, what clutch and gear steps finish a complete stop when preparing to go again?
sec05-card-f32.teaching_text: Pushing the clutch in prevents stalling as RPMs drop, and slotting first gear readies you for green.

sec05-card-f33.question_text: Whether rolling forward or backing up, which way do you turn the steering wheel?
sec05-card-f33.teaching_text: Turning the top of the wheel right moves the nose right going forward and swings the tail right in reverse.

sec05-card-f34.question_text: Where on the steering wheel should your two hands rest during normal driving?
sec05-card-f34.teaching_text: Balanced hands on opposite outside edges give instant leverage left or right while staying clear of the airbag.

sec05-card-f35.question_text: How tightly should you hold the steering wheel?
sec05-card-f35.teaching_text: White-knuckle squeezing tires out your forearms and blocks subtle road feedback through the tires.

sec05-card-f36.question_text: Should you wrap your fingers around the steering wheel or steer with your palms?
sec05-card-f36.teaching_text: Palming a turn can slip off smooth leather or plastic mid-corner right when a pothole kicks the wheel.

sec05-card-f37.question_text: How should your thumbs rest while holding the steering wheel?
sec05-card-f37.teaching_text: Resting thumbs lightly along the rim face prevents spoke kickback or airbag blast from spraining hooked thumbs.

sec05-card-f38.question_text: Why must you never steer by grabbing the inside of the steering wheel rim?
sec05-card-f38.teaching_text: Reaching inside the spokes traps your wrists in the airbag zone and tangles your arm if a tire hits a curb.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: How many distinct steering techniques does the Kansas handbook teach for different driving situations?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Highway cruising, tight parking-lot turns, sudden obstacle dodges, and backing each call for tailored handwork.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: What is the other common name for hand-to-hand steering?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Test questions swap both terms interchangeably because one hand pushes the rim up while the other pulls down.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: At which clock numbers does your left hand start for hand-to-hand push-pull steering?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Starting low between seven and eight o'clock relaxes your left shoulder and keeps your forearm clear of the airbag.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: At which clock numbers does your right hand start for hand-to-hand push-pull steering?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Pairing four-to-five on the right with seven-to-eight on the left anchors balanced low-wheel control.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: How do your two hands work together on the rim during a hand-to-hand turn?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Alternating upward pushes and downward pulls keeps at least one firm hand steering the rim continuously.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: In push-pull steering, what does the pushing hand do while the opposite hand pulls downward?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Letting the resting hand glide down the rim mirrors the pulling hand so your arms stay symmetrical.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: How do you straighten the front wheels back onto your path after a hand-to-hand turn?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Feeding the wheel back hand-to-hand instead of letting it spin loose prevents jerky lane overshoot.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: What arm position hazard does hand-to-hand steering prevent across the face of the wheel?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Keeping each hand on its own half of the rim guarantees nothing blocks the center airbag cover.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: Why does keeping your arms from crossing the steering wheel matter so much in airbag-equipped cars?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: If a frontal crash fires the bag while an arm crosses the hub, the bag slams your own wrist into your face.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: Which steering method does the Kansas handbook name as its preferred everyday technique?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Push-pull combines smooth lane tracking with top-tier airbag safety, making it the textbook gold standard.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: Why does the Kansas handbook warn against the old ten-and-two hand position?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: High hands at ten and two sit right where inflating airbags burst outward, risking hand, wrist, and facial fractures.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: For which low-speed maneuvers is hand-over-hand steering recommended?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Tight parking stalls and sharp city corners demand rapid full-lock wheel rotation at walking speeds where airbag risk is low.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: Where on the clock face does your left hand start for hand-over-hand steering?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Starting slightly higher at eight-to-nine gives leverage to push across the top arc during sharp low-speed turns.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: Where on the clock face does your right hand start for hand-over-hand steering?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Notice the clock shift for exam day, using eight-nine and three-four for hand-over-hand versus seven-eight and four-five for push-pull.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: Which section of the steering wheel do your hands work through during a hand-over-hand right turn?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Reaching over to grab and pull inside the upper-right third turns the front wheels briskly to the right.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: Which section of the steering wheel do your hands work through during a hand-over-hand left turn?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Matching the active upper third to your turn direction keeps rapid low-speed hand crossovers consistent.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: How do you keep sharpening a tight turn once you finish one hand-over-hand crossover?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Deep ninety-degree corners or parking bays often take more than one crossover to reach full steering angle.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: After finishing a sharp turn with hand-over-hand steering, how do you bring the car straight?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Walking the wheel back deliberately keeps full steering authority instead of letting caster snap the rim wildly.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: When anti-lock brakes are pulsing hard and you steer around a hazard, why might you need to limit your wheel turn?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Because anti-lock braking preserves front-tire steering bite, cranking the wheel hard flings you straight into neighboring lanes.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: If your tires drop off the pavement edge, why must you keep your return steering input small?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Yanking hard left against a pavement lip slingshots the car across the center line once tires catch asphalt.

sec05-card-r21.question_text: How does highway speed change how much steering wheel turn it takes to shift one lane sideways?
sec05-card-r21.teaching_text: A gentle wrist nudge at seventy miles per hour moves a car sideways faster than a big crank in town.

sec05-card-r22.question_text: Roughly how many degrees of steering-wheel turn does the handbook give for guiding a modern car back onto the road?
sec05-card-r22.teaching_text: A eighth-to-quarter turn climbs a shoulder edge cleanly without whipping the front end toward oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-r23.question_text: During an emergency roadway swerve, what maximum steering-wheel turn angle does the Kansas handbook set?
sec05-card-r23.teaching_text: Half a turn of the wheel with both hands still attached gives maximum evasive bite without tangling your arms.

sec05-card-r24.question_text: What happens to tire grip if you crank past one hundred eighty degrees during a highway swerve?
sec05-card-r24.teaching_text: Turning front tires sideways past their slip limit makes them plow and scrub instead of carving cleanly.

sec05-card-r25.question_text: Where can excessive steering input during an emergency dodge send your vehicle?
sec05-card-r25.teaching_text: Turning a rear-end scare into a head-on collision across the center line makes over-correcting deadly.

sec05-card-r26.question_text: In which two brief situations is steering with just one hand acceptable?
sec05-card-r26.teaching_text: Cruising down the road one-handed cuts emergency reaction leverage, so save single-hand grip strictly for reversing or quick switch reaches.

sec05-card-r27.question_text: When one hand briefly reaches for wipers or climate controls, where must your steering hand stay?
sec05-card-r27.teaching_text: Holding your normal side grip prevents pulling the wheel sideways as your body reaches toward the dash.

sec05-card-r28.question_text: During a brief reach for a dash control, at which clock positions should your remaining wheel hand hold?
sec05-card-r28.teaching_text: Side-balance positions at eight-to-nine or three-to-four hold the car straight far steadier than dangling a hand on the bottom.

sec05-card-r29.question_text: When is gripping the steering wheel at twelve o'clock actually recommended?
sec05-card-r29.teaching_text: Twisting in your seat to look out the rear glass aligns your shoulder naturally with twelve o'clock at walking speed.

sec05-card-r30.question_text: Why does the handbook advise minimizing how often you back up?
sec05-card-r30.teaching_text: Pillars, headrests, and trunk height create blind zones behind every vehicle where low hazards disappear.

sec05-card-r31.question_text: How can choosing a drive-through parking stall make leaving a lot safer?
sec05-card-r31.teaching_text: Driving forward out of a stall gives you panoramic windshield sight of shopping carts, kids, and cross-aisle cars.

sec05-card-r32.question_text: What should you check behind your parked vehicle BEFORE climbing into the driver's seat?
sec05-card-r32.teaching_text: Toys, pets, and toddlers below trunk height never show up through a rear window once you sit inside.

sec05-card-r33.question_text: What must your foot hold down while moving the gear selector into reverse?
sec05-card-r33.teaching_text: Clamping the brake keeps the car stationary while reverse gear engages and flashes white backup lights to warn walkers.

sec05-card-r34.question_text: In the handbook's straight backing setup, which hand holds the wheel and at what clock number?
sec05-card-r34.teaching_text: Anchoring your left hand at top center frees your torso to rotate right toward the rear window.

sec05-card-r35.question_text: Where do your right arm and eyes go during the handbook's standard backing posture?
sec05-card-r35.teaching_text: Draping your right arm across the passenger headrest pivots your shoulders so you look directly through the back glass.

sec05-card-r36.question_text: What blind-spot warning does the handbook attach to using rearview and side mirrors while backing?
sec05-card-r36.teaching_text: Use mirrors only as quick side helpers while keeping your main gaze out the rear window.

sec05-card-r37.question_text: How fast should you reverse, and how should you use the gas pedal?
sec05-card-r37.teaching_text: Walking pace gives pedestrians time to step clear and stops you within inches when you tap the brake.

sec05-card-r38.question_text: Is a vehicle easier or harder to steer accurately when traveling in reverse?
sec05-card-r38.teaching_text: Because the turning front tires trail behind your direction of travel, small wheel movements swing the car sharper than expected.

sec05-card-r39.question_text: How big should your steering adjustments be when backing, and which way do you turn the wheel?
sec05-card-r39.teaching_text: Nudging the top of the wheel gently left swings the rear bumper left smoothly without wild fishtailing.

sec05-card-r40.question_text: While backing around a turn, where else must you glance besides straight back?
sec05-card-r40.teaching_text: As the tail swings into an aisle, your front fenders swing outward toward parked cars beside you.

sec05-card-r41.question_text: How long must you keep looking backward during a backing maneuver?
sec05-card-r41.teaching_text: Spinning forward to grab the shifter while still rolling backward causes low-speed parking-lot bumps.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: Do right-of-way rules grant you an absolute right to plow ahead, or do they define who must yield?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn when another driver makes a mistake causes preventable T-bone crashes.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: What is every driver's overriding duty toward pedestrians, other vehicles, and property even when someone else fails to yield?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Kansas law expects you to brake or steer out of harm's way rather than stand on technical priority.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: What must you do at an intersection if a pedestrian steps out against the signal or crosses unlawfully?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Two tons of steel against a human body leaves zero excuse for failing to stop for an off-rule walker.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Who holds priority whenever your car crosses a sidewalk into or out of a driveway, alley, or parking lot?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Sidewalks belong to foot traffic first, so pause before rolling across concrete aprons into busy lots.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: When is a motor vehicle ever allowed to touch a public sidewalk?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Shortcutting along a sidewalk to dodge a backed-up turn lane is illegal and endangers everyone on foot.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: How must you respond to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, and why shouldn't you honk?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Blasting a horn startles a working guide dog and scrambles the sound cues a blind pedestrian relies on.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: Which two oncoming movements must a left-turning driver yield to at an intersection?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Watch oncoming right-turning cars closely because both of you may be aiming for the exact same cross-street lane.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: At an unmarked, unsigned intersection, which two groups of vehicles must you yield to?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Residential corners without signs rely on yielding to anyone already in the box and ties going to your right.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and how do two drivers break a tie if they stop at the same instant?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Making eye contact and letting the car to your right roll first solves simultaneous four-way stops cleanly.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle pulls onto a main street from a driveway, alley, or shoulder?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Through traffic moves much faster than a car launching from rest, so wait for a wide, unhurried gap.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: Where must you wait if backed-up traffic ahead leaves no room to clear an intersection?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Pulling into the box on green and getting trapped when the light changes gridlocks every cross-street lane.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: Which three groups of authorized people on foot must drivers obey when they direct traffic?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Live directions from officers, highway workers, and school crossing guards override normal signal rhythms to protect people.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: From top to bottom, how are the three colors arranged on a standard vertical traffic signal?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Fixed bulb positions let color-vision-deficient drivers and glare-struck eyes read any vertical light instantly.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: From left to right, how are the colors arranged on a standard horizontal traffic signal?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Low overpasses and windy plains often mount signals sideways, keeping red leftmost where drivers scan first.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: What two conditions still govern your movement even when facing a steady green traffic light?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Green never erases your duty to yield to pedestrians or oncoming cars when turning.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: Right when your red light flips to green, who must you allow to finish first?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Giving cars and walkers already mid-crossing a moment to clear prevents broadside collisions.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Who holds priority over you when turning left on a standard circular green light?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: A plain green ball gives zero left-turn protection, so oncoming traffic and crosswalk walkers go first.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: Even with a green directional arrow illuminated, when may you actually make that movement?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Emergency vehicles, slow pedestrians, or late runners can still occupy the lane your green arrow points into.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Which cross-street drivers should you still watch out for while turning on a protected green arrow?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Drivers turning right on red from the cross street often misjudge or overlook oncoming green-arrow left turners.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: What posted signs and foot traffic must you still respect during a green-arrow phase?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Time-of-day turn restrictions and pedestrians beside your fender still take precedence over rushing a turn.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: What does a steady yellow light warn, and how does traffic behind you factor into stopping?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Checking your mirror ensures a tailgating truck will not slam into you as you brake smoothly to a stop.
sec06-card-f21.must_match_memory_hook: Red coming, stop safely checking rear

visual_sync.text_span: Red coming, stop safely checking rear

sec06-card-f22.question_text: What should you do if the traffic signal turns yellow after you are already inside the intersection?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Panic-stopping or reversing inside the box leaves you stranded across cross-traffic lanes.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: Which three actions should you take when approaching a flashing yellow signal?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Flashing yellow marks high-conflict side streets or firehouses where cross-traffic may pull out unexpectedly.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: What phase is ending when a yellow arrow lights up, and who must you prepare to yield to?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Once protected green arrow time runs out, oncoming straight traffic and crosswalk walkers regain priority.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: Where do you stop for a steady red light, and when may you move before green?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Stopping behind the bar or crosswalk protects pedestrians before you even consider an allowed turn on red.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: What stop and scan steps are mandatory before a right turn on red, and what blocks it completely?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Every right on red starts with dead-stopped wheels, clear pedestrians and cars, and zero prohibiting signs.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: How do you handle an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic light?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Treat flashing red identically to an octagonal stop sign by halting behind the line, looking both ways, and yielding.

sec06-card-f28.question_text: Until what signal change does a steady red arrow forbid moving in its pointed direction?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: Never treat a red arrow like a circular red right-turn option; hold still until a green signal permits.

sec06-card-f29.question_text: Which four visual design features help traffic signs communicate rules, hazards, directions, and services?
sec06-card-f29.teaching_text: Even in heavy rain or fog, sign outlines and background colors tell you the message category immediately.

sec06-card-f30.question_text: What should you do whenever a roadside warning sign alerts you to a possible hazard ahead?
sec06-card-f30.teaching_text: Shedding speed before reaching a hidden curve, merge, or crossing buys critical reaction space.

sec06-card-f31.question_text: What shape, background color, and print color do general road warning signs use?
sec06-card-f31.teaching_text: Yellow diamond panels stand out sharply against green trees and gray pavement in every season.

sec06-card-f32.question_text: Which three pedestrian-heavy warning areas often use bright fluorescent yellow signs?
sec06-card-f32.teaching_text: High-visibility fluorescent yellow-green catches peripheral vision fast at dawn and dusk around children and crosswalks.

sec06-card-f33.question_text: What upcoming feature does a round yellow sign marked with a black X and the letters RR announce?
sec06-card-f33.teaching_text: Only railroad advance warnings use a yellow circle, giving you an unmistakable heads-up before tracks appear.

sec06-card-f34.question_text: What four habits should kick in as soon as you pass a railroad advance-warning sign?
sec06-card-f34.teaching_text: Quiet cabin stereos and lower approach speed let you spot or hear a locomotive even if lights fail.

sec06-card-f35.question_text: What does the white X-shaped crossbuck sign mark right at the tracks, and what must you do if a train approaches?
sec06-card-f35.teaching_text: Treat a white crossbuck just like a yield sign positioned right before the rails.

sec06-card-f36.question_text: Where must your vehicle stay while waiting at a railroad crossing?
sec06-card-f36.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang wider than the steel rails on both sides, so crowding past the stop bar invites disaster.

sec06-card-f37.question_text: Why must you scan for extra tracks and another train every time, even if no track-count plaque is posted?
sec06-card-f37.teaching_text: Pulling out right behind a caboose can put you straight into a second train hidden on parallel rails.

sec06-card-f38.question_text: What do alternating flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean, and where must you stop?
sec06-card-f38.teaching_text: Never try to zig-zag around lowering gates or beat alternating red beacons across the rails.

sec06-card-f39.question_text: May you drive across railroad tracks while the crossing warning bell or train horn is sounding?
sec06-card-f39.teaching_text: Audible bells and locomotive horns mean a train occupies the approach circuit even before you spot its headlight.

sec06-card-f40.question_text: Why should you expect a train at any railroad crossing even if you have never seen one there before?
sec06-card-f40.teaching_text: Freight, maintenance, and detour trains roll through at any hour of day or night regardless of habit.

sec06-card-f41.question_text: Which three physical factors prevent a train from stopping quickly for a car on the tracks?
sec06-card-f41.teaching_text: Thousands of tons rolling on steel wheels carry momentum that no engineer can halt like a car.

sec06-card-f42.question_text: How far can a hundred-car freight train traveling fifty-five miles per hour take to stop under emergency braking?
sec06-card-f42.teaching_text: By the time a locomotive crew sees a car on the crossing, the train often needs eighteen football fields to stop.

sec06-card-f43.question_text: How should you scan and move once you begin driving across railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f43.teaching_text: Never dawdle or pause on the timber planks where traffic ahead could pin your rear bumper over the rail.

sec06-card-f44.question_text: When must you wait behind the railroad tracks even if no gates or red lights are active?
sec06-card-f44.teaching_text: Stopping in a red-light queue with your tail hanging across railroad tracks is a classic fatal trap.

sec06-card-f45.question_text: Between motor vehicles and trains or rail maintenance vehicles, who always holds the right-of-way?
sec06-card-f45.teaching_text: Rail equipment cannot swerve an inch and outweighs passenger cars by thousands of times.

sec06-card-f46.question_text: Why must you avoid shifting gears while your vehicle is crossing railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f46.teaching_text: Missing a gear or stalling mid-shift leaves your car dead right across active train rails.

sec06-card-f47.question_text: What is your number-one immediate priority if your vehicle stalls on railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f47.teaching_text: Cars can be replaced by insurance, so get every passenger unbuckled and clear before worrying about anything else.

sec06-card-f48.question_text: If a train is bearing down on your stalled car, in which direction should you run away from the tracks, and why?
sec06-card-f48.teaching_text: Impact hurls shattered car wreckage forward in the train's travel direction, so angling away toward the oncoming locomotive keeps you behind debris.

sec06-card-f49.question_text: Who should you notify once everyone is safely out of a vehicle stalled on railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f49.teaching_text: Alerting dispatchers and railroad emergency lines right away gives crews a chance to warn approaching trains.

sec06-card-f50.question_text: Why do drivers often misjudge whether they can beat an approaching train?
sec06-card-f50.teaching_text: Large objects framed by parallel rails create an optical illusion that makes sixty miles per hour look like a crawl.

sec06-card-f51.question_text: What color sign sits on or near the crossbuck at every railroad crossing for reporting emergencies?
sec06-card-f51.teaching_text: Spotting that blue plaque gives you a direct hotline to the exact railroad operating those rails.

sec06-card-f52.question_text: Which two crucial numbers are printed on a blue railroad Emergency Notification System sign?
sec06-card-f52.teaching_text: One number connects straight to the railroad desk while the federal crossing ID pinpoints your exact intersection.

sec06-card-f53.question_text: How does the crossing-location ID on the blue ENS sign help when you call the railroad dispatcher?
sec06-card-f53.teaching_text: Rural county roads may lack street signs, whereas the six-digit-and-letter ID tells dispatchers which milepost to halt.

sec06-card-f54.question_text: When is railroad Emergency Notification System reporting staffed and available?
sec06-card-f54.teaching_text: Freight corridors run nonstop on holidays and midnight shifts, so railroad emergency desks answer every hour.

sec06-card-f55.question_text: Which four track emergencies or hazards can you report using the blue ENS sign number?
sec06-card-f55.teaching_text: Reporting stuck crossing arms or blocked rails before a train arrives prevents catastrophic derailments.

sec06-card-f56.question_text: What background color, print color, and two shapes identify standard highway work-zone signs?
sec06-card-f56.teaching_text: Switching from everyday yellow to bright construction orange signals temporary crew activity immediately.

sec06-card-f57.question_text: Which five temporary conditions can orange work-zone signs warn you about ahead?
sec06-card-f57.teaching_text: Scanning orange legends early prepares you for milled asphalt drops, slow loaders, and narrowed speed chutes.

sec06-card-f58.question_text: How must you respond to a work-zone flagger's signals?
sec06-card-f58.teaching_text: Flaggers coordinate blind single-lane work zones where ignoring a paddle causes head-on collisions or worker strikes.

sec06-card-f59.question_text: What job do orange drums, cones, tubes, panels, and barriers perform inside a work zone?
sec06-card-f59.teaching_text: Channeling markers trace temporary lane edges around open trenches, wet concrete, and roadside workers.

sec06-card-f60.question_text: Where must you stop when portable temporary traffic signals control a work zone and a white stop line is painted?
sec06-card-f60.teaching_text: Pulling past a portable signal's stop bar blocks wide dump trucks or opposing single-lane traffic.

sec06-card-f61.question_text: Which three defensive habits keep you out of crashes inside a work zone?
sec06-card-f61.teaching_text: Extra following gap and lower speed prevent chain-reaction rear-enders when construction queues brake suddenly.

sec06-card-f62.question_text: What happens to speeding fines inside Kansas highway work zones?
sec06-card-f62.teaching_text: Doubling speeding penalties backs up orange speed plaques to shield vulnerable crews working inches from traffic.

sec06-card-f63.question_text: Which four everyday traffic laws do regulatory signs state and enforce?
sec06-card-f63.teaching_text: Regulatory signs post binding traffic laws rather than optional advice, so missing one invites a citation.

sec06-card-f64.question_text: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash drawn over a symbol on a regulatory sign mean?
sec06-card-f64.teaching_text: Universal no-symbol graphics let drivers recognize banned U-turns, left turns, or trucks without reading fine print.

sec06-card-f65.question_text: What conditions do posted maximum speed signs assume, and when must you drive slower than posted?
sec06-card-f65.teaching_text: Heavy traffic, rain, ice, or fog stretches stopping distance well past what dry-pavement speed signs assume.

sec06-card-f66.question_text: When a high-speed highway posts both maximum and minimum speed limits, what takes priority during bad weather?
sec06-card-f66.teaching_text: Minimum speed signs stop dry-day crawlers, yet severe storms or ice still require slowing to a safe pace.

sec06-card-f67.question_text: When does a school-zone speed sign marked 'when flashing' enforce its lower limit, and what applies when dark?
sec06-card-f67.teaching_text: Paying sharp attention to yellow beacons keeps kids safe at arrival and dismissal without guessing off-hours.

sec06-card-f68.question_text: How do lane-use control signs look and where are they mounted?
sec06-card-f68.teaching_text: Overhead and curb-mounted arrow panels work alongside painted lane arrows so snow or traffic never hides turn-only bays.

sec06-card-f69.question_text: What shape, background color, and letter color identify a standard stop sign?
