sec06-card-f69.teaching_text: Reserving the eight-sided outline exclusively for stop signs lets you spot cross-street priority from the back too.

sec06-card-f70.question_text: Where do you halt at a stop sign, and what checks come before pulling out?
sec06-card-f70.teaching_text: Halting behind the painted line or crosswalk keeps walkers safe while you scan left, front, right, and left again.

sec06-card-f71.question_text: What does an ALL WAY or numbered-way plaque mounted beneath a stop sign tell you?
sec06-card-f71.teaching_text: Never assume cross-traffic has a stop sign unless an ALL WAY or four-way tab confirms it.

sec06-card-f72.question_text: Which way does a standard yield triangle point, and what colors does it use?
sec06-card-f72.teaching_text: The inverted downward-pointing triangle is unique on American roads so drivers recognize a yield even covered in slush.

sec06-card-f73.question_text: How must you approach and enter an intersection controlled by a yield sign?
sec06-card-f73.teaching_text: Approaching slowly lets you merge smoothly when clear or stop cleanly without skidding if cross-traffic appears.

sec06-card-f74.question_text: What movement is a shared center turn lane built for, and which two misuses are illegal?
sec06-card-f74.teaching_text: Using a two-way center lane to overtake traffic or cruise down the block sets up head-on collisions.

sec06-card-f75.question_text: Which turning directions does a No Turn On Red sign block until the signal turns green?
sec06-card-f75.teaching_text: Even on one-way-to-one-way corners that sometimes allow left on red, this sign locks down every red-phase turn.

sec06-card-f76.question_text: What does a Stop Here On Red sign tell you at an intersection or railroad approach?
sec06-card-f76.teaching_text: Engineers set stop lines back where wide semi-trailers need swing room or induction loops detect waiting cars.

sec06-card-f77.question_text: When must you hold back before entering an intersection posted Do Not Block Intersection?
sec06-card-f77.teaching_text: Fire stations, rail crossings, and hospital drives post these signs so stopped queues never trap emergency rigs.

sec06-card-f78.question_text: What does a Left Turn Yield On Green sign remind drivers sitting in a left-turn lane?
sec06-card-f78.teaching_text: When no green arrow is lit, you must wait for a safe gap in opposing traffic before turning across.

sec06-card-f79.question_text: How must traffic move on a street posted with One Way arrow signs?
sec06-card-f79.teaching_text: Checking one-way arrows before turning off a two-way street stops wrong-way downtown entries before they happen.

sec06-card-f80.question_text: What does a Do Not Pass sign prohibit, and why are those zones placed there?
sec06-card-f80.teaching_text: Hills, curves, intersections, and pedestrian entries hide oncoming vehicles until it is too late to tuck back in.

sec06-card-f81.question_text: What zone ends at a Pass With Care sign, and does it guarantee the road ahead is clear?
sec06-card-f81.teaching_text: Passing becomes legal again past the sign only if you confirm long sightlines and zero oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-f82.question_text: Where does a Keep Right sign direct your vehicle to pass?
sec06-card-f82.teaching_text: Divided medians, bridge piers, and turn islands place Keep Right plaques at their nose to prevent wrong-way entries.

sec06-card-f83.question_text: On a multilane highway, who must move into the right lane at a Slower Traffic Keep Right sign?
sec06-card-f83.teaching_text: Camping below traffic flow in left lanes forces faster drivers to weave and pass on the right.

sec06-card-f84.question_text: What shape, colors, and center bar make up a Do Not Enter sign, and what does it forbid?
sec06-card-f84.teaching_text: Mounted at freeway off-ramps and one-way exits, that bold red circle and horizontal bar scream stop immediately.
sec06-card-f84.must_match_memory_hook: Red circle, white bar blocks entry

visual_sync.text_span: Red circle, white bar blocks entry

sec06-card-f85.question_text: What urgent mistake does a rectangular red Wrong Way sign warn a driver is happening right now?
sec06-card-f85.teaching_text: If you ever see Wrong Way facing your windshield, pull to the edge, stop safely, and turn around.

sec06-card-f86.question_text: Which three background colors and two shapes do highway guide signs use for directions, places, and services?
sec06-card-f86.teaching_text: Color-coding green routes, brown parks, and blue services lets highway drivers filter sign boards at a glance.

sec06-card-f87.question_text: Which two background colors with white print post upcoming destinations, directions, and mileages?
sec06-card-f87.teaching_text: Green boards guide you to cities and exits while brown boards point toward parks, historic sites, and lakes.

sec06-card-f88.question_text: How does the position of the small EXIT tab at the top of an overhead highway guide sign help you pick lanes?
sec06-card-f88.teaching_text: An EXIT plaque tucked on the top-left corner warns early that your ramp peels off from the left lane.

sec06-card-f89.question_text: What colors do motorist service signs use, and which four facilities are classic examples?
sec06-card-f89.teaching_text: Spotting blue hospital or fuel panels ahead lets you exit calmly without last-second lane dives.

sec06-card-f90.question_text: What do distinct route-marker shield shapes and colors identify, and how should you navigate unfamiliar highways?
sec06-card-f90.teaching_text: Distinguishing interstate shields from US and Kansas state markers keeps you on route without staring at a phone.

sec06-card-f100.question_text: What lane-change rule applies alongside a single solid white line between same-direction lanes?
sec06-card-f100.teaching_text: Solid white stripes mark weaving hotspots like tunnels and intersection approaches where casual lane swaps cause sideswipes.

sec06-card-f101.question_text: Which four roadway spots commonly use solid white pavement markings?
sec06-card-f101.teaching_text: Right-edge fog lines keep you on asphalt in dark rain while solid white turn-bay lines organize intersections.

sec06-card-f102.question_text: What does a large white arrow painted directly on your travel lane tell you?
sec06-card-f102.teaching_text: Once you enter a lane stamped with a curved turn-only arrow, going straight cuts off turning neighbors.

sec06-card-f91.question_text: What color combination marks temporary incident-management signs for crashes, floods, or unplanned closures?
sec06-card-f91.teaching_text: Coral-pink boards stand out from planned orange construction so drivers expect sudden emergency detours or responders ahead.

sec06-card-f92.question_text: Which four essential traffic rules and zones do painted pavement markings map out on the asphalt?
sec06-card-f92.teaching_text: Roadway paint works right in your line of sight so you never have to hunt for curb signs.

sec06-card-f93.question_text: What traffic flow direction does a yellow center line always tell you is on the other side of it?
sec06-card-f93.teaching_text: Remembering yellow means two-way traffic stops you from pulling into an oncoming left lane after turning.

sec06-card-f94.question_text: When does a single broken yellow center line allow you to pass a slower vehicle?
sec06-card-f94.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint marks sightline eligibility, never a promise that the oncoming lane is empty right now.

sec06-card-f95.question_text: When one solid yellow line pairs with one broken yellow line, which side may pass and which side cannot?
sec06-card-f95.teaching_text: Read whichever stripe sits closest to your left tires; solid means blind sightline ahead for your direction.

sec06-card-f96.question_text: Who is allowed to pass slower traffic across double solid yellow center lines?
sec06-card-f96.teaching_text: Double yellow stripes lock down overtaking for both directions around hills, curves, and busy driveway corridors.

sec06-card-f97.question_text: Even where passing is barred, when does the Kansas handbook permit crossing a solid yellow line?
sec06-card-f97.teaching_text: Drivers still need to turn left into homes and businesses when oncoming traffic offers a safe gap.

sec06-card-f98.question_text: What does white lane striping between travel lanes tell you about traffic direction?
sec06-card-f98.teaching_text: Seeing white dashes on both sides of your car confirms you are on a multilane road or one-way street.

sec06-card-f99.question_text: When may you change lanes across a broken white line?
sec06-card-f99.teaching_text: Dashed white lines permit smooth lane changes once mirrors, blind-spot checks, and turn signals confirm space.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: Where must you bring your front bumper to a halt when a stop is required, including corners without painted crosswalks?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Following that three-step order keeps your nose clear of stop bars, unmarked walkways, and cross-street lanes.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: What are crosswalks reserved for, and when must drivers yield there?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Yielding starts the moment a pedestrian steps into the crosswalk, never waiting until they walk in front of your hood.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: Do crosswalks exist only where white stripes are painted on the asphalt?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Every street corner connects sidewalks invisibly, so scan for pedestrians even on plain neighborhood asphalt.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: Where do you make your first stop when a white stop line is painted ahead of a crosswalk?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Halting at the advance bar keeps a safety buffer between your bumper and people walking across.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: Where must you stop first when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or parking garage across a sidewalk?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Building walls hide joggers and strollers until your nose reaches the sidewalk edge, so stop before crossing concrete.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: Which maneuver is a shared center left-turn lane built for, and what two uses are off-limits?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Treating the center turn bay like a third travel or passing lane invites head-on crashes with opposing turners.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: Why shouldn't you merge into a shared center left-turn lane way ahead of your turn?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Cruising down the shared center bay multiplies the odds of meeting an oncoming car pulling in from the opposite direction.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: Which three visual checks plus signal come right before steering smoothly into a shared left-turn lane?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Scanning ahead catches oncoming cars already claiming the bay while your left shoulder glance spots passing traffic.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: While waiting inside a shared left-turn lane, which traffic streams must you watch before turning?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Cars nosing out of side lots can cross into the center bay right while you watch oncoming lanes.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: How does a reversible lane work, and what must you verify before steering into it?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Morning inbound lanes flip outbound in the afternoon, so entering from memory instead of reading signals risks a head-on crash.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: Which special yellow pavement stripes and overhead equipment mark a reversible lane?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Twin dashed yellow lines on both edges tell you immediately that overhead X-and-arrow gantries govern flow.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: On overhead lane-control signals, what does a downward green arrow allow and what does a red X forbid?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Never drive beneath a lit red X because oncoming rush-hour traffic likely holds the green arrow from the other end.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: What special lane use does an overhead flashing yellow X allow?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Distinguish flashing from steady on the test because a flashing yellow X marks a shared left-turn-only bay.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: What does an overhead steady yellow X warn is about to happen, and what must you do?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Steady yellow X warns that a red X and opposing flow are moments away, so merge out promptly.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: Even when your reversible lane shows a green arrow, what driver mistake ahead should you stay alert for?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Unfamiliar visitors sometimes misread double-broken yellow lines and pull head-on into an active reversible lane.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: How are reserved special-use lanes marked on signs and pavement?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: A painted white diamond alerts you right away to read the curbside sign for bus, bike, or carpool rules.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: Who may travel in a lane marked Transit or Bus versus a lane marked Bicycle?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Keeping cars out of dedicated transit and bike lanes protects vulnerable riders and keeps city routes moving.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: What does HOV stand for, and what three details might an HOV sign post?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Many carpool lanes open to solo drivers off-peak, so check posted rider minimums, days, and hours.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: How many people must be riding inside your vehicle to use an HOV 3 lane during restricted hours?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: Count total human occupants including driver and children whenever the posted HOV 3 window is active.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: When is backing up inside an active street travel lane ever legal?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Drivers behind you never expect white backup lights in a live lane outside a curb parallel-parking maneuver.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: What is the right move if you overshoot your street turn or highway exit ramp?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: Backing up toward a missed freeway ramp causes catastrophic high-speed rear-end collisions.

sec06-card-r22.question_text: When two or more lanes go your way, which lane should you normally cruise in?
sec06-card-r22.teaching_text: Cruising right keeps faster traffic flowing smoothly on the left without bottlenecking both lanes.

sec06-card-r23.question_text: On a highway with three or more lanes going your direction, which lane is smoothest around busy ramps?
sec06-card-r23.teaching_text: Using the middle lane leaves the right lane open for merging ramps and the left lane clear for passers.

sec06-card-r24.question_text: When may you legally drive along a highway shoulder?
sec06-card-r24.teaching_text: Shoulders hold broken-down cars, glass debris, and emergency responders rather than impatient shortcutters.

sec06-card-r25.question_text: What is the leftmost lane on a multilane road specifically designed for?
sec06-card-r25.teaching_text: Moving back right once your pass finishes prevents frustrated tailgating queues behind you.

sec06-card-r26.question_text: Why is overtaking another vehicle on its right side riskier than passing on the left?
sec06-card-r26.teaching_text: The right-rear blind zone is wider, and slower drivers moving back right often miss cars sneaking inside.

sec06-card-r27.question_text: May you ever drive onto a paved or gravel shoulder to pass a slower or turning car?
sec06-card-r27.teaching_text: Even wide paved shoulders hide cyclists, mailboxes, or soft drop-offs that spin a passing car out.

sec06-card-r28.question_text: Before starting any intersection turn, what must you scan every corner for alongside turning on your blinker?
sec06-card-r28.teaching_text: Checking all four corners early spots turn-ban signs and joggers jogging off the far curb.

sec06-card-r29.question_text: When no special turn arrows are painted, which lane should you approach a turn from?
sec06-card-r29.teaching_text: Turning from a middle lane across outer traffic cuts straight across a neighboring driver's fender.

sec06-card-r30.question_text: Where should your eyes look as you steer smoothly through a turn?
sec06-card-r30.teaching_text: Your hands naturally follow your eyes, so looking down your target lane steers a clean arc.

sec06-card-r31.question_text: Which lane on the cross street should you turn into, and why?
sec06-card-r31.teaching_text: Finishing in the nearest matching lane avoids drifting wide into oncoming or dual-turn neighbors.

sec06-card-r32.question_text: Which four follow-through steps wrap up an intersection turn cleanly?
sec06-card-r32.teaching_text: Matching road speed, clicking off a stuck blinker, checking mirrors, and moving right keeps traffic predictable.

sec06-card-r33.question_text: Why must you avoid swinging left before making a right turn?
sec06-card-r33.teaching_text: Swerving left tricks the driver behind into thinking you are changing left, tempting them up your right side.

sec06-card-r34.question_text: From which lane do you make a right turn unless pavement arrows show dual right-turn bays?
sec06-card-r34.teaching_text: Turning right from an outside lane without dual-turn markings sideswipes curb-lane traffic.

sec06-card-r35.question_text: What dangerous shortcut must you avoid while steering through a left turn?
sec06-card-r35.teaching_text: Slicing early across the cross-street center line puts your front bumper nose-to-nose with waiting cross-traffic.

sec06-card-r36.question_text: Where should opposing left-turning cars pass relative to each other in a standard intersection?
sec06-card-r36.teaching_text: Turning in front of each other rather than looping behind lets both drivers see oncoming straight lanes clearly.

sec06-card-r37.question_text: Which lane must you turn left from unless pavement markings create multiple left-turn bays?
sec06-card-r37.teaching_text: Starting a left from the farthest left lane going your way eliminates crossing live straight traffic.

sec06-card-r38.question_text: At a busy corner with multiple turn lanes, how early should you merge into your needed lane?
sec06-card-r38.teaching_text: Picking your dual-turn bay a full block out stops last-second solid-white-line dives.

sec06-card-r39.question_text: How must you steer through an intersection that has side-by-side dual turning lanes?
sec06-card-r39.teaching_text: Drifting from the inside turn lane to the outside lane mid-intersection clips the car turning right beside you.

sec06-card-r40.question_text: What does the Kansas handbook name as the safest way to reverse your travel direction?
sec06-card-r40.teaching_text: Looping right around a city block avoids backing into traffic and cuts risky left turns across busy lanes.

sec06-card-r41.question_text: How must you turn around if you realize you are heading the wrong direction on an interstate highway?
sec06-card-r41.teaching_text: Using the next off-ramp and overpass keeps every maneuver flowing smoothly at freeway ramp speeds.

sec06-card-r42.question_text: May civilian drivers cross a grassy interstate median or use a paved emergency-vehicle crossover?
sec06-card-r42.teaching_text: Authorized-vehicles-only turnarounds lack acceleration lanes, dumping slow cars straight into seventy-mile-per-hour passing lanes.

sec06-card-r43.question_text: When do drivers use a two-point driveway or alley turnabout?
sec06-card-r43.teaching_text: Dead-end roads and rural stretches without connecting city blocks call for a controlled driveway reversal.

sec06-card-r44.question_text: Why is backing into a driveway safer than nosing in and backing out, and on what road width may you use it?
sec06-card-r44.teaching_text: Backing into an empty driveway lets you pull forward out into live street traffic with clear windshield visibility.

sec06-card-r45.question_text: What signal, stop, and visual checks start a reverse two-point driveway turn?
sec06-card-r45.teaching_text: Stopping just past the driveway with a right signal alerts following cars before you shift into reverse.

sec06-card-r46.question_text: While backing slowly for a reverse two-point turn, when do you start turning the wheel rightward into the driveway?
sec06-card-r46.teaching_text: Turning right as your back bumper lines up with the driveway edge swings the car cleanly off the street.

sec06-card-r47.question_text: Once centered inside the driveway on a reverse two-point turn, how do you finish re-entering the road?
sec06-card-r47.teaching_text: Pulling out forward after straightening your tires gives full left-and-right sightlines before turning left.

sec06-card-r48.question_text: How do you position, signal, and pull into a driveway or alley for a forward two-point turn?
sec06-card-r48.teaching_text: Pulling onto the right side of a wide driveway leaves turning room when you reverse back out.

sec06-card-r49.question_text: In a forward two-point turn, where do you stop inside the driveway and which signal goes on before reversing?
sec06-card-r49.teaching_text: Signaling right tells street drivers which way your rear bumper will swing as you back into the near lane.

sec06-card-r50.question_text: How do you steer out of a forward two-point driveway turn and get moving forward again?
sec06-card-r50.teaching_text: Backing into the nearest lane and stopping fully before shifting to drive avoids crossing opposing traffic twice.

sec06-card-r51.question_text: Which turnaround does the Kansas handbook warn is the hardest and most dangerous, and when is it allowed?
sec06-card-r51.teaching_text: Sitting sideways across both lanes exposes your doors to oncoming traffic if hills or curves hide approaching cars.

sec06-card-r52.question_text: How do you set up at the right edge of the road to begin a three-point turn?
sec06-card-r52.teaching_text: Starting tight against the right edge maximizes every foot of pavement width for your first left cut.

sec06-card-r53.question_text: What signal, checks, and wheel turn carry you across the road on the first leg of a three-point turn?
sec06-card-r53.teaching_text: Checking your left blind spot catches any impatient car trying to pass you just as you crank left.

sec06-card-r54.question_text: On the middle backing leg of a three-point turn, what checks and wheel direction do you use?
sec06-card-r54.teaching_text: Cranking hard right in reverse swings your nose around toward your new travel direction quickly.

sec06-card-r55.question_text: How do you complete the third forward leg of a three-point turnabout?
sec06-card-r55.teaching_text: Rechecking both directions before pulling into the right lane and canceling your blinker completes the turn safely.

sec06-card-r56.question_text: What two basic conditions determine whether you can legally make a U-turn?
sec06-card-r56.teaching_text: Trying a U-turn on a narrow street forces an illegal mid-traffic backup or hits the far curb.

sec06-card-r57.question_text: Before swinging a permitted U-turn, what traffic gap and cross-street movement must you watch?
sec06-card-r57.teaching_text: A cross-street driver turning right on red rarely expects an oncoming car to loop a full U-turn into the same lane.

sec06-card-r58.question_text: Which way does traffic circulate around a roundabout island, and who yields at entry?
sec06-card-r58.teaching_text: Cars already circling the island hold priority, so wait for a clean gap on your left before entering.

sec06-card-r59.question_text: What target speed range does the Kansas handbook recommend when entering a roundabout?
sec06-card-r59.teaching_text: Slowing to fifteen-to-twenty hugs the tight circular geometry smoothly and makes yielding effortless.
sec06-card-r59.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen to twenty miles per hour

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen to twenty miles per hour

sec06-card-r60.question_text: When do you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout, and what two moves are banned inside the circle?
sec06-card-r60.teaching_text: Swapping lanes or overtaking inside curved circle stripes causes instant sideswipes with spiraling neighbors.

sec06-card-r61.question_text: Who must you yield to at roundabout approaches, including when two vehicles arrive together?
sec06-card-r61.teaching_text: Splitter-island crosswalks sit a car length before the yield line, so watch walkers and bikes first.

sec06-card-r62.question_text: Which direction do you steer as you enter a roundabout?
sec06-card-r62.teaching_text: Splitter islands angle every entry rightward so nobody accidentally turns left into oncoming circle traffic.

sec06-card-r63.question_text: How should you use your turn signal when taking an immediate right turn at a roundabout?
sec06-card-r63.teaching_text: Signaling right on approach lets waiting drivers at the next leg know you are peeling off immediately.

sec06-card-r64.question_text: How do you signal when going straight through a roundabout?
sec06-card-r64.teaching_text: Skipping an approach signal avoids confusing the first leg, then clicking right just before your exit alerts others.

sec06-card-r65.question_text: When making a three-quarter left-turn movement around a roundabout, when does the handbook tell you to signal right?
sec06-card-r65.teaching_text: Clicking your right signal after passing the exit before yours tells entering drivers you are leaving next.

sec06-card-r66.question_text: How should you space your car around semi-trucks or buses inside a roundabout?
sec06-card-r66.teaching_text: Long trailers track wide across lane lines and truck aprons to clear tight roundabout curves.

sec06-card-r67.question_text: Which visual equipment on a stopped school bus requires approaching drivers to stop?
sec06-card-r67.teaching_text: Whether red lights flash alone, the octagon arm extends, or both activate together, halt immediately.

sec06-card-r68.question_text: After school-bus red lights go dark and the stop arm folds in, what else must you confirm before rolling?
sec06-card-r68.teaching_text: Young children sometimes drop papers or dart back across even after the bus retracts its arm.

sec06-card-r69.question_text: Do double solid yellow center lines excuse oncoming traffic from stopping for a school bus?
sec06-card-r69.teaching_text: Children walk right across painted yellow stripes, so oncoming traffic must still make a complete stop.

sec06-card-r70.question_text: Does a painted shared center left-turn lane exempt oncoming drivers from stopping for a school bus?
sec06-card-r70.teaching_text: A flat painted turn bay is not a raised physical barrier, so every lane in both directions stops.

sec06-card-r71.question_text: On undivided multilane highways and intersections, which sides of the road must stop for a flashing school bus?
sec06-card-r71.teaching_text: Four-lane undivided roads still require oncoming lanes and intersection approaches to halt completely.

sec06-card-r72.question_text: When is oncoming traffic NOT required to stop for a school bus flashing red lights?
sec06-card-r72.teaching_text: Only a raised grass median, concrete wall, or physical divider between roadways excuses opposite-direction lanes.

sec06-card-r73.question_text: What two basic safety checks make a roadside parking spot safe for passing traffic?
sec06-card-r73.teaching_text: Never leave a car jutting into travel lanes or tucked blind behind a sharp hill crest or curve.

sec06-card-r74.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle relative to designated areas, live traffic, and curbs?
sec06-card-r74.teaching_text: Snugging close to the curb keeps side mirrors and opening doors safely away from passing traffic.

sec06-card-r75.question_text: After setting the parking brake, which gear position secures a manual car versus an automatic car?
sec06-card-r75.teaching_text: Pairing the mechanical parking brake with park or an engaged manual gear provides redundant rollaway protection.

sec06-card-r76.question_text: What two things should you switch off before removing the ignition key?
sec06-card-r76.teaching_text: Turning off headlights prevents a dead battery when you return to the parked car.

sec06-card-r77.question_text: How do you prevent 'dooring' a cyclist or passing car when exiting a street-parked vehicle?
sec06-card-r77.teaching_text: Swinging a driver door into a bike lane without looking causes severe crashes, so scan and shut quickly.

sec06-card-r78.question_text: What must you always do with your keys and door locks whenever walking away from a parked car?
sec06-card-r78.teaching_text: Keys left inside an unlocked car invite joyriding thefts and liability headaches in seconds.

sec06-card-r79.question_text: From which end of a street-parked car should you walk toward your driver door, and why?
sec06-card-r79.teaching_text: Approaching from the front bumper with key in hand lets you watch oncoming lane traffic face-to-face.

sec06-card-r80.question_text: How close to the curb or road edge should you stop parallel before setting downhill parking wheels?
sec06-card-r80.teaching_text: Starting within one foot of the edge sets up clean tire-to-curb contact without sticking your tail out.

sec06-card-r81.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking downhill, whether a curb is present or not?
sec06-card-r81.teaching_text: Turning right toward the curb or shoulder ensures any brake slip wedges into the curb or rolls off-road.

sec06-card-r82.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill beside a raised curb?
sec06-card-r82.teaching_text: Uphill with a curb is the one left-turn exception so the back of the right-front tire catches the curb.

sec06-card-r83.question_text: After turning your wheels away from an uphill curb, how do you seat the tire against the concrete?
sec06-card-r83.teaching_text: Letting the car settle gently backward until rubber kisses concrete chocks the vehicle before setting park.

sec06-card-r84.question_text: Which way do you turn your front wheels when parking uphill where there is NO curb?
sec06-card-r84.teaching_text: Without a concrete curb to catch a left-turned wheel, turning right sends a rolling car off the road instead of into traffic.

sec06-card-r85.question_text: How should you position your car in a parking aisle before swinging into an angle or perpendicular stall?
sec06-card-r85.teaching_text: Giving yourself swing room away from the stall prevents clipping the near-side parked bumper as you turn in.

sec06-card-r86.question_text: How should your wheels and car sit once parked inside an angle or ninety-degree stall?
sec06-card-r86.teaching_text: Straightening your front tires keeps you from lurching into your neighbor's door when you back out later.

sec06-card-r87.question_text: What four steps come right before releasing the brake to back out of an angle or perpendicular space?
sec06-card-r87.teaching_text: Signaling and lighting up reverse lamps warns cross-aisle drivers whose view of you is blocked by tall SUVs.

sec06-card-r88.question_text: While backing out of a parking stall, when do you stop and shift into drive?
sec06-card-r88.teaching_text: Never slam from reverse into drive while still rolling backward in a tight lot aisle.

sec06-card-r100.question_text: How many feet must parked cars stay from a fire-station driveway on the same side versus across the street?
sec06-card-r100.teaching_text: Long ladder trucks need huge across-street swing arcs to pull out of station bays fast.

sec06-card-r101.question_text: Besides driveways, alleys, and private roads, what sidewalk feature must you never block when parking?
sec06-card-r101.teaching_text: Blocking a lowered sidewalk ramp strands wheelchair users and strollers out in street traffic.

sec06-card-r102.question_text: Which four elevated, recessed, or enclosed road structures prohibit parking completely?
sec06-card-r102.teaching_text: Tight walls and missing shoulders leave zero room for traffic or fire crews to squeeze past a parked car.

sec06-card-r103.question_text: May you cross oncoming traffic to park facing against the direction of traffic on that curb?
sec06-card-r103.teaching_text: Parking nose-against-flow forces you to pull blind head-on into oncoming cars when leaving.

sec06-card-r104.question_text: What three forms of official credential allow parking in a marked disability space in Kansas?
sec06-card-r104.teaching_text: Marked blue stalls stay open for mobility access only when drivers respect credential requirements.

sec06-card-r105.question_text: Is stopping or parking alongside another curb-parked car in the street lane ever allowed?
sec06-card-r105.teaching_text: Double parking chokes a live travel lane and forces following cars across center lines.

sec06-card-r89.question_text: Where do you pull up and stop first when setting up to parallel park, and how do you handle cars behind you?
sec06-card-r89.teaching_text: Signaling early and letting tailgaters clear prevents someone crowding your rear bumper just as you reverse.

sec06-card-r90.question_text: Once traffic clears, how do you steer backward into a parallel-parking space?
sec06-card-r90.teaching_text: Looking back while angling in first and counter-steering straight tucks both tires neatly beside the curb.

sec06-card-r91.question_text: How do you finish positioning your car inside a parallel space without tapping the car behind?
sec06-card-r91.teaching_text: Leaving even bumper gaps front and back ensures neither neighbor gets boxed in.

sec06-card-r92.question_text: What first move gives your front bumper room to clear the car ahead when leaving a tight parallel spot?
sec06-card-r92.teaching_text: Easing back a couple feet opens the steering angle needed so your right fender clears the front bumper.

sec06-card-r93.question_text: What checks and clearance check must you make as you pull out of a parallel space into live traffic?
sec06-card-r93.teaching_text: Splitting your glance between oncoming mirror traffic and the parked bumper ahead prevents scraping or cutting someone off.

sec06-card-r94.question_text: Which four everyday pedestrian and traffic zones forbid parking?
sec06-card-r94.teaching_text: Parking on corners, walkways, or narrow construction lanes blinds sightlines and forces walkers into traffic.

sec06-card-r95.question_text: How close to a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal does Kansas forbid parking?
sec06-card-r95.teaching_text: Parking right up to a stop sign hides the octagon and cross-traffic from approaching drivers.

sec06-card-r96.question_text: How many feet must a parked vehicle stay clear of a pedestrian safety zone?
sec06-card-r96.teaching_text: Pair pedestrian safety zones with the thirty-foot sign rule so both numbers lock in effortlessly.

sec06-card-r97.question_text: How close to a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Kansas?
sec06-card-r97.teaching_text: Fire engines need unobstructed fifteen-foot hose radius access the second they arrive at a blaze.

sec06-card-r98.question_text: Within how many feet of a highway-railroad crossing is parking prohibited?
sec06-card-r98.teaching_text: Fifty feet keeps parked vans and trucks from blocking crossing gates, flashers, and down-track train sightlines.

sec06-card-r99.question_text: What is the maximum distance your tires may sit out from the curb when parallel parked?
sec06-card-r99.teaching_text: One foot equals twelve inches, matching the exact twelve-inch setup rule for hill parking.

sec06-card-r106.question_text: What parking rule does a white painted curb indicate?
sec06-card-r106.teaching_text: White curbs mark quick passenger drop-off or mailbox stops where leaving the car long-term draws a ticket.

sec06-card-r107.question_text: What restriction does a yellow painted curb identify?
sec06-card-r107.teaching_text: Always check adjacent signs at a yellow curb for commercial loading rules or time caps.

sec06-card-r108.question_text: Who is a blue painted curb reserved for?
sec06-card-r108.teaching_text: Only vehicles displaying a valid disability plate, placard, or sticker may park along blue curb paint.

sec06-card-r109.question_text: What strict restriction does a red painted curb mark?
sec06-card-r109.teaching_text: Never stop or leave a vehicle beside red fire-lane paint where emergency trucks stage hoses and ladders.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: What two hands-on learning pieces can a driver handbook never replace?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Reading rules builds head knowledge, yet real-time road judgment develops solely behind the wheel with coaching.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: Which three areas around your vehicle must you scan to spot speed or lane problems early?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Staring solely past the hood misses blind-spot mergers and fast tailgaters closing from behind.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: How does aiming your eyes far down your intended path improve steering and traffic flow?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Staring right off your front bumper causes constant jerky corrections and last-second emergency braking.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: At least how far ahead does the Kansas handbook recommend looking on a highway?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Highway speeds eat ground fast, requiring at least a quarter-mile look-ahead to spot slowdowns early.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: Which ahead-of-you clues let you adjust speed or change lanes well in advance?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Catching distant red brake lamps or side-street noses early lets you ease off smoothly.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: How should you approach a traffic light that has already been green for a long time?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Accelerating toward a stale green sets up a panic slam or red-light run when yellow pops.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: How do early speed or lane adjustments help drivers following behind you?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Gradual early cues keep the driver behind your trunk from getting surprised into a rear-end hit.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: How do you measure your look-ahead time while driving?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Picking a distant post or overpass and counting seconds until you pass it checks visual range.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: How many seconds ahead of the vehicle define the Kansas handbook's visual lead?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Scanning twenty to thirty seconds out covers roughly two city blocks or a long highway stretch.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: What two survival advantages does a strong twenty-to-thirty-second visual lead provide?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Seeing trouble twenty seconds early gives plenty of room to either brake gently or steer clear.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: About how many seconds and feet does the handbook's sixty-mph dry-road stop take?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Needing three hundred fifty-nine feet on dry pavement exceeds an entire football field from endzone to endzone.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: About how many seconds and feet does the handbook's thirty-mph dry-road stop require?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Even neighborhood thirty-mile-per-hour travel eats over eight car lengths before your bumper halts.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: Below what forward visibility distance does the handbook warn sixty miles per hour is too fast?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Since stopping from sixty takes roughly three hundred sixty feet, seeing under four hundred outruns your brakes.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: When may even thirty miles per hour be too fast for available visibility?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Thick fog or blind curves shorter than one hundred fifty feet leave barely enough space to react.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: Where is scanning sideways for entering vehicles and walkers most critical?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Cross-traffic threats arrive from ninety-degree angles at corners and rail tracks rather than dead ahead.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: Which everyday access points count as intersections besides street-to-street corners?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Drivers pull out from strip-mall aprons and home driveways with the exact same conflict risk as streets.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: Which five elements should you scan as you roll toward any intersection?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Checking cars, walkers, signals, sightline blocks, and slick asphalt prevents nasty surprises at the stop bar.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: In what order should you look before entering an intersection and right after stopping?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Cross traffic from the left reaches your driver door first, making that final left recheck vital.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: Why must you scan cross traffic right after your light turns green even though cross cars face red?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Charging out the instant green illuminates puts you broadside into drivers trying to beat stale yellows.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: What two conditions must exist before you pull into an intersection?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Entering blind or into backed-up cars strands you sideways inside the box when cross traffic goes.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: How should you proceed after stopping at an intersection where hedges or parked trucks block your view?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: Creeping inch-by-inch lets cross drivers spot your front bumper before your cabin enters their lane.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: Which five roadside zones call for extra sideways scanning?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: Crowded curbs, work crews, and excited kids generate sudden step-outs without warning.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: What two things must you verify before starting a left turn across oncoming lanes?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: Getting halted mid-turn by a crosswalk pedestrian leaves your passenger door exposed to oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-f24.question_text: Which three conflict sources must you check right before turning right?
sec07-card-f24.teaching_text: Focusing solely on cars from the left misses opposing left-turners claiming the same lane or walkers.

sec07-card-f25.question_text: What should you do at the round rail warning, and what two rail hazards should you scan for?
sec07-card-f25.teaching_text: Small yellow track-maintenance carts may not trigger crossing gates yet still collide hard at grade crossings.

sec07-card-f26.question_text: Why should you check your rearview mirrors more frequently in dense traffic?
sec07-card-f26.teaching_text: Catching a distracted driver closing fast behind lets you build front braking cushion before traffic halts.

sec07-card-f27.question_text: Before which four driving situations are mirror checks especially vital?
sec07-card-f27.teaching_text: Changing speed or lane—or rolling down long hills—shifts closing gaps behind your rear bumper fast.

sec07-card-f28.question_text: Which other vehicles must you scan for before moving into a target lane or merge space?
sec07-card-f28.teaching_text: On a three-lane highway, a car two lanes over can dive into the same center gap simultaneously.

sec07-card-f29.question_text: What spacing must you protect ahead while glancing at mirrors for a lane change?
sec07-card-f29.teaching_text: Creeping close to the bumper ahead while looking back guarantees a rear-end crash if traffic brakes.

sec07-card-f30.question_text: What is a vehicle blind spot, and how must you check it?
sec07-card-f30.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave angled pockets beside rear fenders that only an over-the-shoulder glance exposes.

sec07-card-f31.question_text: Why should you use repeated brief glances rather than one long stare over your shoulder?
sec07-card-f31.teaching_text: Looking sideways for two full seconds at sixty miles per hour drives nearly two hundred feet blind.

sec07-card-f32.question_text: What five-step sequence completes a clean lane change?
sec07-card-f32.teaching_text: Skipping the final recheck or leaving your blinker flashing confuses surrounding drivers on fast roads.

sec07-card-f33.question_text: Where is checking your mirrors before slowing down most critical?
sec07-card-f33.teaching_text: Trailing commuters expect cruising speed midblock, not an abrupt brake dive into a small driveway.

sec07-card-f34.question_text: Which vehicles should you watch for in your mirrors on a long or steep downhill grade?
sec07-card-f34.teaching_text: Heavy rigs gain tremendous downhill momentum or suffer hot brake fade right behind slower cars.

sec07-card-f35.question_text: How does the Kansas handbook define perception distance?
sec07-card-f35.teaching_text: Even before your brain decides to brake, your car covers real asphalt just identifying trouble.

sec07-card-f36.question_text: Which three factors can lengthen or shorten your perception distance?
sec07-card-f36.teaching_text: Fatigue, glare, or camouflaged hazards stretch recognition time and add extra feet before reaction even begins.

sec07-card-f37.question_text: What is an alert driver's average perception time according to the handbook?
sec07-card-f37.teaching_text: Even wide-awake drivers burn nearly a full second recognizing danger before muscles start moving.

sec07-card-f38.question_text: What travel interval does reaction distance measure?
sec07-card-f38.teaching_text: Lifting off the throttle and pressing the brake pedal eats another chunk of road at full speed.

sec07-card-f39.question_text: How long is average reaction time, and about how far does a car travel during it at fifty mph?
sec07-card-f39.teaching_text: Covering fifty-five feet before brake pads touch rotors shows why bumper-hugging guarantees rear-end hits.

sec07-card-f40.question_text: What part of a stop does braking distance measure?
sec07-card-f40.teaching_text: Friction only starts scrubbing speed once pads clamp down, and wet or worn tires stretch this phase.

sec07-card-f41.question_text: About how many feet of braking distance does the handbook's fifty-mph dry-road example take?
sec07-card-f41.teaching_text: After perception and reaction finish, friction alone still consumes one hundred fifty-eight feet at fifty.

sec07-card-f42.question_text: Which three distances add together to form total stopping distance?
sec07-card-f42.teaching_text: Test traps quote braking distance alone, forgetting the two human-delay segments before pads engage.

sec07-card-f43.question_text: What minimum total stopping distance does the handbook give at fifty miles per hour under ideal conditions?
sec07-card-f43.teaching_text: Combining perception, reaction, and braking at fifty eats nearly ninety yards even on bone-dry asphalt.

sec07-card-f44.question_text: Compared with twenty miles per hour, how much impact force and braking distance occur at forty?
sec07-card-f44.teaching_text: Kinetic energy squares with speed, so doubling from twenty to forty quadruples stopping demand.

sec07-card-f45.question_text: Compared with twenty miles per hour, how much impact force and braking distance occur at sixty?
sec07-card-f45.teaching_text: Tripling speed from twenty to sixty multiplies crash violence and braking distance ninefold.

sec07-card-f46.question_text: Compared with twenty miles per hour, how much impact force and braking distance occur at eighty?
sec07-card-f46.teaching_text: Quadrupling speed to eighty unleashes sixteen times the crash energy and stopping runway.

sec07-card-f47.question_text: How does slamming on the brakes abruptly affect drivers behind you?
sec07-card-f47.teaching_text: Abrupt deceleration strips away the reaction cushion trailing drivers rely on to halt cleanly.

sec07-card-f48.question_text: How far ahead does the handbook advise searching to avoid last-second panic stops?
sec07-card-f48.teaching_text: Spotting red brake lights ten-plus seconds ahead lets you lift off the gas early and smoothly.

sec07-card-f49.question_text: Beyond safety, what practical wallet benefit comes from planning ahead and slowing gradually?
sec07-card-f49.teaching_text: Coasting gently toward red lights avoids wasting gas accelerating right up to hard brake stabs.

sec07-card-f50.question_text: Which four factors must guide the speed you choose at any moment?
sec07-card-f50.teaching_text: Driving the posted number blindly ignores traffic density, fog, or tight following gaps.

sec07-card-f51.question_text: For which three roadway situations does the handbook specifically call for lower speed?
sec07-card-f51.teaching_text: Tight bends, wet asphalt, and deer crossings demand immediate grip or braking margin.

sec07-card-f52.question_text: When should you slow down for a curve, and why is hard braking mid-curve risky?
sec07-card-f52.teaching_text: Tires already fighting cornering force break traction fast if you stomp the brakes mid-bend.

sec07-card-f53.question_text: Which three conditions require trimming curve-entry speed even further?
sec07-card-f53.teaching_text: Entering a wet or blind bend right behind another bumper leaves nowhere to go if traffic stops.

sec07-card-f54.question_text: Once you enter a curve at a safe speed, how should you use the accelerator?
sec07-card-f54.teaching_text: Gentle steady gas settles weight evenly across all four tires as you track around the bend.

sec07-card-f55.question_text: Why must you slow down at the very first drops of rain, snow, or sleet?
sec07-card-f55.teaching_text: Light moisture blends with baked-on grime and dripped crankcase oil into a slick grease film.

sec07-card-f56.question_text: When is a sudden rainstorm on hot pavement at its slickest?
sec07-card-f56.teaching_text: Heat draws fresh petroleum up from asphalt pores until sustained downpours finally rinse the lane.

sec07-card-f57.question_text: What two vehicle-control penalties come from reduced tire grip on wet pavement?
sec07-card-f57.teaching_text: Water film cuts rubber friction for both straight braking and lateral cornering simultaneously.

sec07-card-f58.question_text: By about how much does the Kansas handbook recommend dropping speed on wet roads?
sec07-card-f58.teaching_text: Shaving ten miles per hour off dry pace buys vital stopping and steering margin in rain.

sec07-card-f59.question_text: How much should you cut your speed when driving on packed snow?
sec07-card-f59.teaching_text: Compacted snow slashes tire bite dramatically, demanding half normal pace or even slower.

sec07-card-f60.question_text: How should you handle speed on icy roads, and what is the safest choice overall?
sec07-card-f60.teaching_text: Solid ice offers near-zero friction, so staying parked beats creeping unless travel is unavoidable.

sec07-card-f61.question_text: Between which calendar dates does Kansas permit studded snow tires?
sec07-card-f61.teaching_text: Running metal studs outside winter dates chews up dry highway pavement and violates state rules.

sec07-card-f62.question_text: Where can a road's center crown and drainage slope pull a skidding vehicle?
sec07-card-f62.teaching_text: Lanes tilt slightly outward to shed rain, so weightless sliding tires drift straight toward ditches.

sec07-card-f63.question_text: How does shaded pavement behave compared with sunny asphalt on cold, wet days?
sec07-card-f63.teaching_text: Tree or building shadows hide black ice long after open sunlit stretches look bone dry.

sec07-card-f64.question_text: Which elevated or sheltered road structures can ice over while regular roads stay clear?
sec07-card-f64.teaching_text: Frigid air chills bridge decks from both top and bottom without warm earth underneath.

sec07-card-f65.question_text: Why is ice near thirty-two degrees often slicker than ice in deep sub-zero cold?
sec07-card-f65.teaching_text: Melting film near freezing acts like grease on an ice rink compared with dry sub-zero frost.

sec07-card-f66.question_text: What happens between your tires and the road during hydroplaning?
sec07-card-f66.teaching_text: When tread grooves cannot clear deep water fast enough, tires lift up like water skis.

sec07-card-f67.question_text: What is your primary defense against hydroplaning in rain or standing puddles?
sec07-card-f67.teaching_text: Lower speed gives tire tread channels time to squeeze water out and touch solid asphalt.

sec07-card-f68.question_text: What conflict comes from driving faster than surrounding traffic, and what pace should you keep?
sec07-card-f68.teaching_text: Constantly weaving past everyone multiplies lane-change exposure, though matching flow never excuses speeding.

sec07-card-f69.question_text: Driving more than how many miles per hour below traffic flow triggers dangerous bunching and passes?
sec07-card-f69.teaching_text: Crawling fifteen-plus under highway flow stacks frustrated cars up into risky passing clusters.

sec07-card-f70.question_text: What should a slow-moving driver do when traffic bunches up behind?
sec07-card-f70.teaching_text: Using a safe turnout clears packed queues before someone gambles on a tight head-on pass.

sec07-card-f71.question_text: Which two kinds of signs must you check and obey on a highway entrance ramp?
sec07-card-f71.teaching_text: Verifying direction stops wrong-way entries, while curved ramp advisory speeds prevent rollovers.

sec07-card-f72.question_text: How should you use a highway acceleration lane before merging onto the main roadway?
sec07-card-f72.teaching_text: Merging twenty miles per hour slower than freeway traffic forces oncoming semis to slam brakes.

sec07-card-f73.question_text: How should you adjust in an acceleration lane if no merge gap opens right away?
sec07-card-f73.teaching_text: Stopping dead at the end of a ramp leaves zero runway left to accelerate into fast traffic.

sec07-card-f74.question_text: What painted line must you avoid crossing while merging from an acceleration lane?
sec07-card-f74.teaching_text: Cutting across solid white gore paint dives prematurely into traffic before angles align.

sec07-card-f75.question_text: Which checks and signal steps complete a safe merge onto a main highway?
sec07-card-f75.teaching_text: Combining mirror glances, a direct head turn, and an early blinker spots fast blind-spot cars.

sec07-card-f76.question_text: How far ahead of your exit does the handbook advise entering the exit lane in heavy traffic?
sec07-card-f76.teaching_text: Positioning half a mile out prevents desperate last-second dives across packed freeway lanes.

sec07-card-f77.question_text: Where should you start slowing down when your highway exit has a deceleration lane?
sec07-card-f77.teaching_text: Braking early in the main fast lane surprises high-speed traffic cruising right behind you.

sec07-card-f78.question_text: What three things must you account for when slowing onto a limited-access exit ramp?
sec07-card-f78.teaching_text: Highway velocitization makes forty feel slow while short ramp queues stop right around curves.

sec07-card-f79.question_text: How should you adjust speed in cramped zones like shopping centers and busy downtown blocks?
sec07-card-f79.teaching_text: Double-parked vans, backing shoppers, and tight curbs leave nowhere to swerve at full speed.

sec07-card-f80.question_text: Why do rush-hour congestion, narrow bridges, tunnels, and toll plazas call for lower speed?
sec07-card-f80.teaching_text: Zero shoulders inside bridges or tunnels plus sudden plaza merges punish anyone carrying excess speed.

sec07-card-f81.question_text: What sudden hazard must you stay alert for near schools, playgrounds, and neighborhood streets?
sec07-card-f81.teaching_text: Kids focus on play rather than traffic, stepping off curbs without a glance.

sec07-card-f82.question_text: Besides trains and exit room, what surface feature at railroad crossings may require slowing down?
sec07-card-f82.teaching_text: Hitting raised or sunken timber and steel rails too fast jolts suspension and upsets steering.

sec07-card-f83.question_text: What two penalties does excess speed impose on steering and reaction?
sec07-card-f83.teaching_text: Going faster covers far more feet before brakes engage while shrinking your tire cornering margin.

sec07-card-f84.question_text: How does higher speed affect roadside barriers and crash outcomes?
sec07-card-f84.teaching_text: Guardrails and crumple zones absorb finite energy before extreme speed punches straight through.

sec07-card-f85.question_text: Which three extra risks—mechanical, personal, and traffic—does the handbook tie to high speed?
sec07-card-f85.teaching_text: Speeding burns brakes and tires, tenses drivers out, and fools pull-out drivers misjudging your approach.

sec07-card-f86.question_text: What speed limit does the Kansas handbook give for an urban district when no different limit is posted?
sec07-card-f86.teaching_text: Unposted city streets default to thirty miles per hour under normal hazard-free conditions.

sec07-card-f100.question_text: What minimum following interval does Kansas specify, and how do unusual weather or traffic change it?
sec07-card-f100.teaching_text: Two seconds sets the dry baseline, while rain, glare, or congestion demand adding extra seconds.

sec07-card-f87.question_text: What road conditions do posted speed limits assume, and when must you drive below them?
sec07-card-f87.teaching_text: Posted signs state the dry, clear ceiling, so rain, ice, fog, or heavy packs require slower speeds.

sec07-card-f88.question_text: Does a posted fifty-five-mph sign make fifty-five appropriate during a snowstorm?
sec07-card-f88.teaching_text: Driving the dry-weather sign in blowing snow violates basic safe-speed duty and invites spinouts.

sec07-card-f89.question_text: When is checking your speedometer frequently especially important?
sec07-card-f89.teaching_text: After miles at seventy, cruising forty-five down a thirty-zone town street feels deceptively slow.

sec07-card-f90.question_text: Which three driving habits lower rollover risk in high-center-of-gravity vehicles?
sec07-card-f90.teaching_text: Tall SUVs and pickups lean harder, requiring calmer pace, gentle inputs, and pre-curve braking.

sec07-card-f91.question_text: What does ABS stand for, and what is it engineered to let a driver do?
sec07-card-f91.teaching_text: Preventing wheel lockup preserves tire rotation so you can steer cleanly without upsetting balance.

sec07-card-f92.question_text: How does ABS affect stopping distance on dry roads compared with wet surfaces?
sec07-card-f92.teaching_text: Assuming anti-lock brakes shrink dry tailgating stops is a classic misconception—steering control is the dry win.

sec07-card-f93.question_text: What three actions does the handbook direct when using ABS in an emergency?
sec07-card-f93.teaching_text: Finding open pavement first ensures your steerable anti-lock stop guides you clear of the obstacle.

sec07-card-f94.question_text: How should you confirm whether an unfamiliar vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec07-card-f94.teaching_text: Knowing whether to stomp-and-hold or threshold-squeeze before starting the trip prevents panic errors.

sec07-card-f95.question_text: How does the dashboard ABS light behave normally at startup versus during a fault?
sec07-card-f95.teaching_text: An amber ABS bulb staying lit while driving warns that anti-lock assist is offline.

sec07-card-f96.question_text: What does ESP stand for, and what two signals does it continuously compare?
sec07-card-f96.teaching_text: Matching wheel-angle sensors against yaw sensors catches the exact split-second a slide begins.

sec07-card-f97.question_text: What mechanical action can ESP take when it senses a traction mismatch?
sec07-card-f97.teaching_text: Braking one strategic corner pivots a sliding chassis back onto line faster than human feet can.

sec07-card-f98.question_text: How should you steer during traction loss in an ESP-equipped vehicle?
sec07-card-f98.teaching_text: Wild steering jerks confuse stability sensors that rely on smooth directional input to straighten the car.

sec07-card-f99.question_text: What core advantage does keeping an open space cushion around your car provide?
sec07-card-f99.teaching_text: Open buffer room on all sides turns sudden neighboring mistakes into calm, easy adjustments.

sec07-card-f101.question_text: How do you count following time with a roadside marker, and what count is too close?
sec07-card-f101.teaching_text: Reaching a signpost fewer than two seconds after the bumper ahead proves tailgating.

sec07-card-f102.question_text: What should you do if your fixed-marker count comes up shorter than two seconds?
sec07-card-f102.teaching_text: Gently backing off speed and repeating the landmark count rebuilds a verified two-second cushion.

sec07-card-f103.question_text: How do slippery road conditions change the basic two-second following rule?
sec07-card-f103.teaching_text: Two seconds only covers dry tire grip, so rain, slush, or ice require wider time gaps.

sec07-card-f104.question_text: How can you help a trailing driver who pulls out to overtake your vehicle?
sec07-card-f104.teaching_text: Easing off builds merge space ahead of your hood and cuts time spent in oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-f105.question_text: What two hazards require leaving extra following space behind a motorcycle?
sec07-card-f105.teaching_text: Motorcycles shed speed rapidly and a spilled rider on pavement needs extra yards to avoid.

sec07-card-f106.question_text: What two visibility wins come from dropping farther back behind a boxy van or truck?
sec07-card-f106.teaching_text: Hanging back puts you inside wide side mirrors while opening your own sightline past the box.

sec07-card-f107.question_text: Why must you keep a bigger front cushion when hauling heavy cargo or towing a trailer?
sec07-card-f107.teaching_text: Added trailer weight shoves your vehicle forward harder under braking and dulls quick swerves.

sec07-card-f108.question_text: How should darkness or visibility-cutting weather change your following distance?
sec07-card-f108.teaching_text: When rain or night hides trouble ahead of the lead car, extra seconds prevent chain-reaction hits.

sec07-card-f109.question_text: How should you adjust the space in front of you when someone tailgates from behind?
sec07-card-f109.teaching_text: A deeper front buffer lets you brake gradually for both cars so the tailgater avoids ramming you.

sec07-card-f110.question_text: How should you adjust following space behind emergency vehicles?
sec07-card-f110.teaching_text: Responders stop, turn, or deploy gear without notice and need wide operating clearance.

sec07-card-f111.question_text: Behind which vehicles must you keep extra room near railroad tracks because they are required to stop?
sec07-card-f111.teaching_text: School buses, transit coaches, and placarded hazmat rigs halt at rails even when lights stay dark.

sec07-card-f112.question_text: Why must you stop farther back behind another vehicle on an uphill grade?
sec07-card-f112.teaching_text: Manual clutches and heavy trucks often drift back a few feet before pulling uphill.

sec07-card-f113.question_text: Which three habits of yours help a driver behind you maintain a safe following gap?
sec07-card-f113.teaching_text: Predictable speed, advance blinkers, and front buffer prevent surprise brake slams behind you.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: What is the easiest move when you are being tailgated and an adjacent lane is open?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Changing into an empty lane clears an impatient bumper rider cleanly off your trunk.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: How should you handle a tailgater when no empty lane exists to move into?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Waiting until oncoming sightlines open before easing speed helps the tailgater pass safely.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: Why must you never tap or slam your brakes sharply to warn off a tailgater?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Brake-checking invites an instant rear-end collision or escalates aggressive retaliation on the highway.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: How many extra seconds should you add to your front following interval when being tailgated?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Padding two to three extra seconds up front covers stopping room for both vehicles.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: How should you manage your speed instead of cruising right beside another car on a multilane road?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Staggering slightly ahead or back preserves an open swerve pocket on at least one side.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: Where inside your lane should you normally track on a two-way road?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Tracking down the middle leaves balanced escape margin away from both oncoming mirrors and ditches.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: How can you help ramp traffic merge smoothly onto a multilane highway?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Sliding one open lane left gives entering cars stress-free room to match highway flow.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: How should you position past parked cars without crossing the centerline?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Giving extra door-swing room inside your own stripe prevents clipping emerging people or bumpers.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Which vulnerable road users especially need extra lateral space for sudden movements?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Children on foot or bikes wobble and turn unpredictably without checking approaching cars.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: Where inside your lane can you ease while a tractor-trailer overtakes you?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Shifting slightly toward the white edge line adds wind-blast separation while staying on pavement.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: How big should a merge opening be before you pull into moving traffic?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Squeezing into a tight slot forces both you and the trailing car into dangerous tailgating.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: How must you cross several lanes on a wide roadway, and why?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Sweeping across three lanes at once misses fast blind-spot traffic hidden behind closer cars.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: From a stop under normal conditions, about how many seconds does crossing straight across an intersection take?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Accelerating from zero across cross lanes eats three to five full seconds of clear gap.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: What two phases must your traffic gap cover when turning onto a moving street?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Clearing the corner alone is half the job if fast cross traffic rear-ends you while accelerating.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: About how many seconds does the handbook's normal right-turn-and-acceleration example take?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Pulling out right and building street pace requires twelve to fifteen seconds of approaching gap.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: About how many seconds does the handbook's normal left-turn-and-acceleration example require?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Crossing near lanes before accelerating left takes fifteen to eighteen seconds—longer than turning right.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: May you start across an intersection on a green light when traffic blocks the exit side?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Green grants permission only when space clears beyond, keeping cross streets free of gridlock.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: Before starting a left turn, what must you confirm will not trap you across oncoming lanes?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Stopping mid-turn for a surprise walker leaves your side doors broadside to opposing traffic.

sec07-card-r19.question_text: Why must you wait before pulling out in front of an approaching car whose turn signal is flashing?
sec07-card-r19.teaching_text: Pulling out on faith causes T-bone wrecks whenever an approaching driver keeps rolling straight.

sec07-card-r20.question_text: What two harmless mistakes explain why an approaching car's blinker might flash past your corner?
sec07-card-r20.teaching_text: Drivers often signal early for an alley just past you or forget non-canceling stalks.

sec07-card-r21.question_text: When is it safe to start driving onto railroad tracks?
sec07-card-r21.teaching_text: Waiting behind the rails until exit traffic moves guarantees you never stall across steel tracks.

sec07-card-r22.question_text: Why should you complete an overtaking pass promptly within safe limits?
sec07-card-r22.teaching_text: Lingering right next to another moving car stretches both blind-spot exposure and oncoming-lane crash risk.

sec07-card-r23.question_text: Which forward and rearward zones must you check before starting to pass?
sec07-card-r23.teaching_text: Missing a side-road pull-out ahead or a faster passer already in your left blind spot causes crashes.

sec07-card-r24.question_text: From how far behind the lead car should you signal and begin a pass?
sec07-card-r24.teaching_text: Starting two-plus seconds back preserves sightlines around the lead bumper and room to abort.
sec07-card-r24.must_match_memory_hook: Signal at least two seconds back

visual_sync.text_span: Signal at least two seconds back

sec07-card-r25.question_text: How should you steer and scan while alongside the vehicle you are passing?
sec07-card-r25.teaching_text: Glancing too long right pulls your hands inward toward the car you are overtaking.

sec07-card-r26.question_text: What rearview mirror cue tells you it is safe to signal and return to your lane after passing?
sec07-card-r26.teaching_text: Seeing both headlights in your center mirror confirms safe bumper clearance before moving right.

sec07-card-r27.question_text: How should you position and pace your car while another driver overtakes you?
sec07-card-r27.teaching_text: Accelerating while someone passes traps both cars in a deadly head-on squeeze.

sec07-card-r28.question_text: Does a broken yellow line or passing-zone sign guarantee it is safe to pass?
sec07-card-r28.teaching_text: Paint marks sightline geometry, not live oncoming traffic, so you still judge clear gap yourself.

sec07-card-r29.question_text: How many vehicles should you pass at once, and how long warns the handbook a pass can take?
sec07-card-r29.teaching_text: Stringing multi-car passes gambles against oncoming cars when a single pass already eats half a minute.

sec07-card-r30.question_text: What is the rule if you can see an oncoming vehicle or feel unsure about passing distance?
sec07-card-r30.teaching_text: Two sixty-mile-per-hour cars close at one hundred twenty combined, turning tiny doubts into head-on wrecks.

sec07-card-r31.question_text: Why is judging passing distance against oncoming traffic naturally tricky for human eyes?
sec07-card-r31.teaching_text: Straight-on profiles show almost zero sideways motion until closing distance becomes dangerously short.

sec07-card-r32.question_text: What does it mean if you can actually see an oncoming vehicle getting closer ahead?
sec07-card-r32.teaching_text: Cars beyond twenty-five seconds look parked, so visible closing motion means too little time to pass.

sec07-card-r33.question_text: At fifty-five to sixty mph, how much clear forward view is needed to pass near hills or curves?
sec07-card-r33.teaching_text: Needing twenty to twenty-five seconds demands at least one-third mile of unobstructed highway ahead.

sec07-card-r34.question_text: How must you treat any hill or curve blocking sight, and how close may no pass start?
sec07-card-r34.teaching_text: Imagining a hidden car rounding every blind bend within a third-mile stops fatal gambles.

sec07-card-r35.question_text: At which roadway junctions and side-access points must you avoid passing?
sec07-card-r35.teaching_text: Cars turning left into or out of side accesses cut straight across the passing lane.

sec07-card-r36.question_text: Which roadside hazards ahead could suddenly force the car you are passing sideways into you?
sec07-card-r36.teaching_text: If the lead driver swerves left around a cyclist or pothole mid-pass, both cars collide.

sec07-card-r37.question_text: What return-space rule governs passing a vehicle inside a line of traffic?
sec07-card-r37.teaching_text: Counting on tight packed drivers to brake and let you squeeze in leaves you stranded left.

sec07-card-r38.question_text: Within how many seconds of travel before a railroad crossing does the handbook advise against passing?
sec07-card-r38.teaching_text: Stopped buses, rough rails, or lowering gates ahead turn pre-track passing into a trap.

sec07-card-r39.question_text: Which two kinds of entering drivers need extra space because they cannot see you well?
sec07-card-r39.teaching_text: Bumpers nosing past hedges or reversing out of driveways move blind until half into your lane.

sec07-card-r40.question_text: What everyday weather gear or window issue warns you someone cannot see traffic clearly?
sec07-card-r40.teaching_text: Peephole-scraped frosty windshields and tilted rain umbrellas block a person from spotting approaching traffic.

sec07-card-r41.question_text: Around which busy or preoccupied groups should you add extra caution and buffer space?
sec07-card-r41.teaching_text: Workers focused on packages or asphalt—and pedestrians staring at phones—step out without looking.

sec07-card-r42.question_text: What erratic moves signal a confused driver hunting for an address or turn?
sec07-card-r42.teaching_text: Lost motorists slam brakes or dive across lanes the instant they spot a house number.

sec07-card-r43.question_text: What should you do if an overtaking driver misjudges oncoming traffic and runs low on room?
sec07-card-r43.teaching_text: Braking to open space ahead of your hood prevents a three-car head-on catastrophe.

sec07-card-r44.question_text: How should you respond when another driver needs an abrupt lane change right ahead of you?
sec07-card-r44.teaching_text: Lifting off the gas for two seconds defuses a sideswipe far better than defending turf.

sec07-card-r45.question_text: How do you separate hazards when an oncoming car and a roadside walker line up ahead?
sec07-card-r45.teaching_text: Slowing early so you meet one hazard at a time preserves wide lateral room past the pedestrian.

sec07-card-r46.question_text: What is the main safety payoff of signaling your position and next move clearly?
sec07-card-r46.teaching_text: Predictable cars rarely get hit because surrounding drivers adjust early before paths cross.

sec07-card-r47.question_text: Why should you switch on headlights whenever rain, snow, or fog cuts visibility?
sec07-card-r47.teaching_text: Daytime running lamps often leave taillights dark, whereas full headlights light both ends.

sec07-card-r48.question_text: When does Kansas law require your headlights to be turned on during wet weather?
sec07-card-r48.teaching_text: Tying headlights directly to wiper use eliminates guesswork during drizzle, mist, or road spray.

sec07-card-r49.question_text: When as evening approaches should you switch your headlights on?
sec07-card-r49.teaching_text: Twilight flattens road contrast before full darkness, so early beams make your car pop.

sec07-card-r50.question_text: Why should you turn headlights on when driving away from a low rising or setting sun?
sec07-card-r50.teaching_text: Oncoming motorists squinting straight into low glare miss dark silhouettes unless headlights shine.

sec07-card-r51.question_text: What three upkeep steps keep headlights effective without blinding oncoming drivers?
sec07-card-r51.teaching_text: Road grime dims output fast, while misaligned bulbs blind oncoming traffic instead of lighting lanes.

sec07-card-r52.question_text: For what legitimate safety purpose is a vehicle's horn designed?
sec07-card-r52.teaching_text: A timely alert stops an unaware walker or drifting driver right before contact occurs.

sec07-card-r53.question_text: Which three everyday horn uses does the Kansas handbook tell drivers to avoid?
sec07-card-r53.teaching_text: Honking to wave hello, vent frustration, or hurry someone cheapens real emergency warnings.

sec07-card-r54.question_text: How should you use your horn around a blind pedestrian?
sec07-card-r54.teaching_text: Sudden horn blasts disorient visually impaired walkers who depend on steady traffic audio.

sec07-card-r55.question_text: Who should you notify if possible during a roadside breakdown, and where might a number appear?
sec07-card-r55.teaching_text: Highway motorist-aid signs post direct dispatch numbers that bring patrol protection faster.

sec07-card-r56.question_text: Where should you guide your vehicle as soon as a breakdown forces a stop?
sec07-card-r56.teaching_text: Coasting your car completely clear of active asphalt dramatically cuts the chance of a rear impact.

sec07-card-r57.question_text: Which vehicle lights must you switch on immediately to mark a disabled car?
sec07-card-r57.teaching_text: Synchronized amber flashers tell fast-closing traffic your vehicle is stopped, not cruising.

sec07-card-r58.question_text: Which two blind spots on a road must you avoid stopping just beyond during a breakdown?
sec07-card-r58.teaching_text: Parking right over a hillcrest or curve hides your bumper until fast traffic tops the blind spot.

sec07-card-r59.question_text: About how far behind a disabled vehicle does the handbook place roadside warning flares?
sec07-card-r59.teaching_text: Placing flares two to three hundred feet back alerts highway traffic early enough to merge left.

sec07-card-r60.question_text: What two dangerous breakdown actions inside a live traffic lane must you never attempt?
sec07-card-r60.teaching_text: Kneeling beside lug nuts in an active travel lane exposes your body directly to passing bumpers.

sec07-card-r61.question_text: Which non-electric signals show passing patrols that your parked car is disabled?
sec07-card-r61.teaching_text: Tying white fabric to a mirror, handle, or antenna—or propping the hood—signals distress even if batteries die.

sec07-card-r62.question_text: Which two kinds of vehicle changes require signaling to surrounding road users?
sec07-card-r62.teaching_text: Using turn blinkers and brake lights together lets everyone around read both steering and slowing.

sec07-card-r63.question_text: How does the handbook match turn-signal modes to intersection turns versus lane shifts?
sec07-card-r63.teaching_text: Full clicks hold through ninety-degree corners, while lane-change detents cover gentle highway merges.

sec07-card-r64.question_text: What check should follow every completed turn or gentle lane change?
sec07-card-r64.teaching_text: Slight highway steering angles rarely trip auto-cancel cams, leaving false turn cues blinking.

sec07-card-r65.question_text: How do brake lights communicate with traffic behind, and when should you begin slowing?
sec07-card-r65.teaching_text: Touching the pedal early flashes red warning lamps well before hard deceleration starts.

sec07-card-r66.question_text: How many light brake-pedal taps does the handbook recommend before an unexpected slowdown?
sec07-card-r66.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps three or four times snaps daydreaming followers awake far faster than steady glow.

sec07-card-r67.question_text: When turning off a fast road that lacks a dedicated turn or exit lane, what must come first?
sec07-card-r67.teaching_text: Signaling and tapping brakes early warns highway followers you must scrub speed inside the main lane.

sec07-card-r68.question_text: Why must you warn early before parking or turning into a driveway just ahead of an intersection?
sec07-card-r68.teaching_text: Drivers behind assume you are rolling up to the green light, not braking mid-approach for a curb spot.

sec07-card-r69.question_text: Why is extra brake-light warning vital when slowing for a hazard or queue with a close follower?
