sec07-card-r69.teaching_text: Your own roofline blocks a tailgater's sightline to stalled traffic until you flash early brake warnings.

sec07-card-r70.question_text: How does Kansas classify holding a driver's license?
sec07-card-r70.teaching_text: Because driving is a state-granted privilege, unsafe or impaired choices can suspend it.

sec07-card-r71.question_text: In what personal condition must you always operate a motor vehicle?
sec07-card-r71.teaching_text: Alcohol, recreational substances, and drowsy medications all wreck reaction time and lane control.

sec07-card-r72.question_text: Who inside a moving vehicle should wear a seat belt?
sec07-card-r72.teaching_text: An unbuckled back-seat rider becomes a lethal projectile inside the cabin during a crash.

sec07-card-r73.question_text: Who shares financial responsibility for damages caused by a minor's driving?
sec07-card-r73.teaching_text: Co-signing a teen application ties family finances directly to every behind-the-wheel choice.

sec07-card-r74.question_text: What two responsibilities stay on a driver whenever leaving a vehicle parked?
sec07-card-r74.teaching_text: Parking clear of walkers and lanes while setting brakes prevents crashes after you walk away.

sec07-card-r75.question_text: What everyday habit solves awkward traffic moments that written statutes do not explicitly cover?
sec07-card-r75.teaching_text: Showing patient cooperation in crowded parking lots or narrow lanes resolves unwritten standoffs peacefully.

sec07-card-r76.question_text: Which three categories of limitations and conditions must you evaluate as driving risks?
sec07-card-r76.teaching_text: Ignoring tired eyes, worn tires, or freezing drizzle stacks all three risk sources together.

sec07-card-r77.question_text: How do built-in risk trade-offs differ between large vehicles and small vehicles?
sec07-card-r77.teaching_text: Big SUVs battle blind zones and top-heaviness, whereas compact cars vanish behind larger fenders.

sec07-card-r78.question_text: How do you manage spotted driving risks, and can road risk ever reach zero?
sec07-card-r78.teaching_text: Smart lane and speed choices slash crash odds dramatically, though traffic never becomes zero-risk.

sec07-card-r79.question_text: What three tactical gains come from timely speed or lane-position adjustments?
sec07-card-r79.teaching_text: Shifting early buys reaction seconds, steadies tire grip, and keeps hazards from hitting together.

sec07-card-r80.question_text: What builds faster, cleaner driving decisions over time?
sec07-card-r80.teaching_text: Logged miles across varied traffic turn deliberate beginner checks into automatic instincts.

sec07-card-r81.question_text: With what active habit must every good driving decision begin?
sec07-card-r81.teaching_text: You cannot react to what you never spotted, so active scanning anchors every choice.

sec07-card-r82.question_text: Once your scan spots other road users, what should you evaluate next?
sec07-card-r82.teaching_text: Judging whose path could intersect yours prioritizes real threats over harmless background cars.

sec07-card-r83.question_text: Which three response categories can execute your driving decision once chosen?
sec07-card-r83.teaching_text: Combining early braking, smooth lane placement, and clear signals turns good awareness into safety.

sec07-card-r84.question_text: What three-step mental loop should you practice continuously while driving?
sec07-card-r84.teaching_text: Spotting trouble early, picking the cleanest counter-move, and acting promptly prevents panic freezes.

sec07-card-r85.question_text: How can asking yourself silent what-if questions while cruising improve emergency readiness?
sec07-card-r85.teaching_text: Pre-planning an escape shoulder before a deer jumps out saves vital split seconds.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: Which three driver actions can avoid a crash, and what determines which one to use?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Fixating on the brake pedal alone wastes open escape lanes when steering or accelerating clears the threat faster.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: Where should you look to learn the specific anti-lock braking instructions for your vehicle?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Finding out how your braking hardware behaves during an emergency is too late once tires approach lockup.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: How should you use the brake pedal when making an emergency stop with anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Pumping an anti-lock pedal defeats the computer cycling that keeps tires rolling and steerable under heavy braking.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: What should you do if an anti-lock brake pedal pushes back or pulses under your foot?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Startled drivers often lift off when the pedal chatters, throwing away crucial stopping power right before impact.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: What happens if you slam the brake pedal too hard in a vehicle without anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Locked front tires slide straight ahead like sled runners regardless of how far you turn the steering wheel.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: How hard should you brake during a rapid stop in a vehicle that lacks anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Squeezing right up to the grip threshold delivers maximum stopping force while keeping all four tires rotating.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: How do you recover if non-ABS brakes lock up during an emergency stop?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Keeping your foot poised on the pedal lets tires spin back up immediately before reapplying controlled stopping force.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: How long should you continue easing and reapplying non-ABS brakes if lockup threatens again?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Slick patches vary down the lane, requiring repeated release-and-squeeze adjustments all the way to zero speed.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: Why can steering around a sudden hazard beat hitting the brakes in many emergencies?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: At highway speeds your car needs hundreds of feet to halt, yet shifting one lane width takes far less.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: How should you hold the wheel and prepare during an emergency steering move?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: One-handed swerves lose leverage when weight transfers violently and the car rebounds back into the lane.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: Where must you aim when steering to escape an imminent collision?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Dodging a stopped bumper by swerving blindly into oncoming traffic trades a fender crash for a head-on wreck.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: How does wearing a seat belt help you control the car during a sharp emergency swerve?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Hard lateral forces slide unbelted drivers across the seat, pulling hands and feet away from vital controls.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: How do you combine braking and steering during an emergency maneuver in an ABS-equipped car?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Anti-lock sensors prevent wheel lockup specifically so you can stomp the pedal and steer toward open space simultaneously.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: How should you manage the brakes while steering around a hazard without anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Slamming non-ABS brakes mid-swerve locks the front tires and plows you straight into the obstacle you tried dodging.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: When can pressing the accelerator help prevent a crash, and what comes right after?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: A quick burst forward can clear an intersection side-impact or incoming rear-ender when space ahead is wide open.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: Which surface conditions and driver inputs commonly cause tires to lose grip?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Combining wet, snowy, or icy asphalt with excess speed or sudden pedal stabs overwhelms tire tread friction.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: Where should your eyes lock immediately when your tires start losing traction?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: Drivers naturally steer toward whatever they stare at, so fixating on a tree guides your bumper straight there.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: What first pedal step helps you tell whether front or rear tires lost traction?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Lifting off both pedals unloads longitudinal tire stress and lets vehicle motion reveal which axle broke loose.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: Which tires have lost grip if turning the steering wheel fails to alter your straight-ahead path?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Plowing straight despite turned front wheels signals an understeer slide where front tread can no longer bite.

sec08-card-f20.question_text: What tire condition is happening when the vehicle swings sideways without extra steering input?
sec08-card-f20.teaching_text: Feeling the tail swing out unprompted warns of rear oversteer that spins the car if left uncorrected.

sec08-card-f21.question_text: How do you recover front-tire grip during a non-ABS skid?
sec08-card-f21.teaching_text: Backing off pedal pressure lets locked front wheels roll again so steering bite returns before gentle reapplication.

sec08-card-f22.question_text: What brake action does the Kansas handbook direct when front tires lose grip in an ABS vehicle?
sec08-card-f22.teaching_text: Full pedal pressure engages anti-lock modulation to shed speed rapidly and bring steering authority back.

sec08-card-f23.question_text: How should you steer and aim your eyes to recover when rear tires slide sideways?
sec08-card-f23.teaching_text: Pointing wheels down your target lane and countersteering smoothly catches whip-back swings as rear tires hook up.

sec08-card-f24.question_text: Why must you avoid glancing into the oncoming lane while recovering from a skid?
sec08-card-f24.teaching_text: Subconscious hand-eye tracking follows your gaze, pulling a recovering car straight into opposing head-on traffic.

sec08-card-f25.question_text: What should you keep doing with the wheel when traction-assistance tech activates during a rear skid?
sec08-card-f25.teaching_text: Stability computers read your steering-wheel angle to know which individual brakes to pulse for recovery.

sec08-card-f26.question_text: What single habit remains a primary defense against injury when a crash cannot be avoided?
sec08-card-f26.teaching_text: Properly buckled belts spread crash deceleration across strong bone structure and stop occupants hitting cabin glass.

sec08-card-f27.question_text: How should you position your body and feet right before your car is struck from behind?
sec08-card-f27.teaching_text: Pinning your head against the restraint limits whiplash while immediate braking stops you from ramming traffic ahead.

sec08-card-f28.question_text: How do lap-and-shoulder belts help in a side crash, and what should you prepare to do?
sec08-card-f28.teaching_text: Remaining anchored in the driver seat lets you steer or brake immediately to prevent a secondary wreck.

sec08-card-f29.question_text: Why do seat belts remain crucial right after an initial frontal impact?
sec08-card-f29.teaching_text: Airbags deflate fractions of a second after deploying, leaving seat belts as your sole restraint in multi-hit chain crashes.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: What routine habit lowers the chance of dangerous mechanical failures on the road?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Routine fluid, belt, and brake inspections catch worn parts in the driveway rather than at seventy miles per hour.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What is the first pedal action the Kansas handbook recommends if your brakes stop working?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Rapidly pumping a sunken hydraulic pedal can build enough residual line pressure to slow the car down.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: How should you apply the parking brake if pumping failed service brakes restores no stopping power?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Yanking the emergency brake full-on locks the rear axle immediately and spins the vehicle out of control.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: What must you stay ready to do if applying the parking brake during brake failure starts a rear skid?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Holding the release latch or button lets you drop cable tension the instant rear tires start sliding sideways.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: What must you do once off the road after losing your brakes completely?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Limping home with dead hydraulics turns the very next stoplight or downhill grade into an unstoppable wreck.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: What is a tire blowout, and how does a front-tire blowout pull the vehicle?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Sudden front drag yanks the steering wheel hard toward the shredded side unless both hands brace immediately.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: How does a rear-tire blowout typically feel from the driver's seat?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Recognizing tail vibration and tug early stops you from stomping the brake and triggering a violent spin.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: What is your immediate steering priority right after a blowout or sudden flat?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Keeping the chassis pointed straight stabilizes weight transfer while the damaged tire loses air.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: How should you shed speed right after a tire blows out?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Hard braking pitches heavy weight onto the shredded rim, tearing rubber loose and flipping or spinning the car.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: Where should you stop after a blowout, and what warning should you switch on?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Rolling slowly on a ruined rim to reach a safe turnout beats getting hit inside a live travel lane.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: What happens to your steering if the engine shuts off while your vehicle is moving?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Losing power-assist makes the wheel heavy, not locked, so muscling firmly still guides you off the road.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: Which gear and braking style should you use to pull off the road after an engine stalls at speed?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Neutral preserves rolling momentum toward the shoulder while one steady press saves remaining vacuum brake boost.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What steps follow once you pull off and stop for a stalled engine that refuses to restart?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Popping the hood and running four-way flashers signals distress clearly while keeping you out of traffic.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: What two mechanical problems can cause accelerator failure?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Knowing throttles can jam wide open prepares you to cut drive power immediately instead of kicking the floorboard.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: How do you safely bring the car off the road if the accelerator sticks down?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Dropping into neutral disconnects surging engine power from the wheels while keeping power steering and brakes alive.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: What must you do once safely stopped after an accelerator-failure incident?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: Shutting the ignition off only after parking preserves steering boost during your exit and prevents repeat runaway surges.

sec08-card-r17.question_text: Why must you resist yanking the wheel right back onto the road when tires drop off the pavement edge?
sec08-card-r17.teaching_text: Jerking back at highway speed catches the asphalt lip and slingshots the car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-r18.question_text: How should you manage pedals and steering immediately after dropping wheels off the pavement?
sec08-card-r18.teaching_text: Split traction between gravel and asphalt spins cars that stomp the brakes, so gentle straight slowing keeps stability.

sec08-card-r19.question_text: Down to what speed does the Kansas handbook recommend slowing before steering back onto pavement?
sec08-card-r19.teaching_text: Dropping to twenty-five miles per hour or below tames the tire hop over a sharp shoulder edge.

sec08-card-r20.question_text: How does straddling the dropped pavement edge help before turning back onto the road?
sec08-card-r20.teaching_text: Scrubbing the inner tire sidewall along a concrete lip resists small inputs until a sudden violent climb-over.

sec08-card-r21.question_text: How much wheel input guides a low-speed pavement return once traffic is clear in every direction?
sec08-card-r21.teaching_text: A crisp quarter-turn climbs the lip cleanly without flinging your nose across into opposing traffic.

sec08-card-r22.question_text: What is the safest move after a drop-off when traffic is heavy and a wide shoulder is available?
sec08-card-r22.teaching_text: Attempting a slow climb-back right beside packed highway traffic risks getting clipped mid-maneuver.

sec08-card-r23.question_text: What should you do if slope or obstacles make returning to the pavement impossible?
sec08-card-r23.teaching_text: Fighting deep mud or steep ditches damages steering parts and risks flipping back toward moving lanes.

sec08-card-r24.question_text: What roadside features can trip a sideways-sliding vehicle into a rollover?
sec08-card-r24.teaching_text: When sliding tires dig sideways into soft turf or strike a low curb, momentum flips the roof over.

sec08-card-r25.question_text: Which two driver inputs commonly trigger vehicle rollovers?
sec08-card-r25.teaching_text: Entering curves too fast or whipping the wheel violently shifts weight past what outside tires can support.

sec08-card-r26.question_text: How can a crash involving multiple vehicles trigger a rollover?
sec08-card-r26.teaching_text: A broadside T-bone impact shoves the chassis sideways fast enough to tip tall vehicles onto their roofs.

sec08-card-r27.question_text: Why are SUVs, vans, pickups, and small trucks more prone to rolling over than passenger sedans?
sec08-card-r27.teaching_text: Taller ride height places mass farther above the tires, multiplying outward lean during corners and swerves.

sec08-card-r28.question_text: How does adding passengers or heavy cargo affect a vehicle's rollover risk?
sec08-card-r28.teaching_text: Packing people and roof or bed gear raises total mass and top-heaviness during sudden lane changes.

sec08-card-r29.question_text: How do moderated speed and extra bad-weather caution lower rollover risk?
sec08-card-r29.teaching_text: Early reaction margin lets you steer smoothly instead of snapping the wheel at the last split second.

sec08-card-r30.question_text: What steering mistake must you avoid at high speed, on soft ground, or after dropping off pavement?
sec08-card-r30.teaching_text: Sharp wheel snaps on loose gravel or fast highways dig sideward rims in and launch rollovers.

sec08-card-r31.question_text: How do seat belts cut severe injury and death during a rollover crash?
sec08-card-r31.teaching_text: Unbelted riders thrown through side windows face crushing roof impacts far deadlier than staying belted inside.

sec08-card-r32.question_text: What two rollover hazards can rollover-sensing side airbags help reduce?
sec08-card-r32.teaching_text: Inflating side curtains cushion heads against shattered glass openings and block occupants from tumbling outside.

sec08-card-r33.question_text: What rule governs how fast you can safely drive at night?
sec08-card-r33.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight beam means obstacles appear closer than your total stopping distance can handle.

sec08-card-r34.question_text: How much extra following time does the Kansas handbook add at night and on unfamiliar night roads?
sec08-card-r34.teaching_text: Darkness hides unlit hazards ahead of the lead car, and unfamiliar curves demand an extra two-second buffer.

sec08-card-r35.question_text: Above what speed does the handbook warn driving is unsafe when weather cuts forward sight to one hundred feet?
sec08-card-r35.teaching_text: Even dry-road thirty-mile-per-hour stops take over one hundred twenty feet, so hundred-foot fog leaves zero margin.

sec08-card-r36.question_text: What should you do when severe weather drops visibility too low to keep driving safely?
sec08-card-r36.teaching_text: Creeping forward half-blind inside active travel lanes invites high-speed chain-reaction pileups from behind.

sec08-card-r37.question_text: Which lights should you run in fog, snow, or heavy rain—even during daylight—and what should you watch for?
sec08-card-r37.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding glare off water droplets, while gray unlit cars vanish into daytime mist.
sec08-card-r37.must_match_memory_hook: Low beams, fog lights, unlit cars

visual_sync.text_span: Low beams, fog lights, unlit cars

sec08-card-r38.question_text: Which three simple tools help cut blinding glare when driving toward a low sun?
sec08-card-r38.teaching_text: Dusty windshields scatter low-angle sunlight into an opaque sheet that hides brake lights and pedestrians.

sec08-card-r39.question_text: What visibility problem hits oncoming drivers when a low rising or setting sun sits directly behind your car?
sec08-card-r39.teaching_text: Staring straight into backlighting washes out your silhouette and turn-signal flashes for oncoming left-turners.

sec08-card-r40.question_text: How should you adjust near a hillcrest or curve that hides the roadway beyond?
sec08-card-r40.teaching_text: Assuming empty asphalt past a blind crest leaves nowhere to go if a tractor or stalled car sits there.

sec08-card-r41.question_text: Why and how much room should you leave when driving past a line of parked cars?
sec08-card-r41.teaching_text: Parked SUVs hide kids and swinging doors until the last instant, so widen your lateral buffer inside your lane.
sec08-card-r41.must_match_memory_hook: Max lane clearance for hidden walkers

visual_sync.text_span: Max lane clearance for hidden walkers

sec08-card-r42.question_text: How must your speed and lane position relate to visible stopping space around hills, curves, traffic, and weather?
sec08-card-r42.teaching_text: Driving faster than the clear pavement you can actually see gambles blindly that nothing sits beyond view.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: Which three habits help drivers share the road safely with everyone around them?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Scanning actively while treating walkers, riders, and trucks as partners prevents ego-driven lane conflicts.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: What legal status and rulebook apply as soon as someone steps out of a parked vehicle?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Crossing parking lanes carelessly right after locking your car ignores that pedestrian duties kick in immediately.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: Where should pedestrians walk when a sidewalk exists, and which side when none is available?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Walking along the left shoulder facing oncoming headlights lets you see and step away from drifting cars.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Which three visibility aids should pedestrians carry or wear when walking at night?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Dark hoodies blend into unlit asphalt until low-beam headlights are way too close to stop.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: What should a pedestrian verify before stepping out even when facing a green light or WALK display?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Distracted right-on-red turners and red-light runners blow past illuminated walk cues every day.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: How do crossing rules differ between starting on DON'T WALK versus seeing it start flashing mid-street?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Turning back halfway across leaves you stranded in traffic when cross-street green phases release.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: What should pedestrians establish with slowing or stopped drivers instead of assuming they will yield?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: A slowing driver looking left for a turn gap may accelerate straight into a walker on the right.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: What must you do if a pedestrian crosses outside a crosswalk unlawfully right ahead of you?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Someone jaywalking illegally never gives a driver legal permission to keep rolling toward a human impact.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: Which intersection crossings require yielding to pedestrians besides painted white crosswalks?
sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Wherever sidewalks meet an intersection street, legal crosswalk protections exist whether paint is present or not.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: How should you treat a marked midblock pedestrian crossing compared with an intersection corner?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Drivers cruising mid-street often overlook painted trail or campus crossings that carry full corner priority.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: What exact action is required when a crossing pedestrian uses a guide dog or white cane?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Inching or rolling near a blind pedestrian masks engine cues and threatens someone who cannot see your fender.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: Does getting a green traffic light cancel your duty to yield to pedestrians still crossing?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Slower seniors or parents with strollers caught mid-crossing when phases flip retain right of way to finish.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: What pedestrian check stays mandatory before turning left or making a U-turn, even on a green arrow?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Runners or distracted walkers sometimes step off against the hand right across your protected left-turn arc.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: From which side do pedestrians often surprise drivers turning right, especially on a red light?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: Staring left for oncoming car gaps blinds right-turning drivers to walkers stepping off the right-hand curb.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: What must you do before passing any vehicle stopped ahead, including on a multilane street?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: Whipping into the next lane past a polite stopped van strikes the hidden pedestrian crossing right in front.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: What check is essential before backing up, especially in busy spots like shopping centers?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Shoppers pushing carts weave constantly behind parked bumpers where rear pillars block quick mirror glances.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: What hazard should you expect and prepare for near schools, playgrounds, and residential blocks?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Small children stand shorter than SUV hoods and chase balls into the street without checking traffic.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: When does a reduced school-zone speed apply, and how must you respond to a school patrol?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: Ignoring active beacons, visible students, or a crossing guard flag brings heavy fines and endangers young walkers.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: What rights and duties apply to bicyclists riding on Kansas roadways?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Treating bicycles like toys that belong off asphalt ignores their legal standing as roadway vehicle operators.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: Why must drivers stay ready for sudden or unexpected movements from bicyclists?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Narrow bike profiles disappear beside A-pillars, and novice riders wobble around wind gusts or cracks.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: Which side of the road should cyclists normally ride on, and how do controls apply to them?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: Riding with right-hand traffic flow and honoring lights keeps closing speeds and corner priority predictable.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: How do bicyclists signal upcoming turns or lane changes to surrounding traffic?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: Knowing standard left, right, and stop arm extensions lets you read a cyclist's next move early.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: When is a bicyclist allowed to move out and occupy the entire travel lane?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Broken glass, potholes, or car doors along the gutter force riders center-lane to avoid crashing.

sec09-card-f24.question_text: For which two intersection movements may a bicyclist ride in the middle or left part of the roadway?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Positioning away from the right curb prevents cyclists going straight from getting hooked by right-turning cars.

sec09-card-f25.question_text: How many cyclists may legally ride side-by-side in a Kansas lane?
sec09-card-f25.teaching_text: Two-abreast riding is lawful in Kansas, even though narrow roads sometimes make single-file courteous.

sec09-card-f26.question_text: What clothing, visibility gear, and mechanical habit does the handbook recommend for cyclists?
sec09-card-f26.teaching_text: High-contrast jerseys and working brakes keep riders both visible to traffic and able to stop cleanly.

sec09-card-f27.question_text: Which bicycle lamp becomes mandatory at dusk, and what rear lamp is strongly recommended?
sec09-card-f27.teaching_text: Written exams separate what law mandates at dusk—a front headlight—from the strongly advised rear lamp.

sec09-card-f28.question_text: Who must yield where a designated bicycle path or bike lane crosses a roadway?
sec09-card-f28.teaching_text: Multi-use trails intersect streets briskly, requiring motorists to yield whenever riders cross the path.

sec09-card-f29.question_text: Outside of four narrow exceptions like driveways or emergencies, what three actions are banned in a bike lane?
sec09-card-f29.teaching_text: Blocking a painted bike lane forces vulnerable riders to swerve suddenly out into high-speed car traffic.

sec09-card-f30.question_text: How should you adjust speed and lateral spacing when approaching or passing a bicyclist?
sec09-card-f30.teaching_text: Close high-speed passes create wind blast that sucks lightweight bicycles sideways toward your tires.

sec09-card-f31.question_text: Why must you avoid overtaking a cyclist right before turning right at an intersection?
sec09-card-f31.teaching_text: Passing and immediately cutting right hooks the cyclist straight into your passenger fender.

sec09-card-f32.question_text: What mistake must you avoid immediately after pulling back in front of an overtaken cyclist?
sec09-card-f32.teaching_text: Narrow bicycle tires have far less braking patch than cars and will slam into your trunk.

sec09-card-f33.question_text: Why should you stay off the horn close to a bicyclist unless a crash threat demands it?
sec09-card-f33.teaching_text: A loud close blast jolts handlebars involuntarily and can pitch a rider straight into your lane.

sec09-card-f34.question_text: Which cyclists are especially likely to enter your path unexpectedly while you are turning?
sec09-card-f34.teaching_text: Young riders roll off driveway aprons and corner ramps fast without scanning behind for turning cars.

sec09-card-f35.question_text: What two aggressive turning errors around bicyclists must drivers never commit?
sec09-card-f35.teaching_text: Slicing sharply across a bike's line or squeezing a rider onto gravel shoulders causes instant wipeouts.

sec09-card-f36.question_text: Where on the roadway should drivers scan for bicycles even though riders belong with traffic flow?
sec09-card-f36.teaching_text: Inexperienced cyclists sometimes ride against traffic or roll off odd angles where textbook scans miss them.

sec09-card-f37.question_text: How do wet asphalt, sand, and loose gravel affect nearby bicyclists?
sec09-card-f37.teaching_text: Skinny two-wheel tires wash out effortlessly on grit or rain, demanding wider following and passing cushions.

sec09-card-f38.question_text: What clues reveal a cyclist's next move when rough pavement keeps both hands on the handlebars?
sec09-card-f38.teaching_text: Lifting one hand over potholes risks a crash, so a rider glancing back left usually plans a move.

sec09-card-f39.question_text: Where must you check before swinging open the door of a parked car?
sec09-card-f39.teaching_text: Opening a steel door across a bike lane gives an approaching rider zero time to brake or swerve.

sec09-card-f40.question_text: Which hand opens the driver's door in the handbook's Dutch Reach, and why does it work?
sec09-card-f40.teaching_text: Reaching across with your far hand naturally pivots your shoulders and eyes toward approaching cyclists.

sec09-card-f41.question_text: Where is checking for bicycles before backing up especially critical?
sec09-card-f41.teaching_text: Low neighborhood bikes and kid tricycles cruise driveways right below high SUV rear glass.

sec09-card-f42.question_text: What painted elements make up a sharrow, and what does it show?
sec09-card-f42.teaching_text: Twin chevrons over a bike stencil guide riders clear of parked car doors inside a shared lane.

sec09-card-f43.question_text: Where does a designated bike lane usually sit, and what stripe separates it?
sec09-card-f43.teaching_text: A solid white line carves out dedicated right-edge travel space that motor vehicles must respect.

sec09-card-f44.question_text: For which three reasons may a cyclist legally leave a marked bike lane?
sec09-card-f44.teaching_text: Expecting riders to stay trapped inside white paint ignores hazards, right-turn lanes, and left-turn setups.

sec09-card-f45.question_text: What kind of streets do signed bike routes or bikeways recommend for cyclists?
sec09-card-f45.teaching_text: Routing bicycles onto lower-volume residential corridors cuts high-speed arterial conflicts for both groups.

sec09-card-f46.question_text: How do traffic rights and duties of motorcycle, scooter, and moped riders compare with car drivers?
sec09-card-f46.teaching_text: Smaller engine size never shrinks a rider's right-of-way priority at intersections or lane merges.

sec09-card-f47.question_text: How much lane width may motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds use, and may two ride side-by-side?
sec09-card-f47.teaching_text: Riders need full lane width to dodge potholes and oil streaks, though two bikes may pair up.

sec09-card-f48.question_text: Are you allowed to squeeze past a motorcycle, scooter, or moped inside the same travel lane?
sec09-card-f48.teaching_text: Sharing a car's width with a bike steals the rider's swerve room and risks a lethal sideswipe.

sec09-card-f49.question_text: How must you check for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds before lane moves or at intersections?
sec09-card-f49.teaching_text: Narrow handlebars hide completely behind mirror housings unless you physically turn to check blind spots.

sec09-card-f50.question_text: Which four technical caps define a motorized bicycle or moped under the Kansas handbook?
sec09-card-f50.teaching_text: Exceeding three point five horsepower, one hundred thirty cubic centimeters, automatic shifting, or thirty speed reclassifies the machine.

sec09-card-f51.question_text: Why must you wait until a motorcycle, scooter, or moped actually starts turning rather than trusting its blinker?
sec09-card-f51.teaching_text: Pulling out in front of a bike with a forgotten blinker causes devastating T-bone rider impacts.

sec09-card-f52.question_text: What two signal quirks on small motorized vehicles require leaving extra maneuvering space?
sec09-card-f52.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling switches and older mopeds carry no blinkers at all, demanding extra cushion.

sec09-card-f53.question_text: Why is signaling early before merging or changing lanes critical around two-wheeled riders?
sec09-card-f53.teaching_text: Motorcyclists rely on early positioning to stay out of car blind spots before steel fenders move over.

sec09-card-f54.question_text: Which road-surface flaws force riders to adjust speed or lane position suddenly?
sec09-card-f54.teaching_text: Grooved bridge decks or loose pebbles that cars barely feel can dump a two-wheeler instantly.

sec09-card-f55.question_text: How many seconds of following distance should you leave behind a motorcycle, scooter, or moped?
sec09-card-f55.teaching_text: Light bikes stop briskly on dry asphalt and slide easily in rain, requiring three-plus seconds and more when wet.

sec09-card-f56.question_text: How should you manage headlights when approaching a motorcycle, scooter, or moped at night?
sec09-card-f56.teaching_text: Glare off a visor or tiny bike mirror blinds a balancing rider far worse than someone inside a car.

sec09-card-f57.question_text: What must you do with your speed and lane position while a motorcyclist overtakes you?
sec09-card-f57.teaching_text: Speeding up or drifting left traps an exposed rider inside oncoming traffic with zero sheet-metal protection.

sec09-card-f58.question_text: How does the typical travel speed of scooters and mopeds compare with full-size motorcycles?
sec09-card-f58.teaching_text: Closing gaps shrink unexpectedly fast when you mistake a thirty-mile-per-hour moped ahead for a highway motorcycle.

sec09-card-f59.question_text: What safety duty still binds emergency-vehicle operators even when responding with traffic-rule exemptions?
sec09-card-f59.teaching_text: Sirens grant signal exemptions, yet ambulance and patrol drivers must still watch cross traffic to prevent wrecks.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: How must you yield when an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens or flashing lights?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Stopping crooked or inside an intersection blocks wide fire trucks trying to swing around traffic.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: What check is required after one emergency vehicle passes before pulling back into traffic?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Police cruisers, fire engines, and ambulances often run in pairs, catching drivers who pull out blindly.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: How far away from an active emergency vehicle does the Kansas handbook require you to stay?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Drafting close behind an ambulance risks slamming into it when crews brake abruptly at the crash scene.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: How should you respond when an emergency rig enters or exits its station garage with lights flashing?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Backing ladder trucks need both directions halted completely until the entire rig clears the street.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: Whose traffic directions govern when you reach an active emergency scene?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Live hand signals from officers and responders override normal lights and paint around crash zones.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: Where should you position your car when pulled over for a police traffic stop?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Giving wide shoulder clearance protects both you and the approaching officer from passing highway mirrors.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: Which four cabin steps should you take right after stopping for a police officer?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Killing engine noise, muting phones, running hazards, and rolling glass down sets up calm communication.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: What extra lighting step should you take during a nighttime police stop?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Lighting the cabin removes dark shadows so the approaching officer sees everyone clearly right away.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: What should you and your passengers do with seat belts and demeanor during a traffic stop?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: Unbuckling early looks like preparing to exit or hide items and removes crash protection on shoulders.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: Where should your hands stay and how should you move during a police stop?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Keeping both hands visible on the rim reassures the officer that nobody is reaching under seats.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: How should you retrieve your license, registration, or insurance when an officer asks?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Telling the officer before reaching into a glovebox while keeping one hand on the wheel prevents misunderstandings.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: When should you exit your vehicle during a traffic stop, and how should you respond verbally?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Popping your door open uninvited steps into live roadside traffic and escalates officer safety tension.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: Why must a driver never attempt to flee from law enforcement?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Running from flashing patrol lights turns a routine traffic ticket into a life-threatening high-speed crash risk.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: How must you pass a stationary emergency, tow, or recovery rig with flashing lights on your side?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: Shifting one lane over—or slowing safely when boxed in—protects roadside crews working inches from traffic.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: In which four ways do large trucks and buses handle differently than passenger cars?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Massive weight and length create huge blind zones while demanding far more space to accelerate, stop, and turn.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: Where around a large truck or bus do No-Zone blind areas exist?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Drivers often remember side blind spots yet forget deep invisible pockets directly ahead of the hood and behind.

sec09-card-r17.question_text: Where does a large truck's right-side blind spot begin, and how far can it stretch?
sec09-card-r17.teaching_text: Cruising along a semi's right flank hides your entire car down the full trailer length.

sec09-card-r18.question_text: What does it mean when you cannot see a truck driver's face in the truck's side mirror?
sec09-card-r18.teaching_text: Optics work both ways, so missing the trucker's reflection proves your car is completely invisible to them.

sec09-card-r19.question_text: Why must you avoid lingering right beside a large truck or bus?
sec09-card-r19.teaching_text: If a tire blows or debris forces the semi sideways, sitting beside its wheels leaves zero escape.

sec09-card-r20.question_text: At least how many feet does a loaded truck at fifty-five miles per hour need to stop under ideal conditions?
sec09-card-r20.teaching_text: Cutting close ahead of a highway rig ignores that over a football field is needed for it to halt.

sec09-card-r21.question_text: When is it safe to pull back in front of a large truck you just passed, and how should you manage speed?
sec09-card-r21.teaching_text: Cutting back early forces eighty thousand pounds into your rear bumper if traffic slows unexpectedly.

sec09-card-r22.question_text: How far back can a large vehicle's rear blind spot reach, and what else does tailgating block?
sec09-card-r22.teaching_text: Riding behind trailer doors blinds both the trucker to you and you to brake lights up ahead.

sec09-card-r23.question_text: What two things should your following position behind a large vehicle give you?
sec09-card-r23.teaching_text: Dropping back into view of the rig's side mirrors ensures mutual awareness and space to brake.

sec09-card-r24.question_text: Why should you move out of the right lane near highway truck weigh stations when possible?
sec09-card-r24.teaching_text: Heavily loaded rigs pulling off scale ramps merge well below highway speed and need the right lane.

sec09-card-r25.question_text: What lane movement may a long truck or bus make right before turning right?
sec09-card-r25.teaching_text: Long trailer axles track inward across curbs unless the cab swings wide left to set up the corner.

sec09-card-r26.question_text: Why must you never squeeze between a right-turning truck or bus and the curb?
sec09-card-r26.teaching_text: Sneaking into that temporary right-hand gap puts your roof directly under off-tracking trailer wheels.

sec09-card-r27.question_text: How should you position your car when meeting a large truck head-on on a two-way road?
sec09-card-r27.teaching_text: Easing right inside your lane cushions against bow-wave wind buffeting and wide trailer mirrors.

sec09-card-r28.question_text: What should you do before turning left if you feel unsure how fast an oncoming truck or bus is moving?
sec09-card-r28.teaching_text: Large windshields look slower than they really move, and heavy rigs cannot scrub speed if you misjudge.

sec09-card-r29.question_text: Besides obeying intersection controls, what extra benefit comes from halting behind painted stop lines?
sec09-card-r29.teaching_text: Creeping past the white bar blocks intersecting tractor-trailers that need every foot of corner throat.

sec09-card-r30.question_text: Why must you never dart ahead of a truck to grab a turn, exit, or single-lane work zone?
sec09-card-r30.teaching_text: Stealing a semi's braking cushion right before a bottleneck leaves the rig zero feet to avoid crushing you.

sec09-card-r31.question_text: Who are downhill runaway ramps built for, and what parking rule applies there?
sec09-card-r31.teaching_text: Stopping for scenery inside a gravel arrestor bed puts your car squarely in the path of brake-failed semis.

sec09-card-r32.question_text: What two hazards should you anticipate whenever passing a stopped city transit bus?
sec09-card-r32.teaching_text: Riders hurry across ahead of the bus bumper just as the coach signals left to pull back out.

sec09-card-r33.question_text: Whom does a transit safety zone protect, and what driving or parking rule applies to it?
sec09-card-r33.teaching_text: Raised or painted rail-boarding islands shield waiting riders and are strictly off-limits to motor vehicles.

sec09-card-r34.question_text: What maximum speed applies when safely passing an active transit safety zone?
sec09-card-r34.teaching_text: Crawling past at ten miles per hour or slower lets you stop instantly if a commuter steps off.

sec09-card-r35.question_text: Where must you stop and how long must you wait when riders board or leave a trolley without a safety zone?
sec09-card-r35.teaching_text: Without a protected island, passengers step directly onto street asphalt and need traffic stopped behind the doors.

sec09-card-r36.question_text: Apart from one-way streets, blocked right space, or police orders, on which side is passing a trolley banned?
sec09-card-r36.teaching_text: Swinging left around streetcars puts you into oncoming tracks or traffic unless one of three narrow exceptions applies.

sec09-card-r37.question_text: What must you do before turning across the path of an approaching trolley or light-rail train?
sec09-card-r37.teaching_text: Steel wheels on steel rails cannot swerve and take far longer to halt than rubber-tired traffic.

sec09-card-r38.question_text: Why might a trolley or light-rail operator fail to spot a car edging toward the tracks early?
sec09-card-r38.teaching_text: Urban storefronts and street trees screen side streets until a car is already across the rails.

sec09-card-r39.question_text: What spacing rule applies when sharing a street lane behind a trolley or light-rail vehicle?
sec09-card-r39.teaching_text: Tailgating a tall streetcar blinds you to overhead signals and passenger stops directly ahead.

sec09-card-r40.question_text: What travel speed does a rear orange-and-red reflective triangle warn drivers to expect?
sec09-card-r40.teaching_text: Spotting the glowing orange triangle from afar warns you that highway closing speed is forty-plus miles per hour.

sec09-card-r41.question_text: How should you approach and overtake any slow-moving vehicle?
sec09-card-r41.teaching_text: Shedding speed early gives time to scan oncoming traffic and hidden field driveways before pulling out.

sec09-card-r42.question_text: Why might rural farm equipment extend across the centerline or take up more than one lane?
sec09-card-r42.teaching_text: Combines and planters span wider than rural asphalt lanes and cross between fields abruptly.

sec09-card-r43.question_text: Why can a tractor's initial move left fool a driver preparing to pass?
sec09-card-r43.teaching_text: Unlit farm rigs often swing left to clear a narrow gate right as an impatient passer pulls alongside.

sec09-card-r44.question_text: Below what speed do farm machines typically travel, and how should you pass them?
sec09-card-r44.teaching_text: Closing on a fifteen-mile-per-hour tractor from highway speed eats up gap distance in mere seconds.

sec09-card-r45.question_text: How do road rights and traffic duties apply to animal-drawn vehicles in Kansas?
sec09-card-r45.teaching_text: Horse-drawn buggies and wagons hold lawful roadway standing alongside motor traffic and follow traffic rules.

sec09-card-r46.question_text: How fast do animal-drawn vehicles normally move, and when might they go even slower?
sec09-card-r46.teaching_text: A buggy moving five to eight miles per hour looks practically parked when you top a sixty-mile-per-hour hill.

sec09-card-r47.question_text: Why must you use extra care when overtaking a heavily loaded animal-drawn wagon?
sec09-card-r47.teaching_text: Stacked hay or farm gear blinds the team driver to cars pulling out behind the wagon.

sec09-card-r48.question_text: Why must you never honk or rev your engine near animal-drawn traffic?
sec09-card-r48.teaching_text: Loud exhaust or horn blasts bolt a harnessed horse straight into oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-r49.question_text: What sudden turning move should you anticipate when trailing an animal-drawn vehicle on rural roads?
sec09-card-r49.teaching_text: Wagons turn left into unmarked farm lanes or driveways where impatient passers get broadsided.

sec09-card-r50.question_text: How and where should horseback riders travel along a roadway?
sec09-card-r50.teaching_text: Staying single-file on the right edge, shoulder, or path keeps horses predictable and clear of centerlines.

sec09-card-r51.question_text: How should you approach or pass someone riding or leading a horse?
sec09-card-r51.teaching_text: Giving generous room at calm speed without horn or exhaust noise keeps the animal settled.

sec09-card-r52.question_text: What should the operator of a slow vehicle do when trailing traffic backs up behind?
sec09-card-r52.teaching_text: Easing over where safe clears frustrating queues before impatient drivers gamble on blind hill passes.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: How should you handle your focus and speed on peaceful, low-traffic rural roads?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: Empty country lanes lull drivers into daydreaming right before a tractor, blind crest, or washboard corner appears.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: How do dirt and gravel roads compare with paved asphalt, and how must you adjust?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Rolling stones slide like marbles under braking tires, stretching your stopping distance well past dry pavement.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: What can potholes and rippled dirt or gravel surfaces do to your vehicle?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Bouncing tires skip off rippled ruts mid-turn, pulling your steering off line if speed stays high.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: Which three steps protect you when thick dust kicks up on a gravel road?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Dust plumes hide brake lights ahead and blind oncoming drivers unless low beams and extra cushion separate cars.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What roadside hazards and bridge preparations belong on narrow rural roads?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Missing shoulders and steep drop-off ditches leave zero room to squeeze past oncoming trucks on one-lane spans.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: How should you adjust for rural roads with sudden dips or tight bends?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: Deep roadway dips can hide an entire stalled car or slow farm wagon until you crest the lip.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: How do open metal bridge gratings affect grip, and what three actions should you take?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Steel grid decks cut tire friction and tug slightly at tread grooves, especially when morning dew wets the metal.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: What natural roadside growth can block your view of cross-traffic at country intersections?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: Towering summer cornfields and untrimmed hedgerows turn open country crossroads into completely blind four-way corners.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: What three steps must you take before topping a rural hillcrest or entering a blind curve?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Wide pickups or farm machinery often straddle unpainted country centerlines just over a blind rise.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: Why must you slow, look both ways, and be ready to stop at rural train crossings?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Many country rail crossings carry only a passive crossbuck sign, so silent assumptions without looking turn fatal.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: How should you approach an uncontrolled rural intersection that has no stop or yield signs?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Unmarked gravel crossroads invite two fast drivers to assume right-of-way at the exact same second.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: Why is driving after dark inherently tougher than driving in daylight?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Narrow beam cones leave roadside ditches, unlit signs, and distant curves cloaked in darkness until much closer.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: About how far ahead of an oncoming car does the Kansas handbook advise dimming high beams?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams a full city block early spares the oncoming driver's night vision from blinding glare.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: How should you respond if an approaching driver forgets to dim their high beams?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: One brief flick reminds them politely, and tracking the white right edge line keeps you inside your lane.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: Should you ever flip your own high beams back on to punish a driver blinding you?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Blinding the other driver creates two sightless cars hurtling straight toward each other at highway speed.

sec10-card-f16.question_text: In which traffic and weather conditions must you stick with low-beam headlights?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Low beams prevent mirror glare for drivers ahead and stop bright light from bouncing back off fog or snow.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: Why do high beams fail in foul weather, and what extra lights help if equipped?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: Moisture droplets scatter upward high beams into a whiteout wall, whereas low-mounted fog lamps cut underneath.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: Why must you avoid looking directly into oncoming headlights at night?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Bright oncoming bulbs bleach your retinas for critical seconds after the car passes, hiding dark hazards ahead.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: Where should your eyes search while driving down dark roads at night?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: Sweeping far ahead plus both shoulders spots unlit vehicles, walkers, and roadside deer before they enter your lane.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: Why must you leave sunglasses and tinted lenses off at night or on gloomy days?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Darkened lenses cut down the faint contrast your eyes desperately need to spot unlit pedestrians and curbs.

sec10-card-f21.question_text: Which water sources trigger road flooding, and how quickly can flash floods hit?
sec10-card-f21.teaching_text: Heavy downpours, snowmelt, or levee breaks can turn a dry low-water crossing into a raging torrent in minutes.

sec10-card-f22.question_text: What is the rule whenever water covers the roadway ahead of you?
sec10-card-f22.teaching_text: Moving floodwater floats passenger cars easily and stalls engines mid-channel where swift currents sweep vehicles away.

sec10-card-f23.question_text: Why must you refuse to cross a flooded road even when the water looks shallow?
sec10-card-f23.teaching_text: Murky sheet water conceals deep sinkholes and collapsed culverts where the asphalt underneath already washed away.

sec10-card-f24.question_text: What should you do if floodwaters block your path and no dry detour exists?
sec10-card-f24.teaching_text: Parking on elevated ground keeps you safe above rising surge waters until flood channels drain back down.

sec10-card-f25.question_text: What traffic changes occur inside work zones, and during which seasons do they appear?
sec10-card-f25.teaching_text: Emergency utility repairs and maintenance pop up year-round, not just during summer paving months.

sec10-card-f26.question_text: Which roadside objects, vehicles, and people warn of and channel a work zone?
sec10-card-f26.teaching_text: Spotting high-visibility vests and orange drums early lets you merge smoothly before temporary tapers pinch down.

sec10-card-f27.question_text: What three kinds of guidance do orange work-zone signs deliver?
sec10-card-f27.teaching_text: Orange diamond and rectangular boards tell you early which lane closes, what detour follows, and how slow to roll.

sec10-card-f28.question_text: Which speed limit governs a work zone when no reduced construction limit is posted?
sec10-card-f28.teaching_text: Lack of a temporary speed plaque never cancels the normal speed sign, though conditions may still demand slowing.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: Which four driving habits keep crews and traffic safe through an active work zone?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Sudden stops ripple fast through narrow barrel chutes, making flagger obedience and wider front buffers essential.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: Why must you read every sign carefully even through a familiar multi-month road project?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: Crews move concrete barriers and switch closed lanes overnight, catching autopilot commuters completely off guard.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: When does the handbook advise moving into the open through lane for an upcoming work zone?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Sliding over as soon as advance signs appear prevents bottlenecks and risky last-second dives at the barrels.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: Should you relax caution inside a nighttime work zone when no crew members are present?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Drop-offs, shifted lane lines, narrow concrete k-rails, and parked graders stay just as dangerous at midnight.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle relative to roadside workers or heavy machinery when possible?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Moving into an outer lane or easing away gives workers on foot crucial breathing room beside live traffic.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: Which roadwork jobs roll steadily down the highway, and how long must you obey their signs?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Passing one mower or paint truck does not mean the zone ended until you clear the official end-road-work sign.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: How should you plan your schedule or route around known highway construction?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Leaving early or picking a clean alternate route removes the temptation to tailgate or speed past crews.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: What two steering escapes must you never attempt just to miss an animal in your lane?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: Jerking left into oncoming cars or right into trees turns a survivable bumper strike into a fatal crash.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: Why are violent animal-dodging swerves dangerous, and what stays priority number one?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Rollovers and head-on collisions kill far more drivers than straight, controlled braking through an animal strike.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: At which daily hours and during which autumn months does Kansas urge heightened animal watch?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Breeding and hunting movement peaks from October through December right when dim twilight hides brown coats.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: What real-world pattern determines where highway crews place deer-crossing warning signs?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Those yellow diamonds are not random guesses; they flag corridors with documented histories of deer collisions.

sec10-card-r12.question_text: What telltale visual cue helps you spot animals near woods and creeks after dark?
sec10-card-r12.teaching_text: Headlight beams reflect off animal retinas along brushy ditches long before dark fur becomes visible.

sec10-card-r13.question_text: Why must you slow right down even if a deer stands calmly beside the shoulder?
sec10-card-r13.teaching_text: Startled deer pivot unpredictably back into traffic, and one crossing doe almost always trails two more behind.

sec10-card-r14.question_text: Which vehicle lights can alert drivers behind and oncoming that wildlife is on or beside the road?
sec10-card-r14.teaching_text: Blinking four-way flashers prompt fast traffic behind you to lift off the gas before they hit hidden deer.

sec10-card-r15.question_text: Which three steps help avoid an animal safely when you spot it with plenty of room ahead?
sec10-card-r15.teaching_text: Brake taps flash red warning lights to trailing drivers while horn blasts encourage the animal off the asphalt.

sec10-card-r16.question_text: When does the handbook allow hard braking for an animal, and what tire mistake must you avoid?
sec10-card-r16.teaching_text: With nobody close behind, firm controlled braking sheds impact energy fast so long as tires stay rolling straight.

sec10-card-r17.question_text: What is the rule when an animal jumps out so close that hitting it cannot be avoided?
sec10-card-r17.teaching_text: Staying planted inside your lane absorbs impact with front crumple steel instead of rolling into a ditch.

sec10-card-r18.question_text: Whom must you notify after colliding with a large animal like a deer or cow?
sec10-card-r18.teaching_text: Officers clear dangerous carcasses from dark lanes and file the official report needed for collision coverage.

sec10-card-r19.question_text: What should you do—and never do—if you strike a pet near houses?
sec10-card-r19.teaching_text: Letting nearby owners know helps an injured pet get care while staying outside protects your personal safety.

sec10-card-r20.question_text: Across which three everyday driving environments can pets dart onto the road?
sec10-card-r20.teaching_text: Unleashed dogs and farm cats roam country gravel and farmyards just as often as suburban cul-de-sacs.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: What core purpose does the Kansas driver knowledge exam serve?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: Sampling key handbook rules proves you know street laws before taking a real vehicle into live traffic.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: How many multiple-choice questions appear on the Kansas knowledge exam?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: With just twenty-five questions total, every single missed question costs four full percentage points.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: Which four handbook topic areas show up on the Kansas knowledge exam?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Skipping sign shapes or lane-line colors leaves easy points on the table alongside Kansas traffic rules.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: Does the Kansas knowledge exam enforce a countdown timer, and what does fifteen to twenty minutes mean?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: Knowing there is zero ticking clock lets you read every answer choice twice instead of rushing.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: What minimum percentage score is required to pass the Kansas knowledge test?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Eighty percent on twenty-five questions means answering at least twenty items right with five misses max.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: What testing stage opens up once you pass the written knowledge exam and meet age and permit rules?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Clearing the written hurdle qualifies you for behind-the-wheel testing once required holding rules are satisfied.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: Where can applicants aged seventeen or older go to complete the license skills test after passing knowledge?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Not every small renewal counter runs road exams, so pick a full-service Kansas office offering skills testing.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: How long must an applicant under seventeen hold an instruction permit on that license-test path?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Whichever milestone arrives first satisfies the holding period, giving younger teens structured practice across seasons.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: Which three hands-on parts make up the Kansas practical driving examination?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Showing up ready only to drive traffic catches applicants off guard during vehicle walkarounds and cone maneuvers.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: Which two core items must you bring along to take your Kansas driver's license test?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: Arriving without your current instruction permit or proof of Kansas address cancels your test appointment at check-in.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: What must a parent or guardian certify under age eighteen, and what extra step applies under seventeen?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: Every minor needs fifty logged practice hours signed, while sixteen-year-olds also need written parental license consent.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: What does the handbook advise doing before retaking a failed knowledge exam?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Guessing right back into another attempt wastes one of your limited tries before fixing weak chapters.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: How many knowledge-test tries are allowed, and what wait hits if you fail attempt number four?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Burning through four rushed tries locks you out for half a year from that fourth failed attempt.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: What does the pre-trip inspection portion of the exam ask you to prove?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Safe driving starts before turning the key by spotting bald tires, dead brake lights, or broken glass.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: How might an examiner ask you to perform the pre-trip inspection around the car?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Simply pointing silently is not enough; examiners listen for what defect you look for and why it matters.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: Which two messy mechanical actions are never required during the Kansas pre-trip test?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: You will never have to pop the hood or slide underneath on test day—external walkaround and cabin checks suffice.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: With whom should you rehearse vehicle inspections while learning safe versus unsafe signs?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: Rehearsing alongside an experienced supervisor helps you spot real wear bars, cracked lenses, and fluid leaks early.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: What should you look for while walking all the way around your parked car before getting in?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: A ten-second walkaround catches low obstacles, resting pets, or toddlers hidden completely below mirror height.
sec11-card-f18.must_match_memory_hook: Check body; clear kids, pets, debris

visual_sync.text_span: Check body; clear kids, pets, debris

sec11-card-f19.question_text: Which three under-car zones on the pavement should you scan for fresh puddles or drips?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Fresh spots beneath the engine bay, gearbox, or rear tank flag active oil, coolant, transmission, or fuel leaks.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: Why is spotting a fresh puddle underneath the car especially important for sealed systems?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Brake lines and sealed transmissions lack quick daily dipsticks, making ground drips your earliest failure warning.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: Which three aspects of every tire should you inspect before driving?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Soft air pressure, bald grooves, or bulged sidewalls can turn a routine highway merge into a blowout.

sec11-card-f22.question_text: Where do you find your car's recommended tire pressure, and what tool measures it accurately?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Eyeballing radial tires misses moderate underinflation, and sidewall numbers list max ceiling rather than vehicle target.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: What should you inspect on each tire's valve stem and cap?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Cracked rubber stems leak air steadily, while missing caps let grit jam the tiny valve core open.

sec11-card-f24.question_text: How often—and before what special occasion—does the handbook recommend inspecting tires closely?
sec11-card-f24.teaching_text: Tires lose small amounts of air naturally each month, and sustained highway trips punish neglected rubber.

sec11-card-f25.question_text: How do underinflated tires or shallow tread hurt wet-road handling and stopping?
sec11-card-f25.teaching_text: Sagging or bald tread traps water underneath instead of channeling it clear during braking and cornering.
sec11-card-f25.must_match_memory_hook: More hydroplaning, longer stops, less grip

visual_sync.text_span: More hydroplaning, longer stops, less grip

sec11-card-f26.question_text: Why does driving on an underinflated tire raise the danger of a sudden blowout?
sec11-card-f26.teaching_text: Low air lets sidewalls bend excessively every rotation, cooking internal cords until the tire bursts.

sec11-card-f27.question_text: What tire failures can overinflation, sidewall cuts, or impact bruises trigger?
sec11-card-f27.teaching_text: Pumping past spec balloons the center crown stiffly, straining belts and turning curb bruises into ruptures.

sec11-card-f28.question_text: What two checks apply to your headlights during a pre-trip walkaround?
sec11-card-f28.teaching_text: Verifying both low and high beams plus intact, uncracked lenses ensures moisture will not short bulbs out.

sec11-card-f29.question_text: What must you verify on your vehicle's taillights and brake lights?
sec11-card-f29.teaching_text: Cracked red lenses leak white glare or let rainwater corrode the bulbs that protect your rear bumper.

sec11-card-f30.question_text: What vital message do working brake lights send to drivers behind your car?
sec11-card-f30.teaching_text: Instant red brake glow gives trailing traffic crucial split seconds to lift off gas before gaps vanish.

sec11-card-f31.question_text: Why must you check both front and rear turn signals and their lenses?
sec11-card-f31.teaching_text: Both oncoming traffic and trailing cars rely on crisp flashing lenses to anticipate your turns and merges.

sec11-card-f32.question_text: How do you get an accurate engine-oil reading using the dipstick?
sec11-card-f32.teaching_text: Reading splashed oil on the first pull lies; wiping clean and seating all the way shows true crankcase supply.

sec11-card-f33.question_text: Where should you look to find the right oil-change schedule for your specific vehicle?
sec11-card-f33.teaching_text: Modern synthetic intervals vary widely by engine design, making your owner's guide the authoritative source.

sec11-card-f34.question_text: What mixture guide should you follow if coolant drops below the reservoir's minimum mark?
sec11-card-f34.teaching_text: Correct antifreeze-to-water balance prevents winter block freeze-ups and summer highway boilovers alike.

sec11-card-f35.question_text: Why must you never twist open a radiator cap while the engine is still hot?
sec11-card-f35.teaching_text: Pressurized boiling coolant erupts instantly once unsealed, causing severe steam burns unless the engine cools completely.

sec11-card-f36.question_text: Which four active safety items must work on any car brought for the Kansas driving test?
sec11-card-f36.teaching_text: Examiners turn away test vehicles right in the parking lot if blinkers, brake lamps, horn, or tires fail.

sec11-card-f37.question_text: What glass, visibility, and legal plate requirements apply to your road-test vehicle?
sec11-card-f37.teaching_text: Expired registration stickers or spiderwebbed windshields cancel your road exam before leaving the curb.

sec11-card-f38.question_text: What interior climate requirement must your road-test vehicle meet for the examiner and driver?
sec11-card-f38.teaching_text: Sweltering heat or freezing cabins impair driver focus and endanger examiners riding through back-to-back tests.

sec11-card-f39.question_text: What climate feature must work in your test vehicle when outdoor heat tops eighty-five degrees Fahrenheit?
sec11-card-f39.teaching_text: Kansas summer heat above eighty-five degrees makes working air conditioning mandatory to start your road exam.

sec11-card-f40.question_text: What two options satisfy the test-car rule when outdoor temperatures sit between seventy-five and eighty-five degrees?
sec11-card-f40.teaching_text: In that mild warm band, a working right-side window can substitute if cabin air conditioning is out.

sec11-card-f41.question_text: Below what outdoor Fahrenheit reading must your road-test vehicle have a working heater?
sec11-card-f41.teaching_text: Chilly weather below forty-five degrees requires cabin heat both for safe comfort and frost-free glass.

sec11-card-f42.question_text: What three things should you confirm about the driver's seat before starting?
sec11-card-f42.teaching_text: A loose seat track sliding backward under braking pulls your foot off the pedal at the worst moment.

sec11-card-f43.question_text: What damage check and body placement apply when inspecting safety belts?
sec11-card-f43.teaching_text: Frayed webbing snaps under crash loads, and low hip-plus-shoulder routing keeps belt force off soft organs.

sec11-card-f44.question_text: What condition and operation must your windshield and side windows show?
sec11-card-f44.teaching_text: Unobstructed glass preserves sightlines while working window regulators allow hand signals, tolls, and ventilation.

sec11-card-f45.question_text: What checks apply to vehicle doors and mirrors before pulling out?
sec11-card-f45.teaching_text: Secure door latches keep occupants inside during crashes while clean, tight mirrors eliminate blind surprises.
sec11-card-f45.must_match_memory_hook: Doors latch tight; mirrors clean, aimed

visual_sync.text_span: Doors latch tight; mirrors clean, aimed

sec11-card-f46.question_text: What physical and functional checks apply to your windshield wipers and washers?
sec11-card-f46.teaching_text: Torn rubber streaks blinding glare in rain, and dry washer nozzles fail when road mud splashes up.

sec11-card-f47.question_text: What climate controls must you explain during the check, and where do you confirm defroster air?
sec11-card-f47.teaching_text: Confirming airflow right at the base-of-windshield vent proves you can clear sudden fogged glass mid-drive.

sec11-card-f48.question_text: What must you verify about your steering-wheel horn during the equipment check?
sec11-card-f48.teaching_text: A dead horn leaves you voiceless if a distracted driver starts drifting straight into your lane.

sec11-card-f49.question_text: Which three dashboard indicator icons should light up when testing exterior bulbs?
sec11-card-f49.teaching_text: Matching cluster arrows and high-beam icons confirm cabin feedback works without stepping outside while driving.

sec11-card-f50.question_text: How can you check rear brake lights easily, and what if a fault stumps you?
sec11-card-f50.teaching_text: Having someone stand clear behind while you press the pedal spots burnt bulbs fast so a shop can fix faults.

sec11-card-f51.question_text: What must you confirm on the fuel gauge before starting your drive or exam?
sec11-card-f51.teaching_text: Stalling out of gas mid-highway or mid-exam turns an avoidable gauge glance into a roadside hazard.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: Where can the Kansas basic-control maneuvers take place during your exam?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: Depending on your testing station layout, maneuvers may use painted cones, real curbs, or a mix of both.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: How many basic-control exercises are tested, and from which maneuver list are they drawn?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Practicing only right-side parking leaves you rusty if the examiner calls two-point turns, three-point turns, or left parking.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: Where and with whom does the handbook recommend practicing basic-control maneuvers?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: Quiet empty lots with a licensed adult over twenty-one let you master pivot angles without pressuring live traffic.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: What happens before you begin each basic-control exercise with the examiner?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Clearing up any confusion about boundaries or finish spots before shifting gear prevents avoidable point deductions.

sec11-card-r05.question_text: What counts as a direction reversal during a basic-control drill, and what brief stop does not count?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: Stopping briefly to check mirrors or cones costs zero points so long as you keep rolling the same direction.
sec11-card-r05.must_match_memory_hook: Gear shift counts; brief stops free

visual_sync.text_span: Gear shift counts; brief stops free

sec11-card-r06.question_text: How is each extra direction reversal scored during a basic-control exercise?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Planning clean entry angles upfront spares you extra forward-and-back corrections that rack up error points.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: What counts as an encroachment on cones or boundary lines—and what single vehicle part is exempt?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Bumping a cone or tire-touching a painted line counts against you, though side-mirror overhang above a line does not.
sec11-card-r07.must_match_memory_hook: Touching lines or cones; mirrors exempt

visual_sync.text_span: Touching lines or cones; mirrors exempt

sec11-card-r08.question_text: How is each boundary encroachment scored during a basic-control maneuver?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Treating painted lines and cones like real parked fenders keeps your score clean and car undamaged.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: What turn-signal habits are scored during basic-control turns and backing—including steering resets?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Missing a blinker or forgetting to flick an auto-canceled lever back on mid-maneuver adds avoidable errors.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: What visual checks are scored before pulling into or out of a roadway during an exercise?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Relying only on mirrors without turning your head to clear both directions costs points every time.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: Where must you bring the car to rest at the end of a basic-control drill?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Stopping crooked or outside the examiner's target box tacks penalty points onto an otherwise smooth maneuver.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: How far into the side space must you pull during step one of a forward two-point turn?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Pulling nose-in until your entire rear bumper clears the road-edge cones gets the car completely off the street.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: Which way do you back out and finish after pulling forward into the two-point turn bay?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Backing smoothly toward the right lane aligns your nose to roll straight forward toward the starting zone.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: How do you set up and back into the side bay for a reverse two-point turn?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Pulling past the entrance first lets you pivot backward right until your front bumper clears the street cones.
sec11-card-r14.must_match_memory_hook: Pass bay; back right past cones

visual_sync.text_span: Pass bay; back right past cones

sec11-card-r15.question_text: How do you exit the side bay to complete the reverse two-point turn?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: Since you backed in first, exiting is a clean left forward turn with full windshield visibility of cross-traffic.
