sec11-card-r16.question_text: What two surfaces can host the three-point turn exercise, and what skill does it show?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Whether between curbs or painted lines, it proves you can reverse direction tightly inside a narrow two-lane road.

sec11-card-r17.question_text: Within how many inches of the right curb—and inside what limits—must right-side parallel parking finish?
sec11-card-r17.teaching_text: Parking past a foot sticks out into traffic, while crossing side or rear lines taps curb or bumper cones.

sec11-card-r18.question_text: What distance and boundary standards apply when testing left-side parallel parking?
sec11-card-r18.teaching_text: One-way downtown streets often park along the left curb, requiring the exact same twelve-inch precision.
sec11-card-r18.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve inches left curb; inside box

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve inches left curb; inside box

sec11-card-r19.question_text: How does the road test operate, and what two broad areas does the examiner grade?
sec11-card-r19.teaching_text: Following spoken directions calmly lets the examiner judge both specific turns and your overall traffic awareness.

sec11-card-r20.question_text: Where and with whom should beginners start on-road practice before tackling busy traffic?
sec11-card-r20.teaching_text: Mastering smooth stops and turns on calm neighborhood blocks builds muscle memory before multi-lane rush traffic.
sec11-card-r20.must_match_memory_hook: Quiet residential streets; adult over twenty-one

visual_sync.text_span: Quiet residential streets; adult over twenty-one

sec11-card-r21.question_text: Which four steps belong on your approach to a tested intersection turn?
sec11-card-r21.teaching_text: Checking mirrors first, signaling early, braking smoothly, and slotting into the proper turn lane keeps traffic predictable.

sec11-card-r22.question_text: Where must you stop before a turn when required, and how should your front wheels point?
sec11-card-r22.teaching_text: Pre-turning wheels left while waiting means a rear-end bump shoves your car head-on into oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-r23.question_text: What visual reference on the car ahead sets a proper road-test stopping gap in traffic?
sec11-card-r23.teaching_text: Stopping back where their rear tires meet asphalt leaves room to steer around if that vehicle stalls.

sec11-card-r24.question_text: Which four habits does the examiner watch while you actively steer through a turn?
sec11-card-r24.teaching_text: Palming the wheel one-handed or rushing past crosswalk pedestrians racks up deductions or instant failure.

sec11-card-r25.question_text: Which two lane-tracking errors must you avoid while rounding a corner?
sec11-card-r25.teaching_text: Cutting left corners crosses oncoming noses while tight right turns hop the rear tire onto sidewalks.
sec11-card-r25.must_match_memory_hook: Never swing wide or clip curbs

visual_sync.text_span: Never swing wide or clip curbs

sec11-card-r26.question_text: What must you check right after completing a turn—and before sliding into the right lane if needed?
sec11-card-r26.teaching_text: Finish inside your nearest legal turn lane first, then treat any move right as a separate full lane change.

sec11-card-r27.question_text: What three habits apply as you approach an intersection on the road test?
sec11-card-r27.teaching_text: Checking cross streets and mirrors while holding steady lane position spots red-light runners early.
sec11-card-r27.must_match_memory_hook: Scan all around, smooth brake, center

visual_sync.text_span: Scan all around, smooth brake, center

sec11-card-r28.question_text: Which three rules apply while driving straight across an intersection on your test?
sec11-card-r28.teaching_text: Swapping lanes mid-intersection surprises turning cross-traffic and counts directly against your road-test score.
sec11-card-r28.must_match_memory_hook: Ease speed, yield inside, hold lane

visual_sync.text_span: Ease speed, yield inside, hold lane

sec11-card-r29.question_text: What should you do right after clearing an intersection, including if you now need another lane?
sec11-card-r29.teaching_text: Re-establishing rear mirror awareness and accelerating smoothly sets up safe signal-mirror-shoulder lane shifts beyond the corner.

sec11-card-r30.question_text: What four fundamentals does the examiner grade across both urban streets and rural highways?
sec11-card-r30.teaching_text: Keeping flow pace without creeping past the posted sign shows mature speed control in every environment.
sec11-card-r30.must_match_memory_hook: Scans, space, lane center, legal pace

visual_sync.text_span: Scans, space, lane center, legal pace

sec11-card-r31.question_text: What complete sequence applies when the examiner asks you to change lanes left and later return right?
sec11-card-r31.teaching_text: Repeating the full mirror-glance-signal-cancel routine both ways proves blind-spot checks are automatic.

sec11-card-r32.question_text: Which checks, acceleration, and pavement-line rules govern an expressway test merge?
sec11-card-r32.teaching_text: Diving across solid white gore lines before broken dashes start draws immediate examiner deductions.
sec11-card-r32.must_match_memory_hook: Mirrors, glance, signal; respect solid lines

visual_sync.text_span: Mirrors, glance, signal; respect solid lines

sec11-card-r33.question_text: What should you do immediately after blending onto an expressway?
sec11-card-r33.teaching_text: Turning off an un-canceled merge signal and settling into highway cushion keeps fast traffic predictable.
sec11-card-r33.must_match_memory_hook: Cancel blinker; hold space, speed, scans

visual_sync.text_span: Cancel blinker; hold space, speed, scans

sec11-card-r34.question_text: Where and how must you slow down when taking an expressway exit on the test?
sec11-card-r34.teaching_text: Waiting until inside the deceleration lane to brake protects highway speed while honoring yellow ramp advisories.
sec11-card-r34.must_match_memory_hook: Signal, enter deceleration lane, obey ramp

visual_sync.text_span: Signal, enter deceleration lane, obey ramp

sec11-card-r35.question_text: What rules govern entering a limited-access highway regarding checks, stopping, and solid lines?
sec11-card-r35.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily on an acceleration lane or cutting solid lines creates severe high-speed merge conflicts.
sec11-card-r35.must_match_memory_hook: Check, signal, keep rolling; respect solids

visual_sync.text_span: Check, signal, keep rolling; respect solids

sec11-card-r36.question_text: Which four ongoing habits apply while cruising along a limited-access highway?
sec11-card-r36.teaching_text: High-speed multi-lane flow demands constant all-around scanning so fast mergers or sudden slowdowns never surprise you.
sec11-card-r36.must_match_memory_hook: Hold lane, speed, cushion; scan everywhere

visual_sync.text_span: Hold lane, speed, cushion; scan everywhere

sec11-card-r37.question_text: What complete five-part sequence applies when exiting a limited-access road cleanly?
sec11-card-r37.teaching_text: Finishing with a canceled blinker after obeying ramp speeds and cushions closes out highway scoring cleanly.
sec11-card-r37.must_match_memory_hook: Check-signal, slow in lane, obey, cancel

visual_sync.text_span: Check-signal, slow in lane, obey, cancel

sec11-card-r38.question_text: When should you slow for a curve on the road test, and what guides your speed?
sec11-card-r38.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and shedding speed before turning in keeps the car centered smoothly without mid-bend braking.
sec11-card-r38.must_match_memory_hook: Slow before entry; obey warning signs

visual_sync.text_span: Slow before entry; obey warning signs

sec11-card-r39.question_text: What observation question might the examiner ask you at any random moment along the test route?
sec11-card-r39.teaching_text: Actively reading every roadside sign instead of staring blankly at pavement makes this pop question effortless.

sec11-card-r40.question_text: How should you apply the brake pedal during normal stops on the road test?
sec11-card-r40.teaching_text: Late, jerky nose-dive stops signal poor forward scanning and startle trailing traffic.

sec11-card-r41.question_text: Where must both hands stay while driving on the test, and when may one leave briefly?
sec11-card-r41.teaching_text: Keeping both hands outside the wheel rim preserves instant steering leverage and avoids airbag wrist injuries.
sec11-card-r41.must_match_memory_hook: Both hands outside rim; return promptly

visual_sync.text_span: Both hands outside rim; return promptly

sec11-card-r43.question_text: Which two boundary and lane mistakes must you avoid throughout the road test?
sec11-card-r43.teaching_text: Clipping sidewalks endangers pedestrians, and swapping lanes inside intersections blindsides turning traffic.

sec11-card-r44.question_text: When must you check mirrors and traffic around intersections, turns, and lane moves?
sec11-card-r44.teaching_text: Continuous mirror sweeps plus direct shoulder checks before merges or lane shifts catch fast-changing traffic.

sec11-card-r45.question_text: What two timing habits make your turn-signal use clean on the road test?
sec11-card-r45.teaching_text: Late blinkers surprise traffic behind you, and un-canceled blinkers mislead cars waiting ahead.

sec11-card-r46.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop at a red light or stop sign?
sec11-card-r46.teaching_text: Rolling over the white bar or blocking the crosswalk forces pedestrians into live cross-traffic.

sec11-card-r47.question_text: What happens to your road test if you drive off without buckling your seat belt?
sec11-card-r47.teaching_text: Skipping your safety belt ends the exam automatically before you even reach the first corner.

sec11-card-r48.question_text: What road-test outcome follows failing to check your blind spots?
sec11-card-r48.teaching_text: Kansas treats missing shoulder checks as an automatic failure because mirrors alone hide adjacent cars.

sec11-card-r49.question_text: How do speeding, rolling a stop sign, or ignoring signals affect your road test?
sec11-card-r49.teaching_text: Even one mile over the limit or a California rolling stop ends a Kansas road test on the spot.

sec11-card-r50.question_text: What happens on the road test if you fail to yield to a pedestrian or another driver?
sec11-card-r50.teaching_text: Cutting off a walker in a crosswalk or cross-traffic with right-of-way is an immediate disqualifier.

sec11-card-r51.question_text: What test result follows any avoidable crash or physical contact with an object, car, or person?
sec11-card-r51.teaching_text: Even a low-speed bumper tap against a pole, parked fender, or cone barrier terminates the exam.

sec11-card-r52.question_text: What happens if an unsafe move forces another driver to brake hard or swerve around you?
sec11-card-r52.teaching_text: Even without metal touching, making cross-traffic slam brakes to save you from a crash fails the test.

sec11-card-r53.question_text: What test consequence comes from needlessly driving a tire up over a curb or sidewalk?
sec11-card-r53.teaching_text: Mounting a curb during a turn or parking move demonstrates loss of spatial control over pedestrian space.

sec11-card-r54.question_text: What happens to your score if the examiner has to grab the wheel or intervene physically?
sec11-card-r54.teaching_text: Whenever an examiner must step in to prevent danger, the applicant has lost safe independent control.

sec11-card-r55.question_text: How can basic-control exercises blend directly into the on-street road test?
sec11-card-r55.teaching_text: Examiners often call a curbside parallel park or turnaround right along a quiet street before continuing the route.

sec11-card-r56.question_text: What happens once you park back at the testing station at the end of your exam?
sec11-card-r56.teaching_text: Win or retake, listening closely to the examiner's coaching sharpens lifelong habits behind the wheel.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: What two questions should you ask yourself before grabbing the keys for a trip?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Skipping unnecessary solo drives or hopping on transit cuts crash exposure, fuel burn, and city congestion.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: How do carpools and public buses or trains affect your personal driving?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Sharing rides lowers mileage wear on your vehicle and keeps fewer solo bumpers competing for parking.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: What benefit comes from scheduling drives outside rush-hour gridlock?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: Stop-and-go congestion cooks brakes and transmissions while draining driver patience and alertness.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: How should you organize multiple errands instead of making separate back-and-forth drives?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Writing down items and chaining nearby stops into one warm-engine loop saves cold starts, gas, and time.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: What quick check prevents wasted trips before driving to pick up an order or item?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Confirming stock or readiness by phone spares you a pointless round trip in busy traffic.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: Which three everyday benefits come from cutting out unnecessary trips through planning?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Thoughtful trip batching keeps cash in your wallet, frees hours in your week, and thins street traffic.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: Which seven vehicle items should you inspect before heading out on a road trip?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: Catching a cracked belt, low coolant supply, or soft tire in your driveway beats breaking down miles away.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: What personal preparation is essential the night before starting a long drive?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Starting a highway trip already sleep-deprived guarantees highway hypnosis and dangerous microsleeps behind the wheel.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: How should you pick your departure window when your route passes through big cities?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Rolling past metro interchanges outside commuter rush hours keeps traffic flowing smoothly with fewer sudden lane jams.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: Which ramp numbers and scheduled stops belong in a solid road-trip plan?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: Knowing entrance and exit numbers plus meal, fuel, rest, and work-zone delays stops frantic last-second lane dives.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: What physical navigation backup does the handbook advise carrying in the cabin?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Dead phone batteries or rural dead zones never strand you when a marked paper map or written route sits handy.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: How many major-highway miles does the handbook budget per two hours, and where does pace drop?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: Realistic pacing around one hundred to one hundred ten miles every two hours prevents speeding to chase impossible schedules.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: What rest-break rhythm and meal time budget does the Kansas handbook recommend?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: Stretching ten to fifteen minutes every couple hours plus unhurried hour-long meals keeps reaction times crisp all day.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: How many hours behind the wheel should one solo driver treat as a full day's limit?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Pushing solo past eight hours erodes lane tracking and hazard perception almost like impaired driving.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: What daily total driving cap does the handbook recommend even when two or more drivers swap turns?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: Even passengers riding shotgun build road fatigue, so cap shared daily travel around ten to eleven hours.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: Past what nighttime hour does the handbook warn drowsy-driving danger spikes sharply?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: Your body's natural circadian clock pulls eyelids shut hard after eleven at night, especially on dark rural highways.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: What small backup item saves a road trip if your main keys vanish or get locked inside?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Keeping a spare key in your pocket or with a travel partner prevents a remote rest-stop lockout.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: Which four documents, funds, and guides belong with you on a road trip?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Having proof of insurance, emergency funds, your owner's guide, and local maps turns roadside hiccups into minor stops.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: When should you winterize your car and mount winter-ready tires?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: Waiting until the opening blizzard hits traps you on bald summer rubber with packed repair shops.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: Where must winter or all-season tires go on a front-wheel-drive car?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Grippy front tires paired with slick rear tires make the back end spin around wildly during winter braking.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: Between which exact calendar dates does Kansas permit studded snow tires?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: Metal studs chew up bare warm-season pavement, so Kansas restricts them strictly from November one through April one.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: What travel rule applies during an ice storm or snowstorm, especially under a weather advisory?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: Skipping nonessential trips keeps roads clear for plows and rescues you from freezing drifts.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: Which parts of the vehicle must you clear of snow and ice before rolling out?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Driving through a tiny scraped peephole blinds your side checks and hides dim snow-packed brake lights.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: What kind of windshield-washer fluid belongs in your reservoir for winter driving?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Plain water freezes solid inside lines or glazes across cold glass the instant salty truck spray hits.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: Why must you resist passing slower traffic in winter just because your car feels planted?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: All-wheel drive helps you accelerate, not stop quicker, and one hidden glaze patch spins fast passers instantly.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: Which three elevated road structures ice over first when sleet, freezing rain, or snow starts?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Frigid air circulates underneath elevated concrete spans, chilling them below freezing long before warm ground roadbeds.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: What winter hazard can still surprise you even after snowplows scrape the main lanes bare?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Windblown snowdrifts, shaded curves, and refreezing meltwater leave scattered black-ice traps across plowed highways.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: What ongoing habit keeps your vehicle's emergency survival kit ready when trouble hits?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: An empty flashlight or half-eaten snack stash fails during a blizzard if you forget to replace used items.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: Which tire, digging, recovery, and traction hardware belongs in a winter trunk kit?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: A solid spare, shovel, jumper cables, chains, grit, and basic tools get you unstuck or jumped without waiting hours.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: Which lighting, warning, navigation, and medical items belong in your emergency kit?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: Signaling gear, spare batteries, navigation aids, and bandages help rescue crews spot your vehicle and treat minor injuries.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: Which glass-clearing, fire-starting, and cold-weather items complete a winter kit?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Blankets, warm layers, waterproof matches, and a snow brush keep cabin glass clear and body heat safe.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: Which hydration and nonperishable snack foods does the handbook suggest packing?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: Unsalted nuts, dried fruit, and hard candy fuel shivering bodies without triggering heavy salt thirst.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: When is the only time you should ever leave a stranded car during freezing weather?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Blowing snow erases landmarks in yards, whereas rescuers spot a stranded car far easier than a lost walker.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: What immediate mindset and lighting step apply if a winter storm strands your car?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Panic burns energy and invites bad decisions, while four-way flashers keep plows and troopers from hitting you.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: How should you place road flares and bright cloth so rescue crews spot your stranded car?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Setting flares safely fore and aft plus tying bright cloth on the driver door or mirror flags passing plows.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: Why must you dig snow and mud clear of your tailpipe before running the engine while stranded?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: A snow-plugged tailpipe forces odorless exhaust backward into the cabin, causing silent unconsciousness and death.

sec12-card-r19.question_text: How long per hour and with what two safety checks should you run the heater while stranded?
sec12-card-r19.teaching_text: Running ten minutes each hour stretches fuel all night while a clear pipe and cracked window vent fumes.
sec12-card-r19.must_match_memory_hook: Ten minutes hourly; clear pipe, vent

visual_sync.text_span: Ten minutes hourly; clear pipe, vent

sec12-card-r20.question_text: Why must at least one window stay cracked open while idling stranded even in bitter subzero cold?
sec12-card-r20.teaching_text: Sealed cabins can trap invisible carbon monoxide seeping up from beneath an idling vehicle.

sec12-card-r21.question_text: What sleep rule applies when multiple people wait inside a winter-stranded vehicle?
sec12-card-r21.teaching_text: An awake lookout spots passing rescue lights, checks the tailpipe for drifting snow, and watches for drowsiness.

sec12-card-r22.question_text: Which fabrics and gear help prevent frostbite and hypothermia inside a stranded car?
sec12-card-r22.teaching_text: Wool traps body heat even when damp, keeping core temperatures safe during long waits between ten-minute heater runs.

sec12-card-r23.question_text: How often should you inspect tires when driving through extreme summer heat?
sec12-card-r23.teaching_text: Scorching asphalt bakes sidewalls relentlessly, so regular rest-stop checks catch blisters or soft tires before blowouts.

sec12-card-r24.question_text: Why must you never let air out of a hot tire whose pressure rose during highway driving?
sec12-card-r24.teaching_text: Air naturally expands when warm; bleeding it hot leaves the tire dangerously underinflated once it cools down.

sec12-card-r25.question_text: What two engine-oil habits help protect your motor in extreme heat?
sec12-card-r25.teaching_text: Clean oil carries away internal engine friction heat, and watching an oil-temperature gauge spots trouble early.

sec12-card-r26.question_text: What coolant routine applies before and during hot-weather highway trips?
sec12-card-r26.teaching_text: Verifying full reservoir coolant before leaving and scanning the dash temperature needle catches overheating fast.

sec12-card-r27.question_text: What must you do immediately if the coolant gauge climbs past its safe limit?
sec12-card-r27.teaching_text: Pushing an overheating engine just a few extra miles warps cylinder heads or sparks an under-hood fire.

sec12-card-r28.question_text: What pavement surface hazard develops when scorching summer sun bakes blacktop?
sec12-card-r28.teaching_text: Softened asphalt tar bleeds upward into shiny patches that reduce tire grip much like wet grease.

sec12-card-r29.question_text: How does highway speed affect heat buildup in tires and engines on blistering days?
sec12-card-r29.teaching_text: High speed flexes hot tire sidewalls faster and works cooling systems harder, so backing off prevents failures.

sec12-card-r30.question_text: Why must you never park and hide beneath a highway bridge or overpass during a tornado?
sec12-card-r30.teaching_text: Wind speeds accelerate violently through narrow bridge underpasses, blasting sheltered people with lethal flying debris.

sec12-card-r31.question_text: What structure does the Kansas handbook name as the safest shelter during a severe thunderstorm?
sec12-card-r31.teaching_text: Grounded copper pipes and structural wiring channel lightning safely into the earth around indoor occupants.

sec12-card-r32.question_text: Which four cabin steps protect you inside a hard-top car during heavy lightning?
sec12-card-r32.teaching_text: An enclosed steel roof routes strikes outside, provided you keep hands off metal trim and antenna-linked radios.
